statements.english: Two days later, Louis Blériot arrived near Calais with a plane called Number 11.

statements.chinese: 布莱里奥自1905年以来一直在制造飞机，这是他的最新型号。
statements.english: Blériot had been making planes since 1905, and this was his latest model.

statements.chinese: 一周前，他完成了一次成功的陆上飞行，飞行距离达26英里。
statements.english: A week before, he had completed a successful overland flight, during which he covered 26 miles.

statements.chinese: 然而，莱瑟姆并没有轻易放弃。
statements.english: Latham, however, did not give up easily.

statements.chinese: 他也于同日驾驶一架新的“安托瓦内特号”抵达加来附近。
statements.english: He too arrived near Calais on the same day with a new Antoinette.

statements.chinese: 看起来这将是一场激动人心的跨海峡竞赛。
statements.english: It looked as if there would be an exciting race across the Channel.

statements.chinese: 两架飞机都将在7月25日起飞。
statements.english: Both planes were going to take off on July the 25th.

statements.chinese: 但莱瑟姆未能足够早地起床。
statements.english: But Latham failed to get up early enough.

statements.chinese: 凌晨4点15分进行了一次短暂的试飞后，布莱里奥在半小时后出发了。
statements.english: After making a short test flight at 4:15 a.m., Blériot set off half an hour later.

statements.chinese: 他伟大的飞行持续了37分钟。
statements.english: His great flight lasted 37 minutes.

statements.chinese: 当他降落在多佛附近时，第一个迎接他的是一位当地警察。
statements.english: When he landed near Dover, the first person to greet him was a local policeman.

statements.chinese: 一周后，莱瑟姆又进行了一次尝试，到达了离多佛半英里以内的地方。
statements.english: Latham made another attempt a week later and got within half a mile of Dover.

statements.chinese: 但他又一次不幸。
statements.english: But he was unlucky again.

statements.chinese: 他的发动机失灵了，他第二次降落在海上。
statements.english: His engine failed and he landed on the sea for the second time.

courses.title: Lesson 21: Daniel Mendoza
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 24 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 门多萨在成为全英冠军之前，有过多少次失败的尝试？
statements.english: How many unsuccessful attempts did Mendoza make before becoming Champion of all England?

statements.chinese: 两百年前，拳击比赛在英格兰非常盛行。
statements.english: Boxing matches were very popular in England two hundred years ago.

statements.chinese: 在那些日子里，拳击手们赤手空拳地搏斗以争夺奖金。
statements.english: In those days, boxers fought with bare fists for prize money.

statements.chinese: 正因为如此，他们被称为“职业拳击手”。
statements.english: Because of this, they were known as 'prizefighters'.
However, boxing was very crude, for there were no rules and a prizefighter could be seriously injured or even killed during a match.
statements.chinese: 然而，拳击是非常原始的，因为当时没有规则，职业拳击手在比赛中可能会受重伤，甚至死亡。
拳击史上最引人注目的人物之一是丹尼尔·门多萨，他出生于1764年。
statements.english: One of the most colourful figures in boxing history was Daniel Mendoza, who was born in 1764.

statements.chinese: 直到1860年，昆斯伯里侯爵制定了第一套规则后，才引入了手套的使用。
statements.english: The use of gloves was not introduced until 1860, when the Marquis of Queensberry drew up the first set of rules.
Though he was technically a prizefighter, Mendoza did much to change crude prizefighting into a sport, for he brought science to the game.
statements.chinese: 尽管从技术上讲他是一名职业拳击手，但门多萨为将原始的职业拳击比赛转变为一项运动做了很多工作，因为他将科学带入了这项运动。
在他那个时代，门多萨享有巨大的声望。
statements.english: In his day, Mendoza enjoyed tremendous popularity.

statements.chinese: 他深受富人和穷人的喜爱。
statements.english: He was adored by rich and poor alike.

statements.chinese: 门多萨在14岁时参加一场拳击比赛后迅速成名。
statements.english: Mendoza rose to fame swiftly after a boxing match when he was only fourteen years old.

statements.chinese: 这引起了理查德·汉弗莱斯的注意，他当时是英格兰最杰出的拳击手。
statements.english: This attracted the attention of Richard Humphries who was then the most eminent boxer in England.

statements.chinese: 他主动提出训练门多萨，而他的年轻学生也学得很快。
statements.english: He offered to train Mendoza and his young pupil was quick to learn.

statements.chinese: 事实上，门多萨很快就变得非常成功，以至于汉弗莱斯转而反对他。
statements.english: In fact, Mendoza soon became so successful that Humphries turned against him.

statements.chinese: 两人激烈争吵，很明显，争论只能通过一场战斗来解决。
statements.english: The two men quarrelled bitterly and it was clear that the argument could only be settled by a fight.

statements.chinese: 在斯蒂尔顿举行了一场比赛，两人激战了一个小时。
statements.english: A match was held at Stilton, where both men fought for an hour.

statements.chinese: 公众在门多萨身上下了大笔赌注，但他被击败了。
statements.english: The public bet a great deal of money on Mendoza, but he was defeated.

statements.chinese: 门多萨后来又在拳击台上与汉弗莱斯相遇，但他第二次输了。
statements.english: Mendoza met Humphries in the ring on a later occasion and he lost for a second time.

statements.chinese: 直到1790年的第三场比赛，他才最终击败汉弗莱斯，成为英格兰冠军。
statements.english: It was not until his third match in 1790 that he finally beat Humphries and became Champion of England.

statements.chinese: 同时，他创办了一所非常成功的拳击学院，甚至拜伦勋爵也成了他的学生之一。
statements.english: Meanwhile, he founded a highly successful Academy and even Lord Byron became one of his pupils.

statements.chinese: 他赚取了巨额财富，单次出场费高达100英镑。
statements.english: He earned enormous sums of money and was paid as much as ￡100 for a single appearance.

statements.chinese: 尽管如此，他非常奢侈，总是负债累累。
statements.english: Despite this, he was so extravagant that he was always in debt.

statements.chinese: 在他被一位名叫“绅士”杰克逊的拳击手击败后，他很快就被遗忘了。
statements.english: After he was defeated by a boxer called Gentleman Jackson, he was quickly forgotten.

statements.chinese: 他因未能偿还债务而被送进监狱，并于1836年贫困潦倒地去世。
statements.english: He was sent to prison for failing to pay his debts and died in poverty in 1836.

courses.title: Lesson 22: By Heart
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 22 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 有些戏剧非常成功，可以连续上演多年。
statements.english: Some plays are so successful that they run for years on end.
In many ways, this is unfortunate for the poor actors, who are required to go on repeating the same lines night after night.
statements.chinese: 在许多方面，这对可怜的演员来说是不幸的，因为他们被要求夜复一夜地重复同样的台词。

statements.english: One would expect them to know their parts by heart and never have cause to falter.
statements.chinese: 人们会期望他们熟记自己的台词，永远不会出错。
然而，事实并非总是如此。
statements.english: Yet this is not always the case.
A famous actor in a highly successful play was once cast in the role of an aristocrat, who had been imprisoned in the Bastille for 20 years.
statements.chinese: 一位在一部非常成功的戏剧中出演的著名演员，曾被选去扮演一位贵族，他已被关在巴士底狱20年。

statements.english: In the last act, a jailer would always come onto the stage with a letter, which he would hand to the prisoner.
statements.chinese: 在最后一幕，一名狱卒总是会带着一封信上台，把信交给囚犯。

statements.english: Even though the noble was expected to read the letter at each performance, he always insisted that it should be written out in full.
statements.chinese: 尽管这位贵族被要求在每次演出时阅读这封信，他总是坚持信件应该完整地写出来。

statements.english: One night, the jailer decided to play a joke on his colleague to find out if, after so many performances, he had managed to learn the contents of the letter by heart.
statements.chinese: 一天晚上，狱卒决定和他的同事开个玩笑，想知道在这么多次演出之后，他是否已经熟记了信的内容。

statements.english: The curtain went up on the final act of the play and revealed the aristocrat sitting alone behind bars in his dark cell.
statements.chinese: 戏剧的最后一幕拉开帷幕，揭示了贵族独自一人坐在他阴暗牢房的铁窗后。
就在那时，狱卒出现了，手中拿着那封珍贵的信。
statements.english: Just then, the jailer appeared with the precious letter in his hands.

statements.chinese: 他走进牢房，将信递给贵族。
statements.english: He entered the cell and presented the letter to the aristocrat.

statements.chinese: 但他给的副本并没有像往常一样完整写出。
statements.english: But the copy he gave him had not been written out in full as usual.

statements.chinese: 那只是一张白纸。
statements.english: It was simply a blank sheet of paper.
The jailer looked on eagerly, anxious to see if his fellow actor had at last learned his lines.
statements.chinese: 狱卒焦急地看着，渴望知道他的同行演员是否终于记住了台词。
贵族盯着那张白纸看了几秒钟。
statements.english: The noble stared at the blank sheet of paper for a few seconds.

statements.chinese: 然后，他眯起眼睛说：“光线太暗了。
statements.english: Then, squinting his eyes, he said, "The light is dim.

statements.chinese: 替我读一下这封信。”
statements.english: Read the letter to me."

statements.chinese: 他立刻把那张纸递给了狱卒。
statements.english: And he promptly handed the sheet of paper to the jailer.
Finding that he could not remember a word of the letter either, the jailer replied, "The light is indeed dim, sir.
statements.chinese: 狱卒发现自己也记不住信中的一个字，便答道：“光线确实很暗，大人。
我得去拿我的眼镜。”
statements.english: I must get my glasses."

statements.chinese: 说完，他匆匆离开了舞台。
statements.english: With this, he hurried off the stage.
Much to the aristocrat's amusement, the jailer returned a few moments later with a pair of glasses and the usual copy of the letter, which he proceeded to read to the prisoner.
statements.chinese: 令贵族大为 amused 的是，狱卒片刻之后带着一副眼镜回来了，还有那封信的通常版本，他开始向囚犯朗读。

courses.title: Lesson 23: One Man's Meat is Another Man's Poison
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 22 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 当人们试图决定什么可以吃，什么不可以吃的时候，他们会变得相当不合逻辑。
statements.english: People become quite illogical when they try to decide what can be eaten and what cannot be eaten.

statements.chinese: 举个例子，如果你住在地中海地区，你会认为章鱼是一种美味佳肴。
statements.english: If you lived in the Mediterranean, for instance, you would consider octopus a great delicacy.

statements.chinese: 你就不会明白为什么有些人觉得它很恶心。
statements.english: You would not be able to understand why some people find it repulsive.

statements.chinese: 另一方面，一想到用动物脂肪炸土豆，你就会反胃。
statements.english: On the other hand, your stomach would turn at the idea of frying potatoes in animal fat.

statements.chinese: 这在许多北方国家是普遍接受的做法。
statements.english: A normally accepted practice in many northern countries.

statements.chinese: 可悲的事实是，我们大多数人从小就习惯吃某些食物，并且一生都坚持不改。
statements.english: The sad truth is that most of us have been brought up to eat certain foods and we stick to them all our lives.

statements.chinese: 没有哪种生物比普通的蜗牛得到过更多的赞扬和辱骂。
statements.english: No creature has received more praise and abuse than the common garden snail.

statements.chinese: 用酒烹制的蜗牛在世界各地都是一种高级奢侈品。
statements.english: Cooked in wine, snails are a great luxury in various parts of the world.

statements.chinese: 有无数人，从小就学会了将蜗牛与食物联系起来。
statements.english: There are countless people who ever since their early years, have learnt to associate snails with food.

statements.chinese: 我的朋友罗伯特住在一个鄙视蜗牛的国家。
statements.english: My friend Robert lives in a country where snails are despised.

statements.chinese: 由于他的公寓在一个大城镇里，他没有自己的花园。
statements.english: As his flat is in a large town, he has no garden of his own.

statements.chinese: 多年来，他一直让我从我的花园里收集蜗牛，然后带给他。
statements.english: For years, he has been asking me to collect snails from my garden and take them to him.
The idea never appealed to me very much, but one day after a heavy shower, I happened to be walking in my garden when I noticed a huge number of snails taking a stroll on some of my prized plants.
statements.chinese: 这个想法我一直不太喜欢，但有一天，在一场大雨之后，我碰巧在花园里散步，看到大量的蜗牛在我珍贵的植物上爬行。
我一时冲动，收集了几十只蜗牛，把它们放进一个纸袋里，然后带给了罗伯特。
statements.english: Acting on a sudden impulse, I collected several dozen, put them in a paper bag and took them to Robert.

statements.chinese: 罗伯特见到我很高兴，对我的小礼物也同样满意。
statements.english: Robert was delighted to see me and equally pleased with my little gift.

statements.chinese: 我把袋子留在门厅里，罗伯特和我走进客厅，我们聊了几个小时。
statements.english: I left the bag in the hall and Robert and I went into the living room where we talked for a couple of hours.

statements.chinese: 我把蜗牛的事忘得一干二净，这时罗伯特突然说我必须留下来吃晚饭。
statements.english: I had forgotten all about the snails when Robert suddenly said that I must stay to dinner.

statements.chinese: 当然，蜗牛会是主菜。
statements.english: Snails would of course be the main dish.

statements.chinese: 我不喜欢这个主意，我只好不情愿地跟着罗伯特走出了房间。
statements.english: I did not fancy the idea and I reluctantly followed Robert out of the room.

statements.chinese: 令我沮丧的是，我们看到到处都是蜗牛。
statements.english: To my dismay, we saw that there were snails everywhere.

statements.chinese: 它们从纸袋里跑了出来，完全占领了门厅。
statements.english: They had escaped from the paper bag and taken complete possession of the hall.

statements.chinese: 从那以后，我再也无法正眼看蜗牛了。
statements.english: I have never been able to look at a snail since then.

courses.title: Lesson 24: A Skeleton in the Cupboard
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 24 条逐句练习

statements.english: We often read in novels how a seemingly respectable person or family has some terrible secret which has been concealed from strangers for years.
statements.chinese: 我们经常在小说中读到，一个看似体面的人或家庭都有一些可怕的秘密，多年来一直对陌生人隐瞒。
英语中有一个生动的说法来描述这种情况。
statements.english: The English language possesses a vivid saying to describe this sort of situation.

statements.chinese: 这个可怕的秘密被称为“橱柜里的骷髅”。
statements.english: The terrible secret is called a skeleton in the cupboard.
At some dramatic moment in the story, the terrible secret becomes known and a reputation is ruined.
statements.chinese: 在故事的某个戏剧性时刻，这个可怕的秘密被公之于众，名誉扫地。

statements.english: The reader's hair stands on end when he reads in the final pages of the novel that the heroine, a dear old lady, who had always been so kind to everybody, had in her youth poisoned every one of her five husbands.
statements.chinese: 当读者在小说的最后一页读到女主人公——一位亲爱的老太太——总是对每个人都那么好，在她年轻时毒死了她的五个丈夫时，会感到毛骨悚然。
这种事情发生在小说里是完全可以接受的。
statements.english: It is all very well for such things to occur in fiction.
To varying degrees, we all have secrets which we do not want even our closest friends to learn.
statements.chinese: 在不同程度上，我们都有秘密，甚至不想让最亲密的朋友知道。
但我们中很少有人有“橱柜里的骷髅”。
statements.english: But few of us have skeletons in the cupboard.
The only person I know who has a skeleton in the cupboard is George Carlton, and he is very proud of the fact.
statements.chinese: 我认识的唯一一个有“橱柜里的骷髅”的人是乔治·卡尔顿，他对此感到非常自豪。
乔治年轻时学过医。
statements.english: George studied medicine in his youth.
Instead of becoming a doctor, however, he became a successful writer of detective stories.
statements.chinese: 然而，他没有成为一名医生，而是成为了一名成功的侦探小说作家。
我曾在他家度过一个我永远不会忘记的不愉快的周末。
statements.english: I once spent an uncomfortable weekend which I shall never forget at his house.
George showed me to the guest room, which he said was rarely used.
statements.chinese: 乔治把我带到客房，他说那个房间很少用。
他叫我收拾好行李，然后下来吃晚饭。
statements.english: He told me to unpack my things and then come down to dinner.
After I had stacked my shirts and underclothes in two empty drawers, I decided to hang in the cupboard one of the two suits I had brought with me.
statements.chinese: 我把衬衫和内衣叠放在两个空抽屉里后，决定把带来的两套西装中的一套挂进衣柜。

statements.english: I opened the cupboard door and then stood in front of it petrified.
statements.chinese: 我打开衣柜门，然后吓呆地站在它前面。
一个骷髅在我眼前晃动。
statements.english: A skeleton was dangling before my eyes.
The sudden movement of the door made it sway slightly, and it gave me the impression that it was about to leap out at me.
statements.chinese: 门的突然移动使它轻轻摇晃，给我一种它要扑向我的感觉。
我扔下西装，冲下楼去告诉乔治。
statements.english: Dropping my suit, I dashed downstairs to tell George.
This was worse than a terrible secret, this was a real skeleton.
statements.chinese: 这比一个可怕的秘密更糟糕，这是一个真正的骷髅。
但乔治却不以为然。
statements.english: But George was unsympathetic.
"Oh, that," he said with a smile, as if he were talking about an old friend.
statements.chinese: “哦，那个啊，”他微笑着说，好像在谈论一位老朋友。
“那是塞巴斯蒂安。”
statements.english: "That's Sebastian."

statements.chinese: “你忘了我以前也是医学生。”
statements.english: "You forget that I was a medical student once upon a time."

courses.title: Lesson 25: The Cutty Sark
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 25 条逐句练习

statements.english: One of the most famous sailing ships of the 19th century, the Cutty Sark, can still be seen at Greenwich.
statements.chinese: 作为19世纪最著名的帆船之一，卡蒂萨克号至今仍可在格林威治被参观。
她停泊在陆地上，每年有成千上万的人前来参观。
statements.english: She stands on dry land and is visited by thousands of people each year.

statements.chinese: 她作为过去伟大船只的令人印象深刻的提醒。
statements.english: She serves as an impressive reminder of the great ships of the past.
Before they were replaced by steamships, sailing vessels like the Cutty Sark were used to carry tea from China and wool from Australia.
statements.chinese: 在被蒸汽船取代之前，像卡蒂萨克号这样的帆船被用来从中国运茶叶，从澳大利亚运羊毛。
卡蒂萨克号是建造过的最快的帆船之一。
statements.english: The Cutty Sark was one of the fastest sailing ships that has ever been built.

statements.chinese: 唯一能与她匹敌的船是塞莫皮莱号。
statements.english: The only other ship to match her was the Thermopylae.
Both these ships set out from Shanghai on June the 18th, 1872, on an exciting race to England.
statements.chinese: 这两艘船于1872年6月18日从上海启航，进行一场激动人心的英国竞赛。

statements.english: This race, which went on for exactly four months, was the last of its kind.
statements.chinese: 这场持续了整整四个月的比赛，是同类比赛中的最后一次。

statements.english: It marked the end of the great tradition of ships with sails and the beginning of a new era.
statements.chinese: 它标志着帆船伟大传统的终结和新时代的开始。

statements.english: The first of the two ships to reach Java after the race had begun was the Thermopylae.
statements.chinese: 比赛开始后，两艘船中第一个抵达爪哇岛的是塞莫皮莱号。
但在印度洋上，卡蒂萨克号取得了领先。
statements.english: But on the Indian Ocean, the Cutty Sark took the lead.

statements.chinese: 似乎可以肯定她会是第一艘抵达的船。
statements.english: It seemed certain that she would be the first ship home.

statements.chinese: 但在比赛中，她运气很差。
statements.english: But during the race, she had a lot of bad luck.
In August, she was struck by a very heavy storm, during which her rudder was torn away.
statements.chinese: 八月份，她遭遇了一场非常猛烈的风暴，舵被撕裂了。

statements.english: The Cutty Sark rolled from side to side, and it became impossible to steer her.
statements.chinese: 卡蒂萨克号左右摇摆，无法操舵。

statements.english: A temporary rudder was made on board from spare planks, and it was fitted with great difficulty.
statements.chinese: 船上用备用木板制作了一个临时舵，并费了很大的劲才安装好。
这大大降低了船的速度。
statements.english: This greatly reduced the speed of the ship.
For there was danger that if she traveled too quickly, this rudder would be torn away as well.
statements.chinese: 因为存在危险，如果她航行过快，这个舵也会被撕裂。
因此，卡蒂萨克号失去了领先。
statements.english: Because of this, the Cutty Sark lost her lead.
After crossing the equator, the captain called in at a port to have a new rudder fitted.
statements.chinese: 越过赤道后，船长在一个港口停靠，安装了一个新舵。
但到那时，塞莫皮莱号已经领先了500多英里。
statements.english: But by now, the Thermopylae was over 500 miles ahead.
Though the new rudder was fitted at tremendous speed, it was impossible for the Cutty Sark to win.
statements.chinese: 尽管新舵以极快的速度安装好了，卡蒂萨克号还是不可能获胜。
她在塞莫皮莱号之后一周抵达英国。
statements.english: She arrived in England a week after the Thermopylae.
Even this was remarkable, considering that she had had so many delays.
statements.chinese: 即使这样也令人瞩目，考虑到她有如此多的延误。

statements.english: There is no doubt that if she had not lost her rudder, she would have won the race easily.
statements.chinese: 毫无疑问，如果她没有失去船舵，她会轻松赢得比赛。

courses.title: Lesson 26: Wanted a Large Biscuit Tin
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 23 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 没有人能避免受广告的影响。
statements.english: No one can avoid being influenced by advertisements.
Much as we may pride ourselves on our good taste, we are no longer free to choose the things we want.
statements.chinese: 尽管我们可能为自己的好品味而自豪，我们已不能自由选择我们想要的东西了。
因为广告对我们施加着一种微妙的影响。
statements.english: For advertising exerts a subtle influence on us.
In their efforts to persuade us to buy this or that product, advertisers have made a close study of human nature and have classified all our little weaknesses.
statements.chinese: 在他们努力说服我们购买这种或那种产品时，广告商对人性进行了深入研究，并将我们所有的弱点都分了类。
广告商多年前就发现，我们所有人都喜欢不劳而获。
statements.english: Advertisers discovered years ago that all of us love to get something for nothing.
An advertisement which begins with the magic word "free" can rarely go wrong.
statements.chinese: 一则以“免费”这个神奇词语开头的广告很少会出错。

statements.english: These days, advertisers not only offer free samples, but free cars, free houses, and free trips around the world as well.
statements.chinese: 如今，广告商不仅提供免费样品，还有免费汽车、免费房屋，以及免费环球旅行。
他们设计了数百种竞赛，使我们能够赢得巨额奖金。
statements.english: They devise hundreds of competitions which will enable us to win huge sums of money.

statements.chinese: 广播和电视使广告商能够以这种方式吸引数百万人的注意力。
statements.english: Radio and television have made it possible for advertisers to capture the attention of millions of people in this way.
During a radio program, a company of biscuit manufacturers once asked listeners to bake biscuits and to send them to their factory.
statements.chinese: 在一个广播节目中，一家饼干制造商曾要求听众烘焙饼干，然后寄到他们的工厂。
他们承诺以每磅2美元的价格购买听众烘焙的最大饼干。
statements.english: They offered to pay $2 a pound for the biggest biscuit baked by a listener.

statements.chinese: 这次竞赛的反响非常热烈。
statements.english: The response to this competition was tremendous.

statements.chinese: 不久，各种形状和大小的饼干开始陆续运到工厂。
statements.english: Before long, biscuits of all shapes and sizes began arriving at the factory.

statements.chinese: 有一位女士用独轮车运来一块饼干。
statements.english: One lady brought in a biscuit on a wheelbarrow.

statements.chinese: 它重达近500磅。
statements.english: It weighed nearly 500 pounds.

statements.chinese: 不久之后，一位男士带来一块饼干，它占据了他汽车的整个后备箱。
statements.english: A little later, a man came along with a biscuit which occupied the whole boot of his car.

statements.chinese: 所有寄来的饼干都经过仔细称重。
statements.english: All the biscuits that were sent were carefully weighed.

statements.chinese: 最大的一块重713磅。
statements.english: The largest was 713 pounds.

statements.chinese: 看起来这块饼干肯定会赢得奖品。
statements.english: It seemed certain that this would win the prize.
But just before the competition closed, a lorry arrived at the factory with a truly colossal biscuit which weighed 2,400 pounds.
statements.chinese: 但就在比赛结束前，一辆卡车抵达工厂，载着一块重达2400磅的真正巨大的饼干。

statements.english: It had been baked by a college student who had used over 1,000 pounds of flour, 800 pounds of sugar, 200 pounds of fat, and 400 pounds of various other ingredients.
statements.chinese: 它是由一名大学生烘焙的，他用了1000多磅面粉，800磅糖，200磅脂肪，以及400磅各种其他配料。
它太重了，不得不动用起重机才能将其从卡车上卸下。
statements.english: It was so heavy that a crane had to be used to remove it from the lorry.
The manufacturers had to pay more money than they had anticipated, for they bought the biscuit from the student for $4,800.
statements.chinese: 制造商不得不支付比他们预期更多的钱，因为他们以4800美元的价格从学生那里买下了这块饼干。

courses.title: Lesson 27: Nothing to Sell and Nothing to Buy
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 23 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 有人曾说，人人都是靠出卖某种东西而生活的。
statements.english: It has been said that everyone lives by selling something.

statements.chinese: 根据这个说法，教师靠出卖知识而生活。
statements.english: In the light of this statement, teachers live by selling knowledge.

statements.chinese: 哲学家靠出卖智慧而生活，牧师靠出卖精神安慰而生活。
statements.english: Philosophers by selling wisdom, and priests by selling spiritual comfort.
Though it may be possible to measure the value of material goods in terms of money, it is extremely difficult to estimate the true value of the services which people perform for us.
statements.chinese: 虽然衡量物质商品的价值可以用金钱来衡量，但要估计人们为我们提供的服务的真正价值却非常困难。
然而，我们可能会不情愿地支付高额费用给外科医生，因为他为我们提供了这项服务。
statements.english: Yet we might grudge paying a surgeon a high fee for offering us precisely this service.

statements.chinese: 社会的状况是这样的，技能必须像在商店里购买商品一样付费。
statements.english: The conditions of society are such that skills have to be paid for in the same way that goods are paid for at a shop.

statements.chinese: 每个人都有东西可以卖。
statements.english: Everyone has something to sell.

statements.chinese: 流浪汉似乎是这条普遍规则的唯一例外。
statements.english: Tramps seem to be the only exception to this general rule.

statements.chinese: 乞丐几乎是出卖自己作为人类的身份，以引起路人的怜悯。
statements.english: Beggars almost sell themselves as human beings to arouse the pity of passers-by.

statements.chinese: 但真正的流浪汉不是乞丐。
statements.english: But real tramps are not beggars.

statements.chinese: 他们没有什么可卖的，也不向别人索取什么。
statements.english: They have nothing to sell and require nothing from others.

statements.chinese: 在追求独立的过程中，他们不牺牲自己的人格尊严。
statements.english: In seeking independence, they do not sacrifice their human dignity.

statements.chinese: 流浪汉可能会向你要钱，但他绝不会要求你同情他。
statements.english: A tramp may ask you for money, but he will never ask you to feel sorry for him.

statements.chinese: 他是故意选择过这种生活的，并且完全清楚其后果。
statements.english: He has deliberately chosen to lead the life he leads and is fully aware of the consequences.

statements.chinese: 他可能永远不知道下一顿饭从哪里来。
statements.english: He may never be sure where the next meal is coming from.

statements.chinese: 但他却摆脱了困扰其他人的成千上万的焦虑。
statements.english: But he is free from the thousands of anxieties which afflict other people.

statements.chinese: 他少量的物质财产使他能够轻松地从一个地方移动到另一个地方。
statements.english: His few material possessions make it possible for him to move from place to place with ease.

statements.chinese: 由于必须露宿野外，他比我们大多数人更接近大自然。
statements.english: By having to sleep in the open, he gets far closer to the world of nature than most of us ever do.

statements.chinese: 他可能会偶尔打猎、乞讨或偷窃来维持生计。
statements.english: He may hunt, beg, or steal occasionally to keep himself alive.

statements.chinese: 在真正需要的时候，他甚至会做一点工作。
statements.english: He may even, in times of real need, do a little work.

statements.chinese: 但他绝不会牺牲自己的自由。
statements.english: But he will never sacrifice his freedom.

statements.chinese: 我们常常轻蔑地谈论流浪汉，并将他们与乞丐归为一类。
statements.english: We often speak with contempt for tramps and put them in the same class as beggars.

statements.chinese: 但我们中有多少人能诚实地说，我们没有对他们简单的生活方式和无忧无虑感到一丝羡慕呢？
statements.english: But how many of us can honestly say that we have not felt a little envious of their simple way of life and their freedom from care?

courses.title: Lesson 28: Five Pounds Too Dear
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 21 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 为什么连五镑也“嫌贵”？
statements.english: Why was even five pounds 'too dear' ?

statements.chinese: 当那艘巨型客轮驶进港口的时候，许多装载着货品的小船疾驶着向它靠拢。
statements.english: Small boats loaded with wares sped to the great liner as she was entering the harbour.

Before she had anchored, the men from the boats had climbed on board and the decks were soon covered with colourful rugs from Persia, silks from India, copper coffee pots, and beautiful handmade silverware.
statements.chinese: 没等船停稳，小船上的人就爬上了客轮。甲板上很快就摆满了：来自波斯的五光十色的地毯、印度的丝绸、铜咖啡壶以及制作精美的手工银器。
谁都很难不为之所动。
statements.english: It was difficult not to be tempted.
Many of the tourists on board had begun bargaining with the tradesmen, but I decided not to buy anything until I had disembarked.
statements.chinese: 船上许多游客已和小贩们讨价还价起来，而我却决定不买任何东西，直到下船为止。
我刚一下船，就受到一个要向我兜售钻石戒指的人的纠缠。
statements.english: I had no sooner got off the ship than I was assailed by a man who wanted to sell me a diamond ring.
I had no intention of buying one, but I could not conceal the fact that I was impressed by the size of the diamonds.
statements.chinese: 我根本不想买钻石戒指，但我不得不承认我还是给那些钻石的大小留下了深刻的印象。
有些钻石大得像弹子。
statements.english: Some of them were as big as marbles.

statements.chinese: 那个人竭力证明他的钻石是真的。
statements.english: The man went to great lengths to prove that the diamonds were real.

statements.chinese: 当我们走过一家商店的时候，他把一枚钻石使劲地抵在橱窗上，在玻璃上划出了一道深痕。
statements.english: As we were walking past a shop, he held a diamond firmly against the window and made a deep impression in the glass.

statements.chinese: 我花了半个多小时才摆脱了他。
statements.english: It took me over half an hour to get rid of him.

statements.chinese: 第二个向我走来的人是卖高档钢笔和手表的。
statements.english: The next man to approach me was selling expensive pens and watches.

statements.chinese: 我仔细地察看了一支钢笔。它看上去确实是真品。
statements.english: I examined one of the pens closely. It certainly looked genuine.

statements.chinese: 在金笔帽的底部，刻有“美国制造”的字样。
statements.english: At the base of the gold cap, the words 'made in the U.S.A.' had been neatly inscribed.

statements.chinese: 那人说这支笔值50镑，但作为特别优惠，他愿以30镑卖给我。
statements.english: The man said that the pen was worth ￡50, but as a special favour, he would let me have it for ￡30.

statements.chinese: 我摇了摇头，伸出5个手指，表示我愿付5镑。
statements.english: I shook my head and held up five fingers indicating that I was willing to pay ￡5.
Gesticulating wildly, the man acted as if he found my offer outrageous, but he eventually reduced the price to 10 pounds.
statements.chinese: 那人狂乱地打着手势，装出我的出价不可思议的样子，但最终还是把价格降到了10镑。

statements.english: Shrugging my shoulders I began to walk away when, a moment later, he ran after me and thrust the pen into my hands.
statements.chinese: 我耸了耸肩膀，刚要走开，片刻之后，他便追了上来，把钢笔塞到我手里。
尽管他不停地绝望地挥舞着双臂，但他还是爽快地收下了我给他的5镑钱。
statements.english: Though he kept throwing up his arms in despair, he readily accepted the ￡5 I gave him.

statements.chinese: 我对这笔了不起的交易特别满意——直到我回到船上。
statements.english: I felt especially pleased with my wonderful bargain--until I got back to the ship.
No matter how hard I tried, it was impossible to fill this beautiful pen with ink and to this day it has never written a single word!
statements.chinese: 无论我怎么努力，也无法把墨水灌进这支漂亮的钢笔里，而且直到今天，它连一个字也没写出来过！

courses.title: Lesson 29: Funny or Not
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 23 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: “病态”幽默的基础是什么？
statements.english: What is the basis of 'sick' humour?

statements.chinese: 我们觉得一个笑话好不好笑，在很大程度上取决于我们是在哪里长大的。
statements.english: Whether we find a joke funny or not largely depends on where we have been brought up.

statements.chinese: 幽默感与民族特点有着神秘的联系。
statements.english: The sense of humour is mysteriously bound up with national characteristics.

statements.chinese: 例如，法国人可能觉得俄罗斯笑话不好笑。
statements.english: A Frenchman, for instance, might find it hard to laugh at a Russian joke.
In the same way, a Russian might fail to see anything amusing in a joke which would make an Englishman laugh to tears.
statements.chinese: 同样，俄罗斯人可能觉得一个笑话没什么可乐的，而这个笑话却能让英国人捧腹大笑。
大多数有趣的故事都基于滑稽的情境。
statements.english: Most funny stories are based on comic situations.

statements.chinese: 尽管存在民族差异，但某些滑稽情境具有普遍的吸引力。
statements.english: In spite of national differences, certain funny situations have a universal appeal.
No matter where you live, you would find it difficult not to laugh at, say, Charlie Chaplin's early films.
statements.chinese: 无论你住在哪里，你都会觉得很难不对，比如说，查理·卓别林的早期电影发笑。
然而，一种主要源自美国的幽默新类型，最近流行起来。
statements.english: However, a new type of humour, which stems largely from U.S., has recently come into fashion.

statements.chinese: 它被称为“病态幽默”。喜剧演员将他们的笑话建立在悲剧情境上，例如暴力死亡或严重事故。
statements.english: It is called 'sick humour'. Comedians base their jokes on tragic situations like violent death or serious accidents.

statements.chinese: 许多人觉得这种笑话令人反感。
statements.english: Many people find this sort of joke distasteful.

statements.chinese: 下面这个“病态幽默”的例子能让你自己评判。
statements.english: The following example of 'sick humour' will enable you to judge for yourself.

statements.chinese: 一个右腿骨折的男人在圣诞节前几周被送进了医院。
statements.english: A man who had broken his right leg was taken to hospital a few weeks before Christmas.
From the moment he arrived there, he kept on pestering his doctor to tell him when he would be able to go home.
statements.chinese: 从他到达那里那一刻起，他就一直缠着医生，问他什么时候能回家。
他害怕不得不在医院过圣诞节。
statements.english: He dreaded having to spend Christmas in hospital.

statements.chinese: 尽管医生尽了力，但病人的康复很慢。
statements.english: Though the doctor did his best, the patient's recovery was slow.

statements.chinese: 圣诞节那天，这个男人右腿上仍然打着石膏。
statements.english: On Christmas day, the man still had his right leg in plaster.

statements.chinese: 他在床上度过了悲惨的一天，想着自己错过了所有的乐趣。
statements.english: He spent a miserable day in bed thinking of all the fun he was missing.
The following day, however, the doctor consoled him by telling him that his chances of being able to leave hospital in time for New Year celebrations were good.
statements.chinese: 然而，第二天，医生安慰他说，他赶在新年庆祝活动前出院的可能性很大。
男人振作起来，果然，在除夕夜他能一瘸一拐地去参加派对。
statements.english: The man took heart and sure enough, on New Year's Eve he was able to hobble along to a party.
To compensate for his unpleasant experiences in hospital, the man drank a little more than was good for him.
statements.chinese: 为了弥补他在医院的不愉快经历，他多喝了一点酒，这对他身体不好。
在此过程中，他玩得很开心，并且不停地告诉所有人他有多么讨厌医院。
statements.english: In the process, he enjoyed himself thoroughly and kept telling everybody how much he hated hospitals.

statements.chinese: 派对结束时，他还在嘟囔着关于医院的事情，这时他滑到了一块冰上，摔断了左腿。
statements.english: He was still mumbling something about hospitals at the end of the party when he slipped on a piece of ice and broke his left leg.

courses.title: Lesson 30: The Death of a Ghost
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 26 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 为什么两兄弟保守了这个秘密？
statements.english: Why did the two brothers keep the secret?

statements.chinese: 多年来，村民们一直认为恩德利农场闹鬼。
statements.english: For years, villagers believed that Endley farm was haunted.

statements.chinese: 这个农场归乔和鲍勃·科克斯两兄弟所有。
statements.english: The farm was owned by two brothers, Joe and Bob Cox.

statements.chinese: 他们雇了一些农场工人，但没有人愿意在那里长时间工作。
statements.english: They employed a few farmhands, but no one was willing to work there long.

statements.chinese: 每次有工人辞职，他们都会讲同样的故事。
statements.english: Every time a worker gave up his job, he told the same story.

statements.chinese: 农场工人说，他们醒来时总是发现工作已经在一夜之间完成了。
statements.english: Farm labourers said that they always woke up to find that work had been done overnight.

statements.chinese: 干草被割了，牛棚也被清理了。
statements.english: Hay had been cut and cowsheds had been cleaned.

statements.chinese: 一位彻夜未眠的农场工人声称在月光下看到一个身影在割玉米。
statements.english: A farm worker, who stayed up all night, claimed to have seen a figure cutting corn in the moonlight.

statements.chinese: 渐渐地，科克斯兄弟雇佣了一个尽职尽责的幽灵为他们做了大部分工作，这成了一个公认的事实。
statements.english: In time, it became an accepted fact that the Cox brothers employed a conscientious ghost that did most of their work for them.

statements.chinese: 没有人怀疑农场上可能还有其他人从未被见过。
statements.english: No one suspected that there might be someone else on the farm who had never been seen.

statements.chinese: 事实确实如此。
statements.english: This was indeed the case.

statements.chinese: 不久前，村民们惊讶地得知恩德利的幽灵已经死了。
statements.english: A short time ago, villagers were astonished to learn that the ghost of Endley had died.
Everyone went to the funeral, for the 'ghost' was none other than Eric Cox, a third brother who was supposed to have died as a young man.
statements.chinese: 所有人都去参加了葬礼，因为那个“幽灵”不是别人，正是埃里克·科克斯，据说他年轻时就去世了的第三个兄弟。
葬礼结束后，乔和鲍勃揭露了一个他们保守了五十多年的秘密。
statements.english: After the funeral, Joe and Bob revealed a secret which they had kept for over fifty years.

statements.chinese: 埃里克是家里的长子，比他的两个兄弟大得多。
statements.english: Eric had been the eldest son of the family, very much older than his two brothers.

statements.chinese: 第二次世界大战期间，他被迫参军。
statements.english: He had been obliged to join the army during the Second World War.

statements.chinese: 由于他厌恶军队生活，他决定开小差。
statements.english: As he hated army life, he decided to desert his regiment.
When he learnt that he would be sent abroad, he returned to the farm and his father hid him until the end of the war.
statements.chinese: 当他得知自己将被派往国外时，他回到了农场，他的父亲把他藏起来直到战争结束。
由于害怕当局，埃里克在战后也一直躲藏着。
statements.english: Fearing the authorities, Eric remained in hiding after the war as well.

statements.chinese: 他的父亲告诉所有人埃里克在战斗中牺牲了。
statements.english: His father told everybody that Eric had been killed in action.

statements.chinese: 唯一知道这个秘密的其他人是乔和鲍勃。
statements.english: The only other people who knew the secret were Joe and Bob.

statements.chinese: 他们甚至没有告诉他们的妻子。
statements.english: They did not even tell their wives.

statements.chinese: 当他们的父亲去世后，他们认为有责任继续把埃里克藏起来。
statements.english: When their father died they thought it their duty to keep Eric in hiding.

statements.chinese: 这么多年来，埃里克一直过着隐居生活。
statements.english: All these years, Eric had lived as a recluse.
He used to sleep during the day and work at night, quite unaware of the fact that he had become the ghost of Endley.
statements.chinese: 他白天睡觉，晚上工作，完全没有意识到自己已经成为了恩德利的幽灵。
然而，当他去世后，他的兄弟们发现再也无法保守这个秘密了。
statements.english: When he died, however, his brothers found it impossible to keep the secret any longer.

courses.title: Lesson 31: A Lovable Eccentric
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 23 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 真正的怪人从不刻意引人注目。
statements.english: True eccentrics never deliberately set out to draw attention to themselves.

statements.chinese: 他们不顾社会习俗，却丝毫没有意识到自己做了任何非凡的事情。
statements.english: They disregard social conventions without being conscious that they are doing anything extraordinary.
This invariably wins them the love and respect of others, for they add colour to the dull routine of everyday life.
statements.chinese: 这总是能为他们赢得他人的爱戴和尊敬，因为他们为平淡的日常生活增添了色彩。

statements.english: Up to the time of his death, Richard Colson was one of the most notable figures in our town.
statements.chinese: 直到他去世，理查德·科尔森是我们镇上最著名的人物之一。
他是一个精明而富有的商人。
statements.english: He was a shrewd and wealthy businessman.

statements.chinese: 但普通的镇民对他生活的这一面几乎一无所知。
statements.english: But the ordinary townsfolk hardly knew anything about this side of his life.
He was known to us all as Dicky, and his eccentricity had become legendary long before he died.
statements.chinese: 他被我们都称为迪基，在他去世很久之前，他的怪癖就已成为传奇。
迪基非常讨厌势利小人。
statements.english: Dicky disliked snobs intensely.
Though he owned a large car, he hardly ever used it, preferring always to go on foot.
statements.chinese: 尽管他拥有一辆豪华轿车，但他几乎从不使用，总是喜欢步行。
即使下大雨，他也拒绝打伞。
statements.english: Even when it was raining heavily, he refused to carry an umbrella.
One day, he walked into an expensive shop, after having been caught in a particularly heavy shower.
statements.chinese: 一天，他走进一家昂贵的商店，刚被一场特别大的雨淋透。

statements.english: He wanted to buy a 300-pound fur coat for his wife, but he was in such a bedraggled condition, that an assistant refused to serve him.
statements.chinese: 他想为妻子买一件300英镑的皮草大衣，但他当时衣衫褴褛，以至于一名店员拒绝为他服务。

statements.english: Dicky left the shop without a word, and returned carrying a large cloth bag.
statements.chinese: 迪基一言不发地离开了商店，然后提着一个大布袋回来了。
因为它非常重，他把它扔在柜台上。
statements.english: As it was extremely heavy, he dumped it on the counter.
The assistant asked him to leave, but Dicky paid no attention to him, and requested to see the manager.
statements.chinese: 店员让他离开，但迪基没有理会他，并要求见经理。

statements.english: Recognizing who the customer was, the manager was most apologetic, and reprimanded the assistant severely.
statements.chinese: 经理认出这位顾客是谁后，显得非常抱歉，并严厉训斥了店员。

statements.english: When Dicky was given the fur coat, he presented the assistant with the cloth bag.
statements.chinese: 当迪基拿到皮草大衣时，他把那个布袋交给了店员。
里面装着300英镑的硬币。
statements.english: It contained 300 pounds in pennies.

statements.chinese: 他坚持要店员在他离开前数清钱。
statements.english: He insisted on the assistant counting the money before he left.

statements.chinese: 总共72,000个硬币。
statements.english: 72,000 pennies in all.
On another occasion, he invited a number of important critics to see his private collection of modern paintings.
statements.chinese: 另一次，他邀请了一些重要的评论家参观他私人收藏的现代画作。

statements.english: This exhibition received a great deal of attention in the press, for though the pictures were supposed to be the work of famous artists, they had in fact been painted by Dicky.
statements.chinese: 这次展览受到了媒体的广泛关注，因为尽管这些画作据称是著名艺术家的作品，实际上却是迪基画的。

statements.english: It took him four years to stage this elaborate joke, simply to prove that critics do not always know what they are talking about.
statements.chinese: 他花了四年时间策划这个精心设计的玩笑，只是为了证明评论家并非总是知道自己在说什么。

courses.title: Lesson 32: A Lost Ship
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 21 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: “埃尔科”号的全体船员找到他们要寻找的东西了吗？为什么？
statements.english: Did the crew of the Elkor find what they were looking for? Why?

statements.chinese: 打捞行动彻底失败了。
statements.english: The salvage operation had been a complete failure.

statements.chinese: “埃尔科”号这艘小船在巴伦支海域搜寻了几个星期后，正在返航的途中。
statements.english: The small ship, Elkor, which had been searching the Barents Sea for weeks, was on its way home.

statements.chinese: 船长收到了一份来自大陆的电报，指示他放弃搜寻。
statements.english: A radio message from the mainland had been received by the ship's captain instructing him to give up the search.
The captain knew that another attempt would be made later, for the sunken ship he was trying to find had been carrying a precious cargo of gold bullion.
statements.chinese: 船长知道以后还会再进行一次尝试，因为他试图寻找的那艘沉船载有一批珍贵的金条。
尽管收到那份电报，“埃尔科”号的船长还是决定再试一次。
statements.english: Despite the message, the captain of the Elkor decided to try once more.

statements.chinese: 海底被强力拖网仔细搜寻，当一个箱子从海底被捞上来时，船上的人都非常兴奋。
statements.english: The sea bed was scoured with powerful nets and there was tremendous excitement on board when a chest was raised from the bottom.
Though the crew were at first under the impression that the lost ship had been found, the contents of the chest proved them wrong.
statements.chinese: 虽然船员们最初以为找到了那艘失踪的船，但箱子里的东西证明他们错了。
事实上，他们找到的是一艘多年前就已经沉没的船。
statements.english: What they had in fact found was a ship which had been sunk many years before.

statements.chinese: 箱子里装着一个名叫艾伦·菲尔丁的海员的个人物品。
statements.english: The chest contained the personal belongings of a seaman, Alan Fielding.

statements.chinese: 里面有书、衣服和照片，还有海员以前从他妻子那里收到的信件。
statements.english: There were books, clothing and photographs, together with letters which the seaman had once received from his wife.

statements.chinese: “埃尔科”号的船长命令他的船员尽可能多地从残骸中打捞物品。
statements.english: The captain of the Elkor ordered his men to salvage as much as possible from the wreck.
Nothing of value was found, but the numerous items which were brought to the surface proved to be of great interest.
statements.chinese: 没找到什么有价值的东西，但打捞上来的许多物品却引起了人们极大的兴趣。
从打捞上来的一门重型火炮，船长意识到这艘船一定是一艘巡洋舰。
statements.english: From a heavy gun that was raised, the captain realized that the ship must have been a cruiser.
In another chest which contained the belongings of a ship's officer, there was an unfinished letter which had been written on March 14th, 1943.
statements.chinese: 在另一个箱子里，装着一名船上军官的物品，里面有一封写于1943年3月14日、尚未写完的信。
船长从信中得知那艘失踪的船名叫“卡伦”号。
statements.english: The captain learnt from the letter that the name of the lost ship was the Karen.

statements.chinese: 最有价值的发现是船上的航海日志，其中一部分仍然可以阅读。
statements.english: The most valuable find of all was the ship's log book, parts of which it was still possible to read.

statements.chinese: 从日志中，船长得以把所有已发现的信息拼凑起来。
statements.english: From this the captain was able to piece together all the information that had come to light.

statements.chinese: “卡伦”号当时正在驶往俄罗斯的护航船队中，结果被一艘敌方潜艇鱼雷击中。
statements.english: The Karen had been sailing in a convoy to Russia when she was torpedoed by an enemy submarine.

statements.chinese: “埃尔科”号返回家园后，国防部的一名海军官员证实了这一点。
statements.english: This was later confirmed by a naval official at the Ministry of Defence after the Elkor had returned home.

statements.chinese: 所有找到的物品都被送往战争博物馆。
statements.english: All the items that were found were sent to the War Museum.

courses.title: Lesson 33: A Day to Remember
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 26 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 是什么事件引发了这一系列交通事故？
statements.english: What incident began the series of traffic accidents?

statements.chinese: 我们都经历过事事不顺的日子。
statements.english: We have all experienced days when everything goes wrong.

statements.chinese: 一天也许开始得很好，但突然间一切似乎都失去了控制。
statements.english: A day may begin well enough, but suddenly everything seems to get out of control.

statements.chinese: 事情总是这样，很多事情偏偏选择在同一时刻出错。
statements.english: What invariably happens is that a great number of things choose to go wrong at precisely the same moment.

statements.chinese: 仿佛一个微不足道的事件引发了一连串的连锁反应。
statements.english: It is as if a single unimportant event set up a chain of reactions.

statements.chinese: 假设你正在准备饭菜，同时还要照看婴儿。
statements.english: Let us suppose that you are preparing a meal and keeping an eye on the baby at the same time.

statements.chinese: 电话铃响了，这预示着一系列意想不到的灾难即将发生。
statements.english: The telephone rings and this marks the prelude to an unforeseen series of catastrophes.
While you are on the phone, the baby pulls the tablecloth off the table, smashing half your best crockery and cutting himself in the process.
statements.chinese: 当你打电话的时候，婴儿把桌布从桌子上扯了下来，打碎了你一半最好的餐具，还把自己划伤了。
你急忙挂断电话，去照看婴儿、餐具等。
statements.english: You hang up hurriedly and attend to baby, crockery, etc.

statements.chinese: 与此同时，饭菜烧糊了。
statements.english: Meanwhile, the meal gets burnt.

statements.chinese: 好像这些还不足以让你落泪，你的丈夫又回来了，出乎意料地带了三位客人来吃晚饭。
statements.english: As if this were not enough to reduce you to tears, your husband arrives, unexpectedly bringing three guests to dinner.

statements.chinese: 事情也会大规模地出错，正如最近在悉尼郊区帕拉马塔的一些人所发现的那样。
statements.english: Things can go wrong on a big scale as a number of people recently discovered in Parramatta, a suburb of Sydney.

statements.chinese: 一天晚上，在交通高峰期，两辆汽车相撞，两位司机开始争吵起来。
statements.english: During the rush hour one evening two cars collided and both drivers began to argue.

statements.chinese: 紧跟在两辆车后面的一位女士碰巧是位新手司机。
statements.english: The woman immediately behind the two cars happened to be a learner.

statements.chinese: 她突然惊慌失措，把车停了下来。
statements.english: She suddenly got into a panic and stopped her car.

statements.chinese: 这使得跟在她后面的司机猛踩刹车。
statements.english: This made the driver following her brake hard.

statements.chinese: 他的妻子坐在他旁边，手里拿着一个大蛋糕。
statements.english: His wife was sitting beside him holding a large cake.
As she was thrown forward, the cake went right through the windscreen and landed on the road.
statements.chinese: 当她向前扑去时，蛋糕直接穿过挡风玻璃，落在了路上。

statements.english: Seeing a cake flying through the air, a lorry driver who was drawing up alongside the car, pulled up all of a sudden.
statements.chinese: 看到一个蛋糕飞过空中，一位正把车开到汽车旁边的货车司机，突然把车停了下来。
货车上装满了空啤酒瓶，几百个瓶子从车后部滑落到路上。
statements.english: The lorry was loaded with empty beer bottles and hundreds of them slid off the back of the vehicle and on to the road.

statements.chinese: 这又引发了另一场激烈的争吵。
statements.english: This led to yet another angry argument.

statements.chinese: 与此同时，后面的交通堵塞了。
statements.english: Meanwhile, the traffic piled up behind.

statements.chinese: 警察花了将近一个小时才让交通再次恢复通行。
statements.english: It took the police nearly an hour to get the traffic on the move again.

statements.chinese: 与此同时，货车司机不得不清扫数百个碎瓶子。
statements.english: In the meantime, the lorry driver had to sweep up hundreds of broken bottles.

statements.chinese: 只有两只流浪狗从这场混乱中受益，因为它们贪婪地吞食了剩下的蛋糕。
statements.english: Only two stray dogs benefited from all this confusion, for they greedily devoured what was left of the cake.

statements.chinese: 真是倒霉的一天！
statements.english: It was just one of those days!

courses.title: Lesson 34: A Happy Discovery
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 23 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 什么是“幸福的发现”？
statements.english: What was the 'happy discovery' ?

statements.chinese: 古玩店对许多人来说都有一种特殊的魅力。
statements.english: Antique shops exert a peculiar fascination on a great many people.
The more expensive kind of antique shop where rare objects are beautifully displayed in glass cases to keep them free from dust is usually a forbidding place.
statements.chinese: 那些高档古玩店，珍品都漂亮地陈列在玻璃柜里以免沾染灰尘，通常是令人望而却步的地方。
但对于不那么做作的古玩店，人们无需鼓起勇气进去。
statements.english: But no one has to muster up courage to enter a less pretentious antique shop.

statements.chinese: 人们总是希望在那些发霉、阴暗、杂乱的房间构成的迷宫中，能在堆满地板的各式各样的旧货中找到一件真正的珍品。
statements.english: There is always hope that in its labyrinth of musty, dark, disordered rooms a real rarity will be found amongst the piles of assorted junk that litter the floors.

statements.chinese: 没有人会偶然发现珍品。
statements.english: No one discovers a rarity by chance.
A truly dedicated bargain hunter must have patience, and above all, the ability to recognize the worth of something when he sees it.
statements.chinese: 一个真正专注的廉价商品搜寻者必须有耐心，最重要的是，当他看到一件东西时，要有识别其价值的能力。
为此，他必须至少和经销商一样知识渊博。
statements.english: To do this, he must be at least as knowledgeable as the dealer.
Like a scientist bent on making a discovery, he must cherish the hope that one day he will be amply rewarded.
statements.chinese: 就像一个决心有所发现的科学家一样，他必须怀揣希望，总有一天他会得到丰厚的回报。
我的老朋友弗兰克·哈利迪就是这样一个人。
statements.english: My old friend, Frank Halliday, is just such a person.

statements.chinese: 他常常向我描述他是如何以区区50英镑买到一件杰作的。
statements.english: He has often described to me how he picked up a masterpiece for a mere ￡50.

statements.chinese: 一个星期六的上午，弗兰克去了我附近的一家古玩店。
statements.english: One Saturday morning, Frank visited an antique shop in my neighbourhood.

statements.chinese: 因为他以前从未来过这里，所以发现了很多让他感兴趣的东西。
statements.english: As he had never been there before, he found a great deal to interest him.

statements.chinese: 上午很快过去了，弗兰克正准备离开时，他注意到地板上放着一个大包装箱。
statements.english: The morning passed rapidly and Frank was about to leave when he noticed a large packing case lying on the floor.

statements.chinese: 经销商告诉他，这东西刚到，但他懒得打开。
statements.english: The dealer told him that it had just come in, but that he could not be bothered to open it.

statements.chinese: 弗兰克恳求他打开，经销商不情愿地撬开了箱子。
statements.english: Frank begged him to do so and the dealer reluctantly prised it open.

statements.chinese: 里面的东西令人失望。
statements.english: The contents were disappointing.

statements.chinese: 除了一个看起来有趣的雕花匕首外，箱子里装满了陶器，其中大部分都碎了。
statements.english: Apart from an interesting-looking carved dagger, the box was full of crockery, much of it broken.

statements.chinese: 弗兰克轻轻地把陶器从箱子里拿出来，突然注意到包装箱底部有一幅微型画。
statements.english: Frank gently lifted the crockery out of the box and suddenly noticed a miniature painting at the bottom of the packing case.

statements.chinese: 由于它的构图和线条让他想起了他很熟悉的一幅意大利画作，他决定买下它。
statements.english: As its composition and line reminded him of an Italian painting he knew well, he decided to buy it.

statements.chinese: 经销商匆匆看了一眼，告诉他这幅画值50英镑。
statements.english: Glancing at it briefly the dealer told him that it was worth ￡50.

statements.chinese: 弗兰克几乎无法掩饰他的兴奋，因为他知道他做了一个真正的发现。
statements.english: Frank could hardly conceal his excitement, for he knew that he had made a real discovery.

statements.chinese: 这幅小画被证实是科雷吉奥的一幅不为人知的杰作，价值数十万英镑。
statements.english: The tiny painting proved to be an unknown masterpiece by Correggio and was worth hundreds and thousands of pounds.

courses.title: Lesson 35: Justice was Done
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 22 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 在课文中，“正义”一词被赋予了两种不同的含义。
statements.english: The word 'justice' is given two different meanings in the text.

statements.chinese: 它们之间有什么区别呢？
statements.english: What is the distinction between them?

statements.chinese: “正义”一词通常与法庭联系在一起。
statements.english: The word justice is usually associated with courts of law.

statements.chinese: 当一个人的清白或罪行被无可置疑地证明时，我们可能会说正义得到了伸张。
statements.english: We might say that justice has been done when a man's innocence or guilt has been proved beyond doubt.

statements.chinese: 正义是法律复杂机制的一部分。
statements.english: Justice is part of the complex machinery of the law.

statements.chinese: 追求正义的人会踏上一段艰难的旅程，而且永远无法确定他们是否会找到它。
statements.english: Those who seek it, undertake an arduous journey and can never be sure that they will find it.

statements.chinese: 法官，无论多么明智或杰出，都是人，也可能犯错误。
statements.english: Judges, however wise or eminent, are human and can make mistakes.

statements.chinese: 在极少数情况下，正义几乎不再是一个抽象的概念。
statements.english: There are rare instances when justice almost ceases to be an abstract concept.

statements.chinese: 奖励或惩罚在完全没有人类干预的情况下被施加。
statements.english: Reward or punishment are meted out quite independent of human interference.

statements.chinese: 在这种时候，正义就像一股活生生的力量。
statements.english: At such times, justice acts like a living force.
When we use a phrase like 'it serves him right', we are, in part, admitting that a certain set of circumstances has enabled justice to act of its own accord.
statements.chinese: 当我们使用“活该”这样的短语时，我们部分承认了某种情况使正义得以自然而然地发挥作用。

statements.english: When a thief was caught on the premises of a large jewellery store one morning, the shop assistants must have found it impossible to resist the temptation to say 'it serves him right'.
statements.chinese: 一天早上，当一个小偷在一家大型珠宝店的院子里被抓到时，店员们一定觉得很难抵制住说“活该”的冲动。
这家店是一座由老房子改建而成的，有很多大的废弃壁炉和又高又窄的烟囱。
statements.english: The shop was an old converted house with many large, disused fireplaces and tall, narrow chimneys.

statements.chinese: 快到中午时，一个女孩听到墙后传来一阵低沉的哭声。
statements.english: Towards midday, a girl heard a muffled cry coming from behind one of the walls.
As the cry was repeated several times, she ran to tell the manager who promptly rang up the fire brigade.
statements.chinese: 哭声重复了几次之后，她跑去告诉经理，经理立刻给消防队打了电话。

statements.english: The cry had certainly come from one of the chimneys, but as there were so many of them, the firemen could not be certain which one it was.
statements.chinese: 哭声确实是从一个烟囱里传出来的，但由于烟囱太多，消防员无法确定是哪一个。
他们通过敲击墙壁并聆听那个人的哭声来确定正确的烟囱。
statements.english: They located the right chimney by tapping at the walls and listening for the man's cries.
After chipping through a wall which was eighteen inches thick, they found that a man had been trapped in the chimney.
statements.chinese: 在凿穿一堵18英寸厚的墙后，他们发现一个人被困在烟囱里了。

statements.english: As it was extremely narrow, the man was unable to move, but the fire fighters were eventually able to free him by cutting a huge hole in the wall.
statements.chinese: 由于烟囱非常狭窄，那个人无法动弹，但消防员最终通过在墙上凿开一个大洞，成功地解救了他。

statements.english: The sorry-looking, blackened figure that emerged, admitted at once that he had tried to break into the shop during the night but had got stuck in the chimney.
statements.chinese: 那个狼狈不堪、浑身漆黑的人影出现后，立刻承认他曾试图在夜间闯入商店，但被卡在了烟囱里。
他已经在里面待了将近十个小时。
statements.english: He had been there for nearly ten hours.

statements.chinese: 甚至在将那个人移交给警方之前，正义就已经得到了伸张。
statements.english: Justice had been done even before the man was handed over to the police.

courses.title: Lesson 36: A Chance in a Million
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 20 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 这百万分之一的机遇是什么呢？
statements.english: What was the chance in a million?

statements.chinese: 我们不像以前那样轻信了。
statements.english: We are less credulous than we used to be.
In the nineteenth century, a novelist would bring his story to a conclusion by presenting his readers with a series of coincidences--most of them wildly improbable.
statements.chinese: 在19世纪，小说家在故事的结尾会给读者安排一连串的巧合——其中大部分都是极不可能发生的。
读者们欣然接受一个默默无闻的女仆竟然是主人公的母亲这一事实。
statements.english: Readers happily accepted the fact that an obscure maidservant was really the hero's mother.
A long-lost brother, who was presumed dead, was really alive all the time and wickedly plotting to bring about the hero's downfall. And so on.
statements.chinese: 一个被认为已死去的失散多年的兄弟，实际上一直活着，并且阴险地策划着让主人公垮台。诸如此类。
现代读者会觉得这种天真的结局完全不能接受。
statements.english: Modern readers would find such naive solutions totally unacceptable.

statements.chinese: 然而，在现实生活中，情况有时确实会凑巧地导致巧合的发生，除了19世纪的小说家，其他任何人都觉得不可思议。
statements.english: Yet, in real life, circumstances do sometimes conspire to bring about coincidences which anyone but a nineteenth century novelist would find incredible.
When I was a boy, my grandfather told me how a German taxi driver, Franz Bussman, found a brother who was thought to have been killed twenty years before.
statements.chinese: 我小时候，祖父给我讲了一个德国出租车司机弗朗兹·布斯曼的故事，他找到了一个被认为在20年前阵亡的兄弟。
在和妻子徒步旅行时，他停下来和一名工人交谈。
statements.english: While on a walking tour with his wife, he stopped to talk to a workman.
After they had gone on, Mrs. Bussman commented on the workman's close resemblance to her husband and even suggested that he might be his brother.
statements.chinese: 他们继续前行后，布斯曼夫人评论说那个工人长得很像她丈夫，甚至猜测他可能是她丈夫的兄弟。

statements.english: Franz poured scorn on the idea, pointing out that his brother had been killed in action during the war.
statements.chinese: 弗朗兹对这个想法嗤之以鼻，指出他兄弟在战争中阵亡了。

statements.english: Though Mrs. Bussman was fully acquainted with this story, she thought that there was a chance in a million that she might be right.
statements.chinese: 尽管布斯曼夫人完全了解这个故事，她觉得她有可能说对了，尽管几率是百万分之一。
几天后，她派了一个男孩去问那个工人，他是否叫汉斯·布斯曼。
statements.english: A few days later, she sent a boy to the workman to ask him if his name was Hans Bussman.

statements.chinese: 不用说，那个人的名字就是汉斯·布斯曼，他确实是弗朗兹失散多年的兄弟。
statements.english: Needless to say, the man's name was Hans Bussman and he really was Franz's long-lost brother.
When the brothers were reunited, Hans explained how it was that he was still alive.
statements.chinese: 兄弟俩团聚后，汉斯解释了他为什么还活着。

statements.english: After having been wounded towards the end of the war, he had been sent to hospital and was separated from his unit.
statements.chinese: 在战争快结束时受伤后，他被送往医院，与部队失散了。
医院被轰炸了，汉斯徒步回到了西德。
statements.english: The hospital had been bombed and Hans had made his way back into Western Germany on foot.

statements.chinese: 同时，他的部队失散了，所有关于他的记录都被销毁了。
statements.english: Meanwhile, his unit was lost and all records of him had been destroyed.
Hans returned to his family home, but the house had been bombed and no one in the neighbourhood knew what had become of the inhabitants.
statements.chinese: 汉斯回到了他的老家，但是房子被炸毁了，邻居们也不知道住户们怎么样了。

statements.english: Assuming that his family had been killed during an air raid, Hans settled down in a village fifty miles away where he had remained ever since.
statements.chinese: 以为他的家人在空袭中丧生，汉斯在一个五十英里外的小村庄安顿下来，自此一直住在那里。

courses.title: Lesson 37: The Westhaven Express
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 25 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 作者犯了什么错误？
statements.english: What was the mistake the author made?

statements.chinese: 我们已经习惯了认为火车是准时的。
statements.english: We have learnt to expect that trains will be punctual.

statements.chinese: 经过多年的条件反射，我们大多数人对火车时刻表都产生了不可动摇的信任。
statements.english: After years of conditioning, most of us have developed an unshakable faith in railway timetables.
Ships may be delayed by storms; flights may be cancelled because of bad weather; but trains must be on time.
statements.chinese: 船只可能因风暴而延误；航班可能因恶劣天气而取消；但火车必须准时。
只有异常大的降雪才可能暂时打乱铁路服务。
statements.english: Only an exceptionally heavy snow fall might temporarily dislocate railway services.

statements.chinese: 当事情出错时，责备铁路当局实在是太容易了。
statements.english: It is all too easy to blame the railway authorities when something does go wrong.

statements.chinese: 事实是，当错误发生时，它们更有可能是我们的，而不是他们的。
statements.english: The truth is that when mistakes occur, they are more likely to be ours than theirs.

statements.chinese: 查阅了我的火车时刻表后，我满意地注意到有一趟开往韦斯特黑文的特快列车。
statements.english: After consulting my railway timetable, I noted with satisfaction that there was an express train to Westhaven.

statements.chinese: 它直接从我当地的车站出发，行程仅需一小时十七分钟。
statements.english: It went direct from my local station and the journey lasted a mere hour and seventeen minutes.

statements.chinese: 当我登上火车时，我不禁注意到许多当地人也上车了。
statements.english: When I boarded the train, I could not help noticing that a great many local people got on as well.

statements.chinese: 当时，这并没有让我觉得奇怪。
statements.english: At the time, this did not strike me as odd.

statements.chinese: 我想，除了我自己之外，肯定有很多人也希望利用这项优质服务。
statements.english: I reflected that there must be a great many people besides myself who wished to take advantage of this excellent service.

statements.chinese: 当火车在离铁路线几英里外的一个小站威德利停靠时，我也没有感到惊讶。
statements.english: Neither was I surprised when the train stopped at Widley, a tiny station a few miles along the line.

statements.chinese: 即使是强大的特快列车也可能被信号灯拦住。
statements.english: Even a mighty express train can be held up by signals.

statements.chinese: 但当火车在一个又一个车站磨蹭时，我开始感到疑惑。
statements.english: But when the train dawdled at station after station, I began to wonder.

statements.chinese: 我突然意识到，这趟特快列车并不是以每小时九十英里的速度呼啸而过，而是以每小时三十英里的速度缓慢行驶。
statements.english: It suddenly dawned on me that this express was not roaring down the line at ninety miles an hour, but barely chugging along at thirty.

statements.chinese: 一小时十七分钟过去了，我们甚至还没有走完一半的路程。
statements.english: One hour and seventeen minutes passed and we had not even covered half the distance.

statements.chinese: 我问一位乘客这是否是韦斯特黑文特快，但他甚至没有听说过。
statements.english: I asked a passenger if this was the Westhaven Express, but he had not even heard of it.

statements.chinese: 我决定一到站就投诉。
statements.english: I determined to lodge a complaint as soon as we arrived.

statements.chinese: 两个小时后，我正在韦斯特黑文车站愤怒地与站长交谈。
statements.english: Two hours later, I was talking angrily to the station master at Westhaven.

statements.chinese: 当他否认这趟火车存在时，我借了他的时刻表。
statements.english: When he denied the train's existence, I borrowed his copy of the timetable.

statements.chinese: 当我告诉他白纸黑字写着时，我的声音带着一丝胜利。
statements.english: There was a note of triumph in my voice when I told him that it was there in black and white.

statements.chinese: 他简短地瞥了一眼，然后告诉我再看一次。
statements.english: Glancing at it briefly, he told me to look again.

statements.chinese: 一个小小的星号引导我看到了页面底部的脚注。
statements.english: A tiny asterisk conducted me to a footnote at the bottom of the page.

statements.chinese: 它写着：“此项服务已暂停。”
statements.english: It said: 'This service has been suspended.'

courses.title: Lesson 38: The First Calendar
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 20 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 刻在石头、骨头和象牙上的点、线和符号有什么重要性？
statements.english: What is the importance of the dots, lines, and symbols engraved on stone, bones and ivory?

statements.chinese: 未来的历史学家在记录我们这个时代的历史时将处于独特的地位。
statements.english: Future historians will be in a unique position when they come to record the history of our own times.

statements.chinese: 他们将很难知道从不断积累的大量证据中选择哪些事实。
statements.english: They will hardly know which facts to select from the great mass of evidence that steadily accumulates.

statements.chinese: 更重要的是，他们不必仅仅依赖书面文字。
statements.english: What is more, they will not have to rely solely on the written word.

statements.chinese: 电影、视频、CD和CD-ROM只是他们将拥有的令人眼花缭乱的信息中的一部分。
statements.english: Films, videos, CDs and CD-ROMs are just some of the bewildering amount of information they will have.

statements.chinese: 他们将能够，可以说，看到和听到我们的行动。
statements.english: They will be able, as it were, to see and hear us in action.

statements.chinese: 但是，试图重构遥远过去的历史学家总是面临一项艰巨的任务。
statements.english: But the historian attempting to reconstruct the distant past is always faced with a difficult task.

statements.chinese: 他必须从仅有的稀少线索中推断出他所能推断的一切。
statements.english: He has to deduce what he can from the few scanty clues available.

statements.chinese: 即使看似微不足道的遗迹也能为早期人类的历史提供有趣的线索。
statements.english: Even seemingly insignificant remains can shed interesting light on the history of early man.
Up to now, historians have assumed that calendars came into being with the advent of agriculture, for then man was faced with a real need to understand something about the seasons.
statements.chinese: 迄今为止，历史学家一直认为日历是随着农业的出现而产生的，因为那时人类确实需要了解一些关于季节的知识。
最近的科学证据似乎表明这个假设是错误的。
statements.english: Recent scientific evidence seems to indicate that this assumption is incorrect.

statements.chinese: 历史学家长期以来一直对刻在墙壁、骨头和猛犸象牙上的点、线和符号感到困惑。
statements.english: Historians have long been puzzled by dots, lines and symbols which have been engraved on walls, bones, and the ivory tusks of mammoths.

statements.chinese: 制造这些标记的游牧民族在最后一次冰河时期（约公元前35,000年开始，约公元前10,000年结束）靠狩猎和捕鱼为生。
statements.english: The nomads who made these markings lived by hunting and fishing during the last Ice Age which began about 35, 000 B.C. and ended about 10, 000 B.C.
By correlating markings made in various parts of the world, historians have been able to read this difficult code.
statements.chinese: 通过关联世界各地制作的标记，历史学家已经能够解读这个难懂的密码。
他们发现它与日子的流逝和月亮的盈亏有关。
statements.english: They have found that it is connected with the passage of days and the phases of the moon.

statements.chinese: 事实上，这是一种原始的日历。
statements.english: It is, in fact, a primitive type of calendar.

statements.chinese: 长期以来人们都知道墙壁上描绘的狩猎场景不仅仅是一种艺术表现形式。
statements.english: It has long been known that the hunting scenes depicted on walls were not simply a form of artistic expression.

statements.chinese: 它们具有明确的含义，因为它们是早期人类最接近书写文字的形式。
statements.english: They had a definite meaning, for they were as near as early man could get to writing.

statements.chinese: 这些绘画与有时伴随它们的标记之间可能存在明确的关系。
statements.english: It is possible that there is a definite relation between these paintings and the markings that sometimes accompany them.

statements.chinese: 看来人类早在比人们猜测的20,000年前就在真正努力理解季节了。
statements.english: It seems that man was making a real effort to understand the seasons 20, 000 years earlier than has been supposed.

courses.title: Lesson 39: Nothing to Worry About
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 23 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 布鲁斯的行为与其他人的行为有什么不同？
statements.english: What was the differnce between Bruce's behaviour and that of other people?

statements.chinese: 穿过平原的崎岖道路很快变得非常糟糕，以至于我们试图让布鲁斯开车回到我们来时的村庄。
statements.english: The rough road across the plain soon became so bad that we tried to get Bruce to drive back to the village we had come from.

statements.chinese: 尽管路面上布满了巨石和坑洞，布鲁斯却丝毫没有感到不安。
statements.english: Even though the road was littered with boulders and pitted with holes, Bruce was not in the least perturbed.

statements.chinese: 他扫了一眼地图，告诉我们下一个村庄只有区区二十英里远。
statements.english: Glancing at his map, he informed us that the next village was a mere twenty miles away.

statements.chinese: 并不是布鲁斯总是低估困难。
statements.english: It was not that Bruce always underestimated difficulties.

statements.chinese: 他根本就没有危险意识。
statements.english: He simply had no sense of danger at all.

statements.chinese: 无论条件如何，他都认为汽车应该尽可能快地行驶。
statements.english: No matter what the conditions were, he believed that a car should be driven as fast as it could possibly go.

statements.chinese: 当我们在尘土飞扬的小路上颠簸时，我们猛打方向盘以避开大块巨石。
statements.english: As we bumped over the dusty track, we swerved to avoid large boulders.

statements.chinese: 车轮卷起石子，在车底下发出不祥的敲击声。
statements.english: The wheels scooped up stones which hammered ominously under the car.

statements.chinese: 我们确信迟早会有石子把我们的油箱撕开一个洞或者损坏发动机。
statements.english: We felt sure that sooner or later a stone would rip a hole in our petrol tank or damage the engine.

statements.chinese: 因此，我们不停地回头看，想知道我们是否在身后留下了一串油迹和汽油。
statements.english: Because of this, we kept looking back, wondering if we were leaving a trail of oil and petrol behind us.
What a relief it was when the boulders suddenly disappeared, giving way to a stretch of plain where the only obstacles were clumps bushes.
statements.chinese: 当巨石突然消失时，我们松了一口气，取而代之的是一片平坦的开阔地，那里唯一的障碍物是灌木丛。
但更糟糕的还在后面。就在我们前方，有一道巨大的裂缝。
statements.english: But there was worse to come. Just ahead of us there was a huge fissure.

statements.chinese: 布鲁斯响应我们再次的恳求，停了下来。
statements.english: In response to renewed pleadings, Bruce stopped.

statements.chinese: 尽管我们都下车检查裂缝，他却仍然待在车里。
statements.english: Though we all got out to examine the fissure, he remained in the car.

statements.chinese: 我们告诉他，那道裂缝绵延五十码，宽两英尺，深四英尺。
statements.english: We informed him that the fissure extended for fifty yards and was two feet wide and four feet deep.

statements.chinese: 即使这样也毫无作用。
statements.english: Even this had no effect.
Bruce went into a low gear and drove at a terrifying speed, keeping the front wheels astride the crack as he followed its zigzag course.
statements.chinese: 布鲁斯挂入低档，以惊人的速度行驶，让前轮跨过裂缝，沿着它之字形的路线前进。
还没等我们有时间担心会发生什么，我们又回到了平原上。
statements.english: Before we had time to worry about what might happen, we were back on the plain again.

statements.chinese: 布鲁斯又一次查阅了地图，告诉我们村庄现在只剩下十五英里远了。
statements.english: Bruce consulted the map once more and told us that the village was now only fifteen miles away.

statements.chinese: 我们的下一个障碍是一个大约半英里宽的浅水池。
statements.english: Our next obstacle was a shallow pool of water about half a mile across.

statements.chinese: 布鲁斯冲了过去，但在水池中央，汽车嘎然而止。
statements.english: Bruce charged at it, but in the middle, the car came to a grinding halt.

statements.chinese: 仪表盘上一个黄灯愤怒地闪烁着，布鲁斯却高兴地宣布发动机里没油了！
statements.english: A yellow light on the dashboard flashed angrily and Bruce cheerfully announced that there was no oil in the engine!

courses.title: Lesson 40: Who's Who
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 21 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 警察是如何发现这整件事是个恶作剧的？
statements.english: How did the policeman discover that the whole thing was a joke?

statements.chinese: 大学学生为什么似乎比其他人更喜欢恶作剧，这一点从未得到解释。
statements.english: It has never been explained why university students seem to enjoy practical jokes more than anyone else.

statements.chinese: 学生们擅长一种特殊类型的恶作剧：骗局。
statements.english: Students specialize in a particular type of practical joke: the hoax.

statements.chinese: 邀请消防队扑灭一场不存在的火灾是一种粗俗的欺骗形式，任何有自尊的学生都不会沉溺其中。
statements.english: Inviting the fire brigade to put out a nonexistent fire is a crude form of deception which no self-respecting student would ever indulde in.

statements.chinese: 学生们经常制造一些有趣的场面，除了受害者，每个人都觉得好笑。
statements.english: Students often create amusing situations which are funny to everyone except the victims.

When a student recently saw two workmen using a pneumatic drill outside his university, he immediately telephoned the police and informed them that two students dressed up as workmen were tearing up the road with a pneumatic drill.
statements.chinese: 最近，当一名学生看到两名工人在他大学外面使用一台气动钻时，他立即打电话报警，并告知警察有两名打扮成工人的学生正在用气动钻挖路。

statements.english: As soon as he had hung up, he went over to the workmen and told them that if a policeman ordered them to go away, they were not to take him seriously.
statements.chinese: 他一挂掉电话，就走到工人那里，告诉他们如果一个警察命令他们离开，他们不必把他当真。
他补充说，有个学生打扮成警察，正在对人们开各种愚蠢的玩笑。
statements.english: He added that a student had dressed up as a policeman and was playing all sorts of silly jokes on people.

statements.chinese: 警察和工人都很感谢这名学生提供的这条提前消息。
statements.english: Both the police and the workmen were grateful to the student for this piece of advance information.

statements.chinese: 这名学生藏在附近的一个拱门里，在那里他能看到和听到发生的一切。
statements.english: The student hid in an archway nearby where he could watch and hear everything that went on.

statements.chinese: 果不其然，一名警察来到了现场，并礼貌地要求工人离开。
statements.english: Sure enough, a policeman arrived on the scene and politely asked the workmen to go away.

statements.chinese: 当他从其中一名工人那里得到非常粗鲁的答复时，他威胁要强行把他们带走。
statements.english: When he received a very rude reply from one of the workmen, he threatened to remove them by force.

statements.chinese: 工人们告诉他想怎样就怎样，于是警察打电话请求支援。
statements.english: The workmen told him to do as he pleased and the policeman telephoned for help.

statements.chinese: 不久之后，又有4名警察赶到，并与工人们进行交涉。
statements.english: Shortly afterwards, 4 more policemen arrived and remonstrated with the workmen.

statements.chinese: 由于工人们拒绝停止工作，警察试图没收气动钻。
statements.english: As the men refused to stop working, the police attempted to seize the pneumatic drill.

statements.chinese: 工人们激烈反抗，其中一人发了脾气。
statements.english: The workmen struggled fiercely and one of them lost his temper.

statements.chinese: 他威胁要报警。
statements.english: He threatened to call the police.

statements.chinese: 听罢此言，警察讽刺地指出，这几乎没有必要，因为这些人已经被逮捕了。
statements.english: At this, the police pointed out ironically that this would hardly be necessary as the men were already under arrest.

statements.chinese: 其中一名工人假装认真地问道，在被带到警察局之前，他是否可以打个电话。
statements.english: Pretending to speak seriously, one of the workmen asked if he might make a telephone call before being taken to the station.

statements.chinese: 许可被准予，一名警察陪他去了公用电话亭。
statements.english: Permission was granted and a policeman accompanied him to a pay phone.

statements.chinese: 只有当他看到那个人实际上是在打电话给警察时，他才意识到他们都成了骗局的受害者。
statements.english: Only when he saw that the man was actually telephoning the police did he realize that they had all been the victims of a hoax.

courses.title: Lesson 41: Illusions of Pastoral Peace
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 28 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 乡下人进城看戏，有什么特殊的忧虑会使他们败兴？
statements.english: What particular anxiety spoils the country dweller's visit to the theatre?

statements.chinese: 宁静的乡村生活从来没有吸引过我。
statements.english: The quiet life of the country has never appealed to me.
City born and city bred, I have always regarded the country as something you look at through a train window, or something you occasionally visit during the weekend.
statements.chinese: 我生在城里，长在城里，始终认为乡村是透过火车车窗看的东西，或者至多是周末偶尔去逛逛的地方。
我的大部分朋友都住在城里，然而他们一提到乡村就手舞足蹈。
statements.english: Most of my friends live in the city, yet they always go into raptures at the mere mention of the country.
Though they extol the virtues of the peaceful life, only one of them has ever gone to live in the country and he was back in town within six months.
statements.chinese: 尽管他们盛赞宁静生活的种种好处，但只有一个人去乡下住过，而且不到6个月就回到了城里。
即使他，至今仍幻想乡村生活不知怎么的要优于城市生活。
statements.english: Even he still lives under the illusion that country life is somehow superior to town life.

statements.chinese: 他总是谈论那里的人们多么友好，空气多么清新，多么贴近大自然，生活节奏多么悠闲。
statements.english: He is forever talking about the friendly people, the clean atmosphere, the closeness to nature and the gentle pace of living.
Nothing can be compared, he maintains, with the first cockcrow, the twittering of birds at dawn, the sight of the rising sun glinting on the trees and pastures.
statements.chinese: 他坚持认为，没有什么能与第一声鸡鸣、黎明时鸟儿的啁啾相比，也不能与旭日普照树林和牧场的景象相比。
这田园诗般的乡村景色只是部分景象。
statements.english: This idyllic pastoral scene is only part of the picture.

statements.chinese: 我的朋友没有提到在电视机前度过的漫长而孤寂的冬夜——这几乎是唯一的娱乐方式。
statements.english: My friend fails to mention the long and friendless winter evenings in front of the TV--virtually the only form of entertainment.
He says nothing about the poor selection of goods in the shops, or about those unfortunate people who have to travel from the country to the city every day to get to work.
statements.chinese: 他没有提及商店里商品的选择少得可怜，也没有提及那些每天不得不从乡下到城里上班的可怜人。
为什么人们愿意每天忍受4个小时的车程，只为享受住在乡下这种可疑的优待，这真是超出我的理解。
statements.english: Why people are prepared to tolerate a four-hour journey each day for the dubious privilege of living in the country is beyond me.

statements.chinese: 如果他们选择住在他们本该居住的城市，就可以避免许多痛苦和花费。
statements.english: They could be saved so much misery and expense if they chose to live in the city where they rightly belong.

statements.chinese: 如果你能放弃乡村那一点点田园乐趣，你就会发现城市能为你提供生活中最美好的东西。
statements.english: If you can do without the few pastoral pleasures of the country, you will find the city can provide you with the best that life can offer.

statements.chinese: 你永远不必跑很远的路去看望朋友。
statements.english: You never have to travel miles to see your friends.

statements.chinese: 他们总是住在附近，随时都可以进行非正式的聊天或晚间娱乐。
statements.english: They invariably live nearby and are always available for an informal chat or an evening's entertainment.

statements.chinese: 我乡下的一些熟人每年进城一两次，看戏作为一种特殊的享受。
statements.english: Some of my acquaintances in the country come up to town once or twice a year to visit the theatre as a special treat.

statements.chinese: 对他们来说，这是一项大工程，需要周密的计划。
statements.english: For them this is a major operation which involves considerable planning.

statements.chinese: 随着戏接近尾声，他们会担心是否能赶上最后一班回家的火车。
statements.english: As the play draws to its close, they wonder whether they will ever catch that last train home.

statements.chinese: 城市居民从不会经历这种焦虑。
statements.english: The city dweller never experiences anxieties of this sort.

statements.chinese: 最新的展览、电影或戏剧，只需坐一小段公交车就能到达。
statements.english: The latest exhibitions, films, or plays are only a short bus ride away.

statements.chinese: 购物也总是一种乐趣。
statements.english: Shopping, too, is always a pleasure.

statements.chinese: 品种如此繁多，你永远不必将就次等货。
statements.english: There is so much variety that you never have to make do with second best.

statements.chinese: 乡下人进城购物时会变得狂热，然后蹒跚着回家，身上背着尽可能多的异国情调的物品。
statements.english: Country people run wild when they go shopping in the city and stagger home loaded with as many of the exotic items as they can carry.

statements.chinese: 城市也并非没有它的美丽时刻。
statements.english: Nor is the city without its moments of beauty.

statements.chinese: 在寒冷潮湿的冬夜，广告牌散发出的温暖光芒总能给人带来慰藉。
statements.english: There is something comforting about the warm glow shed by advertisements on cold wet winter nights.
Few things could be more impressive than the peace that descends on deserted city streets at weekends when the thousands that travel to work every day are tucked away in their homes in the country.
statements.chinese: 几乎没有什么能比周末空旷的城市街道上降临的宁静更令人印象深刻，当每天上班的成千上万人都在乡下的家中安睡时。

statements.english: It has always been a mystery to me why city dwellers, who appreciate all these things, obstinately pretend that they would prefer to live in the country.
statements.chinese: 对我来说，城市居民明明欣赏所有这些优点，却固执地假装他们更喜欢住在乡下，这始终是个谜。

courses.title: Lesson 42: Modern Cavemen
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 30 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 作者把贝杰深洞与什么作比较？
statements.english: With what does the writer compare the Gouffre Berger?

statements.chinese: 洞穴探险，即人们所知的“探洞”，是一项比较新的运动。
statements.english: Cave exploration, or pot-holing, as it has come to be known, is a relatively new sport.

statements.chinese: 也许是出于对孤独的渴望，或是想作一次意想不到的发现，把人们引到地下去的。
statements.english: Perhaps it is the desire for solitude or the chance of making an unexpected discovery that lures people down to the depths of the earth.

statements.chinese: 想对探洞者的动机作出满意的解释是不可能的。
statements.english: It is impossible to give a satisfactory explanation for a pot-holer's motives.

statements.chinese: 对于他来说，洞穴有着与高山对于登山者一样的奇异魅力。
statements.english: For him, caves have the same peculiar fascination which high mountains have for the climber.

statements.chinese: 它们唤起人们只能模模糊糊感知到的本能。
statements.english: They arouse instincts which can only be dimly understood.

statements.chinese: 勘探真正深的洞穴并非是周日下午散步者所能胜任的。
statements.english: Exploring really deep caves is not a task for the Sunday afternoon rambler.

statements.chinese: 这种活动需要像军事行动一样精确的计划和预见性。
statements.english: Such undertakings require the precise planning and foresight of military operations.

statements.chinese: 在下到一个很深的洞穴之前，光是架设绳梯和建立补给站就可能需要长达8天的时间。
statements.english: It can take as long as eight days to rig up rope ladders and to establish supply bases before a descent can be made into a very deep cave.

statements.chinese: 这种预防是必要的，因为无法预知探洞者将会遇到的困难究竟是什么性质。
statements.english: Precautions of this sort are necessary, for it is impossible to foretell the exact nature of the difficulties which will confront the pot-holer.

statements.chinese: 世界上已知最深的洞穴是格勒诺布尔附近的贝杰深洞。
statements.english: The deepest known cave in the world is the Gouffre Berger near Grenoble.

statements.chinese: 它深达3723英尺。
statements.english: It extends to a depth of 3, 723 feet.

statements.chinese: 这个巨大的深渊是由一条地下河形成的，这条河在岩石的裂缝中开凿出一条通道。
statements.english: This immense chasm has been formed by an underground stream which has tunnelled a course through a flaw in the rocks.

statements.chinese: 洞口位于多芬阿尔卑斯山脉的一个高原上。
statements.english: The entrance to the cave is on a plateau in the Dauphine Alps.

statements.chinese: 由于洞口只有6英尺宽，所以几乎难以察觉。
statements.english: As it is only six feet across, it is barely noticeable.

statements.chinese: 如果不是杰出的法国探洞者贝杰发现了洞口，这个洞穴可能永远也不会被发现。
statements.english: The cave might never have been discovered had not the entrance been spotted by the distinguished French pot-holer, Berger.

statements.chinese: 自从被发现以来，它已成为探洞者们的一种“珠穆朗玛峰”。
statements.english: Since its discovery, it has become a sort of pot-holers' Everest.

statements.chinese: 尽管已经进行过多次下降探险，但其中大部分仍有待勘探。
statements.english: Though a number of descents have been made, much of it still remains to be explored.

statements.chinese: 一队探洞者最近下到了贝杰深洞。
statements.english: A team of pot-holers recently went down the Gouffre Berger.
After entering the narrow gap on the plateau, they climbed down the steep sides of the cave until they came to a narrow corridor.
statements.chinese: 他们进入高原上的那个狭窄的缝隙后，沿着洞穴陡峭的侧壁向下攀爬，直到来到一条狭窄的通道。

statements.english: They had to edge their way along this, sometimes wading across shallow streams, or swimming across deep pools.
statements.chinese: 他们不得不侧身沿着这条通道前行，有时涉过浅浅的小溪，有时游过深深的水潭。
突然，他们来到一个瀑布，瀑布落入洞穴底部的一个地下湖中。
statements.english: Suddenly they came to a waterfall which dropped into an underground lake at the bottom of the cave.

statements.chinese: 他们跳入湖中，把装备装到一艘充气橡皮艇上，然后让水流把他们带到对岸。
statements.english: They plunged into the lake, and after loading their gear on an inflatable rubber dinghy, let the current carry them to the other side.

statements.chinese: 为了保护自己不受冰冷湖水的侵袭，他们不得不穿上特制的橡胶衣。
statements.english: To protect themselves from the icy water, they had to wear special rubber suits.

statements.chinese: 在湖的远端，他们遇到了被水冲刷而成的巨大碎石堆。
