statements.english: At the far end of the lake, they came to huge piles of rubble which had been washed up by the water.
In this part of the cave, they could hear an insistent booming sound which they found was caused by a small waterspout shooting down into a pool from the roof of the cave.
statements.chinese: 在洞穴的这部分，他们能听到一种持续不断的轰鸣声，他们发现这是由一股小小的水柱从洞顶射入水潭所引起的。
探洞者们挤过岩石中的一道裂缝，来到一个巨大的洞穴，其大小相当于一个巨大的音乐厅。
statements.english: Squeezing through a cleft in the rocks, the pot-holers arrived at an enormous cavern, the size of a huge concert hall.
After switching on powerful arc lights, they saw great stalagmites--some of them over forty feet high--rising up like tree-trunks to meet the stalactites suspended from the roof.
statements.chinese: 打开强光弧光灯后，他们看到了巨大的石笋——其中一些高达40多英尺——像树干一样向上生长，与悬挂在洞顶的钟乳石相接。
四周，一堆堆的石灰石闪耀着彩虹般的光芒。
statements.english: Round about, piles of limestone glistened in all the colours of the rainbow.

statements.chinese: 在洞穴诡异的寂静中，唯一能听到的声音是头顶高高的拱顶不断滴落的水声。
statements.english: In the eerie silence of the cavern, the only sound that could be heard was made by water which dripped continuously from the high dome above them.

courses.title: Lesson 43: Fully Insured
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 29 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 保险公司通常愿意为任何事物投保。
statements.english: Insurance companies are normally willing to insure anything.

statements.chinese: 为公共或私人财产投保是世界上大多数国家的标准做法。
statements.english: Insuring public or private property is a standard practice in most countries around the world.
If, however, you were holding an open-air garden party or a fate, it would be equally possible to insure yourself in the event of bad weather.
statements.chinese: 然而，如果你正在举办一场露天花园派对或游园会，那么为应对恶劣天气而投保也同样是可能的。

statements.english: Needless to say, the bigger the risk an insurance company takes, the higher the premium you will have to pay.
statements.chinese: 不用说，保险公司承担的风险越大，你需要支付的保费就越高。

statements.english: It is not uncommon to hear that a shipping company has made a claim for the lost ship.
statements.chinese: 经常听说一家航运公司为失事船只提出了索赔。

statements.english: But the claim made by a local authority to recover the cost of salvaging a sunken pie dish must surely be unique.
statements.chinese: 但是，地方当局提出的索赔为了收回打捞一个沉没的馅饼盘的成本肯定是非同寻常的。

statements.english: Admittedly, it was an unusual pie dish, for it was 18 feet long and 6 feet wide.
statements.chinese: 诚然，那是一个不同寻常的馅饼盘，因为它有18英尺长，6英尺宽。

statements.english: It had been purchased by a local authority so that an enormous pie could be baked for an annual fair.
statements.chinese: 它是由当地政府购买的，以便为一个年度展览烤制一个巨大的馅饼。
馅饼委员会决定，运输这个盘子的最佳方式是通过运河。
statements.english: The pie committee decided that the best way to transport the dish would be by canal.

statements.chinese: 于是他们为这次行程投了保。
statements.english: So they insured it for the trip.
Shortly after it was launched, the pie committee went to a local inn to celebrate.
statements.chinese: 启动后不久，馅饼委员会去了一家当地的旅馆庆祝。

statements.english: At the same time, a number of teenagers climbed onto the dish and held a little party of their own.
statements.chinese: 同时，一些青少年爬上了馅饼盘，并举办了一个他们自己的小型派对。

statements.english: Modern dances proved to be more than the dish could bear, for during the party it capsized and sank in seven feet of water.
statements.chinese: 现代舞对馅饼盘来说是难以承受的，因为在派对期间它翻覆了，沉入了七英尺深的水中。

statements.english: The pie committee telephoned a local garage owner who arrived in a recovery truck to salvage the pie dish.
statements.chinese: 馅饼委员会给当地的一位车库老板打了电话，他开着一辆救援卡车赶来打捞这个馅饼盘。

statements.english: Shivering in their wet clothes, the teenagers looked on while three men dived repeatedly into the water to locate the dish.
statements.chinese: 青少年们穿着湿衣服瑟瑟发抖，看着三名男子反复潜入水中寻找馅饼盘。

statements.english: They had little difficulty in finding it, but hauling it out of the water proved to be a serious problem.
statements.chinese: 他们很快就找到了它，但是把它从水里拖出来却是个大问题。

statements.english: The sides of the dish were so smooth that it was almost impossible to attach ropes and chains to the rim without damaging it.
statements.chinese: 馅饼盘的侧面非常光滑，几乎不可能在不损坏它的情况下将绳索和链条固定在边缘。

statements.english: Eventually, chains were fixed to one end of the dish and a powerful winch was put into operation.
statements.chinese: 最终，链条被固定在馅饼盘的一端，一个强力绞车投入了使用。

statements.english: The dish rose to the surface and was gently drawn towards the canal bank.
statements.chinese: 馅饼盘浮出水面，然后被轻轻地拉向运河岸边。

statements.english: For one agonizing moment, the dish was perched precariously on the bank of the canal.
statements.chinese: 在一个令人痛苦的时刻，馅饼盘摇摇晃晃地停在运河岸边。
但它突然失去平衡，滑回了水中。
statements.english: But it suddenly overbalanced and slipped back into the water.

statements.chinese: 这些人现在不得不再次尝试。
statements.english: The men were now obliged to try once more.
This time, they fixed heavy metal clamps to both sides of the dish so that they could fasten the chains.
statements.chinese: 这次，他们将重型金属夹固定在馅饼盘的两侧，这样他们就可以固定链条了。
馅饼盘现在必须垂直吊起，因为一侧正抵着运河的侧壁。
statements.english: The dish now had to be lifted vertically because one edge was resting against the side of the canal.
The winch was again put into operation and one of the men started up the truck.
statements.chinese: 绞车再次投入使用，其中一人启动了卡车。

statements.english: Several minutes later, the dish was successfully hauled above the surface of the water.
statements.chinese: 几分钟后，馅饼盘被成功地吊出水面。

statements.english: Water streamed in torrents over its sides with such force that it set up a huge wave in the canal.
statements.chinese: 水从馅饼盘的两侧倾泻而下，力量之大，以至于在运河中激起了巨大的波浪。

statements.english: There was danger that the wave would rebound off the other side of the bank and send the dish plunging into the water again.
statements.chinese: 危险在于，波浪会从运河的另一边反弹回来，再次将馅饼盘冲入水中。

statements.english: By working at tremendous speed, the men managed to get the dish onto dry land before the wave returned.
statements.chinese: 通过以极快的速度工作，男人们设法在波浪返回之前将馅饼盘弄到了岸上。

courses.title: Lesson 44: Speed and Comfort
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 33 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 远距离旅行的人们常常需要决定是选择陆路、海路还是航空。
statements.english: People traveling long distances frequently have to decide whether they would prefer to go by land, sea, or air.

statements.chinese: 几乎没有人会真正喜欢在火车上坐好几个小时。
statements.english: Hardly anyone can positively enjoy sitting in a train for more than a few hours.

statements.chinese: 火车车厢很快就会变得拥挤和闷热。
statements.english: Train compartments soon get cramped and stuffy.

statements.chinese: 几乎不可能让你的思绪从旅途中抽离。
statements.english: It is almost impossible to take your mind off the journey.
Reading is only a partial solution, for the monotonous rhythm of the wheels clicking on the rails soon lulls you to sleep.
statements.chinese: 阅读只是部分解决方案，因为车轮在铁轨上单调的咔嗒声很快就会让你昏昏欲睡。
白天，睡眠是断断续续的。
statements.english: During the day, sleep comes in snatches.

statements.chinese: 晚上，当你很少想睡觉的时候，你也很少能睡着。
statements.english: At night, when you rarely wish to go to sleep, you rarely manage to do so.
If you are lucky enough to get a couchette, you spend half the night staring at the small blue light in the ceiling, or fumbling to find your passport when you cross a frontier.
statements.chinese: 如果你足够幸运能得到一个卧铺，你会半夜盯着天花板上的小蓝灯，或者在过边境时摸索着找护照。
不可避免地，你会筋疲力尽地到达目的地。
statements.english: Inevitably, you arrive at your destination almost exhausted.
Long car journeys are even less pleasant, for it is quite impossible even to read.
statements.chinese: 长途汽车旅行甚至更不愉快，因为甚至连阅读都是不可能的。
在高速公路上，你至少可以相当安全地高速行驶。
statements.english: On motorways, you can at least travel fairly safely at high speeds.
But more often than not, the greater part of the journey is spent on narrow, bumpy roads, which are crowded with traffic.
statements.chinese: 但通常情况下，旅途的大部分时间是在狭窄颠簸的道路上度过的，这些道路交通拥堵。

statements.english: By comparison, trips by sea offer a great variety of civilized comforts.
statements.chinese: 相比之下，海上旅行提供了各种文明的舒适体验。

statements.english: You can stretch your legs on the spacious decks, play games, swim, meet interesting people, and enjoy good food.
statements.chinese: 你可以在宽敞的甲板上伸展双腿，玩游戏，游泳，结识有趣的人，享受美食。
当然，这一切都基于海面风平浪静的前提。
statements.english: Always assuming, of course, that the sea is calm.
If it is not, and you are likely to get seasick, no form of transport could be worse.
statements.chinese: 如果不是，而且你很可能会晕船，那么没有哪种交通方式会更糟糕了。

statements.english: Even if you travel in ideal weather, sea journeys take a long time.
statements.chinese: 即使你在理想的天气下旅行，海上旅程也需要很长时间。

statements.english: Relatively few people are prepared to sacrifice up to a third of their holidays for the pleasure of traveling on a ship.
statements.chinese: 相对而言，很少有人愿意牺牲三分之一的假期，只为享受在船上旅行的乐趣。

statements.english: Aeroplanes have the reputation of being dangerous, and even hardened travelers are intimidated by them.
statements.chinese: 飞机素来有危险的名声，即使是经验丰富的旅行者也会被它们吓倒。
它们还有一个严重的缺点，就是是最昂贵的交通方式。
statements.english: They also have the grave disadvantage of being the most expensive form of transport.

statements.chinese: 但在速度和舒适度上，没有什么能与它们匹敌。
statements.english: But nothing can match them for speed and comfort.
Traveling at a height of 30,000 feet, far above the clouds, and at over 500 miles an hour, is an exhilarating experience.
statements.chinese: 在三万英尺的高空，远高于云层，以每小时超过五百英里的速度飞行，是一种令人振奋的体验。

statements.english: You do not have to devise ways of taking your mind off the journey, for an aeroplane gets you to your destination rapidly.
statements.chinese: 你不必绞尽脑汁想办法让思绪从旅途中抽离，因为飞机能让你迅速到达目的地。
几个小时里，你舒服地靠在深扶手椅中，享受飞行。
statements.english: For a few hours, you settle back in a deep armchair to enjoy the flight.

statements.chinese: 真正的享乐主义者可以在某些航班上免费观看电影并品尝香槟。
statements.english: The real escapist can watch a free film show and sip champagne on some services.
But even when such refinements are not available, there is plenty to keep you occupied.
statements.chinese: 但即使没有这些精致的服务，也有足够多的事情让你忙碌。
飞机为你提供了独特而令人叹为观止的世界景观。
statements.english: An aeroplane offers you an unusual and breathtaking view of the world.

statements.chinese: 你毫不费力地翱翔于高山和深谷之上。
statements.english: You soar effortlessly over high mountains and deep valleys.

statements.chinese: 你真正看到了大地的形状。
statements.english: You really see the shape of the land.
If the landscape is hidden from view, you can enjoy the extraordinary sight of unbroken cloud-planes that stretch out for miles before you, while the sun shines brilliantly in a clear sky.
statements.chinese: 如果风景被遮挡，你可以欣赏到连绵不绝的云海奇景，它们在你眼前绵延数英里，同时，太阳在晴朗的天空中璀璨生辉。
旅程如此平稳，没有什么能阻止你阅读或睡觉。
statements.english: The journey is so smooth that there is nothing to prevent you from reading or sleeping.
However you decide to spend your time, one thing is certain: You will arrive at your destination fresh and uncrumpled.
statements.chinese: 无论你决定如何度过你的时间，有一件事是肯定的：你将精神焕发、神采奕奕地抵达目的地。
你不必花接下来的几天来从漫长而艰辛的旅途中恢复过来。
statements.english: You will not have to spend the next few days recovering from a long and arduous journey.

courses.title: Lesson 45: The Power of the Press
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 30 条逐句练习

statements.english: In democratic countries, any efforts to restrict the freedom of the press are rightly condemned.
statements.chinese: 在民主国家，任何限制新闻自由的努力都理所当然地受到谴责。
然而，这种自由很容易被滥用。
statements.english: However, this freedom can easily be abused.
Stories about people often attract far more public attention than political events.
statements.chinese: 关于人们的故事常常比政治事件更能吸引公众的注意力。

statements.english: Though we may enjoy reading about the lives of others, it is extremely doubtful whether we would equally enjoy reading about ourselves.
statements.chinese: 尽管我们可能喜欢阅读别人的生活，但我们是否会同样喜欢阅读我们自己的生活，这是非常值得怀疑的。
还来自那些希望宣传自己产品的婴儿食品和肥皂制造商。
statements.english: but from baby food and soap manufacturers who wished to advertise their products.
Acting on the contention that facts are sacred, reporters can cause untold suffering to individuals by publishing details about their private lives.
statements.chinese: 秉持事实神圣不可侵犯的论点，记者们通过公布个人私生活的细节，可能会给他们造成无法言喻的痛苦。

statements.english: Newspapers exert such tremendous influence that they can not only bring about major changes to the lives of ordinary people, but can even overthrow a government.
statements.chinese: 报纸施加着如此巨大的影响，以至于它们不仅能给普通人的生活带来重大改变，甚至可以推翻一个政府。

statements.english: The story of a poor family that acquired fame and fortune overnight dramatically illustrates the power of the press.
statements.chinese: 一个贫困家庭一夜之间获得名望和财富的故事，生动地说明了报刊的力量。

statements.english: The family lived in Aberdeen, a small town of 23,000 inhabitants in South Dakota.
statements.chinese: 这个家庭住在阿伯丁，一个位于南达科他州，拥有2.3万居民的小镇。

statements.english: As the parents had five children, life was a perpetual struggle against poverty.
statements.chinese: 由于这对父母有五个孩子，生活是一场与贫困的无休止的斗争。

statements.english: They were expecting their sixth child, and were faced with even more pressing economic problems.
statements.chinese: 他们正期待着第六个孩子，并面临着更加紧迫的经济问题。

statements.english: If they had had only one more child, the fact would have passed unnoticed.
statements.chinese: 如果他们只多了一个孩子，这件事就会被忽视。

statements.english: They would have continued to struggle against economic odds, and would have lived in obscurity.
statements.chinese: 他们将继续与经济困境作斗争，并默默无闻地生活。

statements.english: But they suddenly became the parents of quintuplets, four girls and a boy, an event which radically changed their lives.
statements.chinese: 但是他们突然成了五胞胎的父母，四个女孩和一个男孩，这一事件彻底改变了他们的生活。

statements.english: The day after the birth of the five children, an aeroplane arrived in Aberdeen, bringing 60 reporters and photographers.
statements.chinese: 五个孩子出生后的第二天，一架飞机抵达阿伯丁，载来了60名记者和摄影师。

statements.english: The news was of national importance, for the poor couple had become the parents of the only quintuplets in America.
statements.chinese: 这个消息具有全国性的重要意义，因为这对贫困夫妇成了美国唯一的五胞胎的父母。
成名之路迅速展开。
statements.english: The rise to fame was swift.
Television cameras and newspapers carried the news to everyone in the country.
statements.chinese: 电视摄像机和报纸将这一消息传遍了全国各地。

statements.english: Newspapers and magazines offered the family huge sums for the exclusive rights to publish stories and photographs.
statements.chinese: 报纸和杂志向这个家庭提供了巨额资金，以获取独家发表新闻和照片的权利。

statements.english: Gifts poured in, not only from unknown people, but from baby food and soap manufacturers who wished to advertise their products.
statements.chinese: 礼物如潮水般涌来，不仅来自不认识的人，还来自那些希望宣传自己产品的婴儿食品和肥皂制造商。

statements.english: The old farmhouse the family lived in was to be replaced by a new $100,000 home.
statements.chinese: 这个家庭居住的旧农舍将被一栋价值10万美元的新房取代。

statements.english: Reporters kept pressing for interviews, so lawyers had to be employed to act as spokesmen for the family at press conferences.
statements.chinese: 记者们不停地要求采访，因此不得不雇佣律师在新闻发布会上担任这个家庭的发言人。
这一事件给小镇本身带来了巨大的变化。
statements.english: The event brought serious changes to the town itself.
Plans were announced to build a huge new highway, as Aberdeen was now likely to attract thousands of tourists.
statements.chinese: 宣布了修建一条大型新高速公路的计划，因为阿伯丁现在很可能会吸引成千上万的游客。

statements.english: Signposts erected on the outskirts of the town directed tourists not to Aberdeen, but to Quint City, USA.
statements.chinese: 竖立在小镇郊区的路标指引游客不是去阿伯丁，而是去美国五胞胎城。

statements.english: The local authorities discussed the possibility of erecting a Quint Museum to satisfy the curiosity of the public and to protect the family from inquisitive tourists.
statements.chinese: 当地政府讨论了建立一个五胞胎博物馆的可能性，以满足公众的好奇心，并保护这个家庭免受好奇游客的打扰。

statements.english: While the five babies were still quietly sleeping in oxygen tents in a hospital nursery, their parents were paying the price for fame.
statements.chinese: 当五个婴儿还在医院育儿室的氧气帐篷里安静地睡觉时，他们的父母正在为名声付出代价。
他们将再也无法过上正常的生活。
statements.english: It would never again be possible for them to lead normal lives.
They had become the victims of commercialization, for their names had acquired a market value.
statements.chinese: 他们成了商业化的受害者，因为他们的名字已经获得了市场价值。

statements.english: The town itself received so much attention that almost every one of the inhabitants was affected to a greater or less degree.
statements.chinese: 这个小镇本身受到了如此多的关注，以至于几乎每个居民都受到了一定程度的影响。

courses.title: Lesson 46: Do It Yourself
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 32 条逐句练习

statements.english: So great is our passion for doing things for ourselves, that we are becoming increasingly less dependent on specialized labor.
statements.chinese: 我们自己动手做事情的热情如此之高，以至于我们越来越不依赖专业劳工。
再没有人能以对某一学科一无所知为由而推诿了。
statements.english: No one can plead ignorance of a subject any longer.

statements.chinese: 因为有无数关于自己动手的出版物。
statements.english: For there are countless do-it-yourself publications.
Armed with the right tools and materials, newlyweds gaily embark on the task of decorating their own homes.
statements.chinese: 备齐了合适的工具和材料，新婚夫妇愉快地着手装饰自己的家园。

statements.english: Men of all ages spend hours of their leisure time, installing their own fireplaces, laying out their own gardens, building garages, and making furniture.
statements.chinese: 各年龄段的男士们都把闲暇时间花在安装自己的壁炉，布置自己的花园，建造车库和制作家具上。

statements.english: Some really keen enthusiasts, go so far as to build their own record players and radio transmitters.
statements.chinese: 有些真正热衷的爱好者，甚至自己动手制作唱机和无线电发射器。

statements.english: Shops cater for the do-it-yourself craze, not only by running special advisory services for novices, but by offering consumers bits and pieces which they can assemble at home.
statements.chinese: 商店迎合这种自己动手的热潮，不仅为新手提供专门的咨询服务，还向消费者提供可以在家组装的零配件。
这种事情为被压抑的创造性精力提供了一个绝佳的宣泄口。
statements.english: Such things provide an excellent outlet for pent-up creative energy.
But unfortunately, not all of us are born handymen.
statements.chinese: 但不幸的是，我们并非所有人生来就是巧匠。
妻子们往往相信她们的丈夫足智多谋，多才多艺。
statements.english: Wives tend to believe that their husbands are infinitely resourceful and versatile.
Even husbands who can hardly drive a nail in straight, are supposed to be born electricians, carpenters, plumbers, and mechanics.
statements.chinese: 即使是那些连钉子都钉不直的丈夫，也被认为是天生的电工、木匠、管道工和机械师。

statements.english: When lights fuse, furniture gets rickety, pipes get clogged, or vacuum cleaners fail to operate, wives automatically assume that their husbands will somehow put things right.
statements.chinese: 当灯泡烧坏了，家具摇摇晃晃了，管道堵塞了，或者吸尘器坏了，妻子们就会理所当然地认为，她们的丈夫总会把事情搞定。

statements.english: The worst thing about the do-it-yourself game, is that sometimes husbands live under the delusion that they can do anything, even when they have been repeatedly proved wrong.
statements.chinese: 自己动手这件事最糟糕的地方在于，有时丈夫们会自欺欺人地认为他们无所不能，即使他们已被屡次证明是错的。
这更多的是一个面子问题。
statements.english: It is a question of pride as much as anything else.
Last spring, my wife suggested that I call in a man to look at our lawn mower.
statements.chinese: 去年春天，我妻子建议我请人来检查一下我们的割草机。

statements.english: It had broken down the previous summer, and though I promised to repair it, I had never got round to it.
statements.chinese: 它在去年夏天就坏了，尽管我答应要修好它，但我一直没动手。

statements.english: I would not hear of the suggestion, and said that I would fix it myself.
statements.chinese: 我根本不听这个建议，说我自己会把它修好。

statements.english: One Saturday afternoon, I hauled the machine into the garden, and had a close look at it.
statements.chinese: 一个星期六下午，我把机器拖到花园里，仔细地检查起来。

statements.english: As far as I could see, it only needed a minor adjustment, a turn of a screw here, a little tightening up there, a drop of oil, and it would be as good as new.
statements.chinese: 就我看来，它只需要稍微调整一下，这里拧一下螺丝，那里紧固一下，再滴几滴油，就会焕然一新。
不出所料，维修工作并不那么简单。
statements.english: Inevitably, the repair job was not quite so simple.

statements.chinese: 割草机就是不肯工作。
statements.english: The mower firmly refused to mow.

statements.chinese: 于是我决定把它拆开。
statements.english: So I decided to dismantle it.

statements.chinese: 花园里很快就散落着一堆堆曾经组成割草机的金属碎片。
statements.english: The garden was soon littered with chunks of metal which had once made up a lawn mower.

statements.chinese: 但我对自己非常满意。
statements.english: But I was extremely pleased with myself.
I had traced the cause of the trouble: one of the links in the chain that drives the wheels had snapped.
statements.chinese: 我找到了故障的原因：驱动轮的链条上有一个链节断了。

statements.english: After buying a new chain, I was faced with the insurmountable task of putting the confusing jigsaw puzzle together again.
statements.chinese: 买了一条新链条后，我面临着一个难以克服的任务：把这个令人困惑的拼图游戏重新组装起来。

statements.english: I was not surprised to find that the machine still refused to work after I had reassembled it, for the simple reason that I was left with several curiously shaped bits of metal, which did not seem to fit anywhere.
statements.chinese: 我重新组装好后，发现机器仍然拒绝工作，这并不奇怪，原因很简单，我剩下了一些形状奇特的金属碎片，它们似乎哪里都安不上。
我绝望地放弃了。
statements.english: I gave up in despair.
The weeks passed, and the grass grew.
statements.chinese: 几周过去了，草长高了。

statements.english: When my wife nagged me to do something about it, I told her that either I would have to buy a new mower, or let the grass grow.
statements.chinese: 当我妻子催促我采取行动时，我告诉她，要么我得买一台新割草机，要么就让草继续长。
不用说，我们的房子现在被一片“丛林”包围着。
statements.english: Needless to say, our house is now surrounded by a jungle.
Buried somewhere in deep grass, there is a rusting lawn mower, which I have promised to repair, one day.
statements.chinese: 埋在深草的某个地方，有一台生锈的割草机，我曾答应总有一天会把它修好。

courses.title: Lesson 47: Too High a Price
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 26 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 作者把什么描述为“一个有趣的、老式的噪音来源”？
statements.english: What does the writer describe as an 'amusing old-fashioned source of noise' ?

statements.chinese: 污染是人口过剩、过度工业化的地球所付出的代价。
statements.english: Pollution is the price we pay for an overpopulated, overindustrialized planet.
When you come to think about it, there are only four ways you can deal with rubbish: dump it, burn it, turn it into something you can use again, attempt to produce less of it.
statements.chinese: 仔细想想，处理垃圾只有四种方法：倾倒、焚烧、回收利用，或者试图减少垃圾产量。
我们一直在尝试这四种方法，但全球垃圾的巨大产量正威胁着要将我们淹没。
statements.english: We keep trying all four methods, but sheer volume of rubbish we produce worldwide threatens to overwhelm us.

statements.chinese: 然而，垃圾只是污染地球问题的一部分。
statements.english: Rubbish, however, is only part of the problem of polluting our planet.

statements.chinese: 生产日益增长的廉价食物的需求导致了另一种污染。
statements.english: The need to produce ever increasing quantities of cheap food leads to a different kind of pollution.

statements.chinese: 工业化农业方法生产廉价肉类产品：牛肉、猪肉和鸡肉。
statements.english: Industriallized farming metheods produce cheap meat products: beef, pork and chicken.

statements.chinese: 杀虫剂和化肥的使用生产廉价谷物和蔬菜。
statements.english: The use of pesticides and fertilizers produces cheap grain and vegetables.
The price we pay for cheap food may be already too high: Mad Cow Disease (BSE) in cattle, salmonella in chicken and eggs, and listeria in dairy products.
statements.chinese: 我们为廉价食物付出的代价可能已经太高了：牛身上的疯牛病（BSE），鸡肉和鸡蛋中的沙门氏菌，以及奶制品中的李斯特菌。

statements.english: And if you think you'll abandon meat and become a vegetarian, you have the choice of very expensive organically-grown vegetables or a steady diet of pesticides every time you think you're eating fresh salads and vegetables, or just having an innocent glass of water!
statements.chinese: 如果你认为你会放弃肉类成为素食者，你可以选择非常昂贵的有机蔬菜，或者每次你以为在吃新鲜沙拉和蔬菜时，都伴随着大量的农药，或者仅仅是喝一杯纯净的水！
然而，还有一种更阴险的污染，它尤其影响城市地区并侵入我们的日常生活，那就是噪音。
statements.english: However, there is an even more insidious kind of pollution that particularly affects urban area and invades our daily lives, and that is noise.

statements.chinese: 昼夜不停响起的防盗警报只会惹恼路人，并实际上帮助窃贼入室盗窃。
statements.english: Burglar alarms going off at any time of the day or night serve only to annoy passers-by and actually assist burglars to burgle.

statements.chinese: 汽车警报在街上不断对我们尖叫，是极度恼人的来源。
statements.english: Car alarms constantly scream at us in the street and are a source of profound irritation.

statements.chinese: 最近一项关于噪音影响的调查显示（令人惊讶的是？）
statements.english: A recent survey of the effects of noise revealed (surprisingly?)

statements.chinese: 狗在夜间不停吠叫被评为1到7级噪音污染中最高的形式。
statements.english: that dogs barking incessantly in the night rated the highest form of noise pollution on a scale ranging from 1 to 7.

statements.chinese: 该调查揭示了许多我们真正不喜欢的噪音来源。
statements.english: The survey revealed a large number of sources of noise that we really dislike.

Lawn mowers whining on a summer's day, late-night parties in apartment blocks, noisy neighbours, vehicles of all kinds, especially large container trucks thundering through quiet villages, planes and helicopters flying overhead, large radios carried round in public places and played at maximum volume.
statements.chinese: 夏日里割草机的嗡嗡声，公寓楼里的深夜派对，吵闹的邻居，各种车辆，特别是大型集装箱卡车轰隆隆地穿过宁静的村庄，飞机和直升机从头顶飞过，公共场所里大声播放的收音机。
新技术也对噪音有所“贡献”。
statements.english: New technology has also made its own contribution to noise.

statements.chinese: 很多人反对手机，尤其是在餐馆或公共交通工具等公共场所使用手机。
statements.english: A lot of people object to mobile phones, especially when they are used in public places like restaurant or on public transport.

statements.chinese: 手机上的大声对话侵扰我们的思绪，或者打断我们与朋友安静聊天的乐趣。
statements.english: Loud conversations on mobile phones invade our thoughts or interrupt the pleasure of meeting friends for a quiet chat.

statements.chinese: 噪音污染调查揭示了一个相当令人惊讶且可能有趣的、老式的噪音来源。
statements.english: The noise pollution survey revealed a rather surprising and possibly amusing old-fashioned source of noise.

statements.chinese: 结果是打鼾！男性被发现是最大的“罪魁祸首”。
statements.english: It turned out to be snoring! Men were found to be the worst offenders.

statements.chinese: 调查显示，20%的三十多岁男性会打鼾。
statements.english: It was revealed that 20% of men in their mid-thirties snore.

statements.chinese: 这个数字在六十多岁男性中飙升至惊人的60%。
statements.english: This figure rises to a staggering 60% of men in their sixties.
Against these figures, it was found that only 5% of women snore regularly, while the rest are constantly woken or kept awake by their trumpeting partners.
statements.chinese: 与这些数字相比，只有5%的女性会规律性打鼾，而其余的女性则不断地被她们打鼾的伴侣吵醒或保持清醒。
无论噪音来源是什么，有一件事是肯定的：宁静，似乎已成为一段美好的回忆。
statements.english: Whatever the source of noise, one thing is certain: silence, it seems, has become a golden memory.

courses.title: Lesson 48: The Silent Village
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 37 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 在这个人们常常出行旅游的世界上，仍然有成千上万个游客无法到达的地方。
statements.english: In this much-traveled world, there are still thousands of places which are inaccessible to tourists.

statements.chinese: 我们总是认为，偏远地区的村民是友善好客的。
statements.english: We always assume that villagers in remote places are friendly and hospitable.
But people who are cut off not only from foreign tourists, but even from their own countrymen, can be hostile to travelers.
statements.chinese: 但是，那些不仅与外国游客隔绝，甚至与本国同胞也隔绝的人，可能对旅行者怀有敌意。
探访那些真正偏远的村庄，很少是愉快的经历。
statements.english: Visits to really remote villages are seldom enjoyable.

statements.chinese: 正如我和妻子在巴尔干地区旅行时所发现的。
statements.english: As my wife and I discovered during a tour through the Balkans.
We had spent several days in a small town, and visited a number of old churches in the vicinity.
statements.chinese: 我们在一个小镇上度过了几天，参观了附近一些古老的教堂。

statements.english: These attracted many visitors, for they were not only of great architectural interest, but contained a large number of beautifully preserved frescoes as well.
statements.chinese: 这些教堂吸引了许多游客，因为它们不仅具有巨大的建筑价值，而且还保存着大量精美的壁画。

statements.english: On the day before our departure, several busloads of tourists descended on the town.
statements.chinese: 在我们出发的前一天，几辆满载游客的巴士抵达了小镇。

statements.english: This was more than we could bear, so we decided to spend our last day exploring the countryside.
statements.chinese: 这超出了我们的承受范围，所以我们决定最后一天去乡下探险。

statements.english: Taking a path which led out of the town, we crossed a few fields, until we came to a dense wood.
statements.chinese: 沿着一条通出小镇的小路，我们穿过了几片田野，直到我们来到一片茂密的树林。
我们以为这条小路会突然中断。
statements.english: We expected the path to end abruptly.

statements.chinese: 但我们发现它蜿蜒穿行于树林之中。
statements.english: But we found that it traced its way through the trees.
We tramped through the wood for over two hours, until we arrived at a deep stream.
statements.chinese: 我们在树林里跋涉了两个多小时，直到我们来到一条很深的溪流边。

statements.english: We could see that the path continued on the other side, but we had no idea how we could get across the stream.
statements.chinese: 我们看到小路在对岸继续延伸，但我们不知道如何才能过河。

statements.english: Suddenly my wife spotted a boat, moored to the bank.
statements.chinese: 突然，我妻子发现了一艘船，停泊在岸边。

statements.english: In it there was a boatman, fast asleep.
statements.chinese: 船上有一个船夫，睡得很香。

statements.english: We gently woke him up, and asked him to ferry us to the other side.
statements.chinese: 我们轻轻地叫醒了他，请他把我们摆渡到对岸。

statements.english: Though he was reluctant to do so at first, we eventually persuaded him to take us.
statements.chinese: 虽然他一开始不情愿，但我们最终说服了他带我们过去。

statements.english: The path led to a tiny village, perched on the steep sides of a mountain.
statements.chinese: 这条小路通向一个很小的村庄，坐落在陡峭的山坡上。

statements.english: The place consisted of a straggling unmade road which was lined on either side by small houses.
statements.chinese: 这个地方由一条蜿蜒崎岖的未铺路组成，两旁是小房子。

statements.english: Even under a clear blue sky, the village looked forbidding, as all the houses were built of gray mud bricks.
statements.chinese: 即使在晴朗的蓝天下，村庄也显得令人生畏，因为所有的房子都是用灰色的泥砖建造的。

statements.english: The village seemed deserted, the only sign of life being an ugly-looking black goat, tied to a tree on a short length of rope in a field nearby.
statements.chinese: 村庄似乎空无一人，唯一的生命迹象是一只看起来很丑的黑山羊，被一根短绳子绑在一棵树上，就在附近的一块田地里。

statements.english: Sitting down on a dilapidated wooden fence near the field, we opened a couple of tins of sardines, and had a picnic lunch.
statements.chinese: 我们坐在田边一处破旧的木栅栏上，打开了两罐沙丁鱼，然后吃了野餐。

statements.english: All at once I noticed that my wife seemed to be filled with alarm.
statements.chinese: 突然，我注意到妻子似乎充满了警觉。

statements.english: Looking up, I saw that we were surrounded by children in rags, who were looking at us silently as we ate.
statements.chinese: 抬头一看，我看到我们被一群衣衫褴褛的孩子包围着，他们在我们吃饭时默默地看着我们。

statements.english: We offered them food, and spoke to them kindly.
statements.chinese: 我们给了他们食物，并亲切地与他们交谈。
但他们仍然一动不动。
statements.english: But they remained motionless.
I concluded that they were simply shy of strangers.
statements.chinese: 我断定他们只是害羞，不愿与陌生人接触。

statements.english: When we later walked down the main street of the village, we were followed by a silent procession of children.
statements.chinese: 当我们后来沿着村子的主街走下去时，一群孩子默默地跟在我们后面。

statements.english: The village, which had seemed deserted, immediately came to life.
statements.chinese: 这个原本看起来空无一人的村庄，立刻变得热闹起来。
窗户里出现了面孔。
statements.english: Faces appeared at windows.
Men in shirt-sleeves stood outside their houses and glared at us.
statements.chinese: 穿着衬衫的男人站在屋外，怒视着我们。

statements.english: Old women in black shawls peered at us from doorways.
statements.chinese: 披着黑色披肩的老妇人从门道里窥视着我们。

statements.english: The most frightening thing of all was that not a sound could be heard.
statements.chinese: 最令人恐惧的是，听不到任何声音。

statements.english: There was no doubt that we were unwelcome visitors.
statements.chinese: 毫无疑问，我们是不受欢迎的客人。
我们不需要更多的警告。
statements.english: We needed no further warning.
Turning back down the main street, we quickened our pace and made our way rapidly towards the stream, where we hoped the boatman was waiting.
statements.chinese: 沿着主街走回去，我们加快了脚步，迅速地向溪流走去，我们希望船夫在那里等着。

courses.title: Lesson 49: The Ideal Servant
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 30 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 幸好我的哈里特姑妈多年前就去世了。
statements.english: It is a good thing my Aunt Harriet died years ago.

statements.chinese: 如果她今天还活着，她就无法就她最喜欢的话题——家佣——发表自己的看法了。
statements.english: If she were alive today, she would not be able to air her views on her favourite topic of conversation, domestic servants.

statements.chinese: 哈里特姑妈生活在那个悠闲的时代，那时佣人是用来做家务的。
statements.english: Aunt Harriet lived in that leisurely age when servants were employed to do housework.

statements.chinese: 她有一座巨大的、错综复杂的乡间别墅，名为“山墙”。
statements.english: She had a huge, rambling country house called The Gables.

statements.chinese: 她对这座房子感情深厚，尽管它对她来说太大了，但她在丈夫去世很久之后仍然坚持住在那里。
statements.english: She was sentimentally attached to this house, for even though it was far too big for her needs, she persisted in living there long after her husband's death.

statements.chinese: 在她变老之前，哈里特姑妈曾经慷慨地款待客人。
statements.english: Before she grew old, Aunt Harriet used to entertain lavishly.

statements.chinese: 我小时候经常去“山墙”拜访。
statements.english: I often visited The Gables when I was a boy.

statements.chinese: 无论有多少客人，这座大房子总是 immaculate (一尘不染)。
statements.english: No matter how many guests were present, the great house was always immaculate.

statements.chinese: 镶木地板光亮如镜。
statements.english: The parquet floors shone like mirrors.

statements.chinese: 高度抛光的银器陈列在闪闪发光的玻璃柜中。
statements.english: Highly polished silver was displayed in gleaming glass cabinets.

statements.chinese: 甚至我叔叔的大量藏书也奇迹般地没有灰尘。
statements.english: Even my uncle's huge collection of books was kept miraculously free from dust.

statements.chinese: 哈里特姑妈统领着一支看不见的佣人队伍，他们不停地擦洗、清洁和抛光。
statements.english: Aunt Harriet presided over an invisible army of servants that continuously scrubbed, cleaned and polished.

statements.chinese: 她总是把他们称为“流动的居民”，因为他们来来去去太频繁了，我甚至没有机会记住他们的名字。
statements.english: She always referred to them as "the shifting population," for they came and went with such frequency that I never even got a chance to learn their names.

statements.chinese: 尽管我的姑妈奉行的是当时开明的政策，即她从不允许她的家政人员每天工作超过八小时，但她却极难取悦。
statements.english: Though my aunt pursued what was in those days an enlightened policy, in that she never allowed her domestic staff to work more than eight hours a day, she was extremely difficult to please.

statements.chinese: 尽管她总是谴责人性的反复无常，但她一生都在不懈地寻找理想的佣人，甚至在被贝西伤透了心之后也是如此。
statements.english: While she always decried the fickleness of human nature, she carried on an unrelenting search for the ideal servant to the end of her days, even after she had been sadly disillusioned by Bessie.

statements.chinese: 贝西为哈里特姑妈工作了三年。
statements.english: Bessie worked for Aunt Harriet for three years.

statements.chinese: 在那段时间里，她赢得了姑妈的信任，以至于被任命为家政主管。
statements.english: During that time, she so gained my aunt's confidence that she was put in charge of the domestic staff.

statements.chinese: 哈里特姑妈对贝西的勤劳和效率赞不绝口。
statements.english: Aunt Harriet could not find words to praise Bessie's industry and efficiency.

statements.chinese: 除了所有其他资质，贝西还是一位烹饪专家。
statements.english: In addition to all her other qualifications, Bessie was an expert cook.

statements.chinese: 她扮演了三年完美佣人的角色，直到哈里特姑妈发现了她“小小的弱点”。
statements.english: She acted the role of the perfect servant for three years before Aunt Harriet discovered her "little weakness."

statements.chinese: 离开“山墙”一周后，我的姑妈在一个下午 неожиданно (出乎意料地) 带着一群客人回来了，并指示贝西准备晚餐。
statements.english: After being absent from The Gables for a week, my aunt unexpectedly returned one afternoon with a party of guests and instructed Bessie to prepare dinner.

statements.chinese: 不仅这顿饭远低于通常的标准，而且贝西似乎也无法稳稳地走路。
statements.english: Not only was the meal well below the usual standard, but Bessie seemed unable to walk steadily.

statements.chinese: 她撞到家具，并不断地嘟囔着关于客人的话。
statements.english: She bumped into the furniture and kept mumbling about the guests.

statements.chinese: 当她端着最后一道菜，一个巨大的布丁进来时，她在地毯上绊倒了，布丁飞向空中，险些砸到我的姑妈，然后带着相当大的力道撞在了餐桌上。
statements.english: When she came in with the last course, a huge pudding, she tripped on the carpet, and the pudding went flying through the air, narrowly missed my aunt, and crashed on the dining table with considerable force.

statements.chinese: 尽管这引起了客人们的极大欢笑，哈里特姑妈却被吓坏了。
statements.english: Though this occasioned great mirth among the guests, Aunt Harriet was horrified.

statements.chinese: 她不情愿地得出结论，贝西喝醉了。
statements.english: She reluctantly came to the conclusion that Bessie was drunk.

statements.chinese: 客人们当然从贝西为他们开门的那一刻起就意识到了这一点，而且早在最后一场灾难发生之前，他们就很难掩饰自己的开心。
statements.english: The guests had, of course, realized this from the moment Bessie opened the door for them, and long before the final catastrophe had had a difficult time trying to conceal their amusement.

statements.chinese: 这个可怜的女孩立刻被解雇了。
statements.english: The poor girl was dismissed instantly.

statements.chinese: 她离开后，哈里特姑妈发现贝西的衣柜里堆满了各种形状和大小的空酒瓶，整齐地堆放着。
statements.english: After her departure, Aunt Harriet discovered that there were piles of empty wine bottles of all shapes and sizes, neatly stacked in what had once been Bessie's wardrobe.

statements.chinese: 它们神秘地从酒窖“找到”了去那里的路。
statements.english: They had mysteriously "found their way there" from the wine cellar.

courses.title: Lesson 50: New Year Resolutions
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 41 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 新的一年是制定決心的時刻。
statements.english: The new year is a time for resolutions.

statements.chinese: 至少在精神上,我們大多數人都可以列出令人望而生畏的該做和不該做的清單。
statements.english: Mentally at least, most of us could compile formidable lists of do's and don'ts.

statements.chinese: 那些老一套的愛好年復一年地重複出現,毫無新意。
statements.english: The same old favorites recur year in, year out with monotonous regularity.

statements.chinese: 我們決心每天早上早起,少吃。
statements.english: We resolve to get up earlier each morning, eat less.

statements.chinese: 找更多的時間陪孩子玩耍。
statements.english: Find more time to play with the children.

statements.chinese: 處理上千件家務事。
statements.english: Do a thousand and one jobs about the house.

statements.chinese: 對不喜歡的人友好。
statements.english: Be nice to people we don't like.

statements.chinese: 小心駕駛。
statements.english: Drive carefully.

statements.chinese: 每天帶狗散步。
statements.english: And take the dog for a walk every day.

statements.chinese: 過去的經驗告訴我們,有些成就根本無法實現。
statements.english: Past experience has taught us that certain accomplishments are beyond attainment.

statements.chinese: 如果我們仍然是老煙槍,那只是因為我們經常經歷失敗帶來的挫敗感。
statements.english: If we remain inveterate smokers, it is only because we have so often experienced the frustration that results from failure.

statements.chinese: 我們大多數人自我完善的努力都失敗了,因為我們的計劃過於雄心勃勃,而且我們從來沒有時間去執行它們。
statements.english: Most of us fail in our efforts at self-improvement, because our schemes are too ambitious and we never have time to carry them out.

statements.chinese: 我們還犯了一個根本性的錯誤,就是向所有人宣布我們的決心。
statements.english: We also make the fundamental error of announcing our resolutions to everybody.

statements.chinese: 這樣當我們故態復萌時,看起來就更傻了。
statements.english: So that we look even more foolish when we slip back into our bad old ways.

statements.chinese: 意識到這些陷阱,今年我試圖將我的決心保密。
statements.english: Aware of these pitfalls, this year I attempted to keep my resolutions to myself.

statements.chinese: 我只給自己定了兩個適度的目標。
statements.english: I limited myself to two modest ambitions.

statements.chinese: 每天早上做體育鍛煉,晚上多讀書。
statements.english: To do physical exercises every morning and to read more of an evening.

statements.chinese: 新年前夜的通宵派對為我提供了一個很好的藉口,讓我在新年的第一天沒有執行這兩個新決心。
statements.english: An all-night party on New Year's Eve provided me with a good excuse for not carrying out either of these new resolutions on the first day of the year.

statements.chinese: 但第二天,我便專心致志地投入到這項任務中。
statements.english: But on the second, I applied myself assiduously to the task.

statements.chinese: 每天的鍛煉只持續了11分鐘。
statements.english: The daily exercises lasted only 11 minutes.

statements.chinese: 我打算在清晨,在所有人起床之前進行。
statements.english: And I proposed to do them early in the morning before anyone had got up.

statements.chinese: 要求我比平時早11分鐘起床的自律是相當可觀的。
statements.english: The self-discipline required to drag myself out of bed 11 minutes earlier than usual was considerable.

statements.chinese: 儘管如此,我還是設法偷偷溜到客廳裡兩天,才被人發現。
statements.english: Nevertheless, I managed to creep down into the living room for two days before anyone found me out.

statements.chinese: 在地毯上跳來跳去,把身體扭成不舒服的姿勢之後,我精疲力盡地坐在早餐桌旁。
statements.english: After jumping about on the carpet and twisting the human frame into uncomfortable positions, I sat down at the breakfast table in an exhausted condition.

statements.chinese: 正是這一點出賣了我。
statements.english: It was this that betrayed me.

statements.chinese: 第二天早上,全家人都走進來觀看表演。
statements.english: The next morning the whole family trooped in to watch the performance.

statements.chinese: 這確實令人不安。
statements.english: That was really unsettling.

statements.chinese: 但我愉快地抵擋住了家人的嘲諷和挖苦,很快每個人都習慣了這個想法。
statements.english: But I fended off the taunts and jibes of the family good-humouredly, and soon everybody got used to the idea.

statements.chinese: 然而,我的熱情逐漸消退。
statements.english: However, my enthusiasm waned.

statements.chinese: 我花在鍛煉上的時間逐漸減少。
statements.english: The time I spent at exercises gradually diminished.

statements.chinese: 漸漸地,那11分鐘變成了零。
statements.english: Little by little, the 11 minutes fell to zero.

statements.chinese: 到1月10日,我又回到了原點。
statements.english: By January the 10th, I was back to where I had started from.

statements.chinese: 我認為,如果我早上花更少的時間在鍛煉上讓自己筋疲力盡,那麼下班回家後我的頭腦就會保持清醒,適合閱讀。
statements.english: I argue that if I spent less time exhausting myself at exercises in the morning, I would keep my mind fresh for reading when I got home from work.

statements.chinese: 抵制住電視的催眠作用,我連續幾個晚上坐在房間裡,眼睛緊盯著一本書。
statements.english: Resisting the hypnotizing effect of television, I sat in my room for a few evenings with my eyes glued to a book.

statements.chinese: 然而,一天晚上,感覺又冷又孤單,我下樓坐在電視機前,假裝看書。
statements.english: One night however, feeling cold and lonely, I went downstairs and sat in front of the television, pretending to read.

statements.chinese: 那成了我的失敗之處。
statements.english: That proved to be my undoing.

statements.chinese: 因為我很快又恢復了在屏幕前打瞌睡的舊習。
statements.english: For I soon got back to my old bad habit of dozing off in front of the screen.

statements.chinese: 我仍然沒有放棄多讀書的決心。
statements.english: I still haven't given up my resolution to do more reading.

statements.chinese: 事實上,我剛買了一本名為《如何每分鐘閱讀一千字》的書。
statements.english: In fact, I have just bought a book entitled, How to read a thousand words a minute.

statements.chinese: 也許它能解決我的問題。
statements.english: Perhaps it will solve my problem.

statements.chinese: 但我就是沒時間讀它。
statements.english: But I just haven't had time to read it.

courses.title: Lesson 51: Predicting the Future
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 23 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 莱昂·巴格里特未能预见到的“未来”电子发展是什么？
statements.english: What was the 'future' electronic development that Leon Bagrit wasn't able to foresee?

statements.chinese: 预测未来是出了名的困难。
statements.english: Predicting the future is notoriously difficult.
Who could have imagined, in the mid 1970s, for example, that by the end of the 20th century, computers would be as common in people's homes as TV sets?
statements.chinese: 举例来说，在20世纪70年代中期，谁能想到，到20世纪末，电脑在人们家中会像电视机一样普及？

statements.english: In the 1970s, computers were common enough, but only in big business, government departments and large organizations.
statements.chinese: 在20世纪70年代，电脑已经很常见了，但只存在于大企业、政府部门和大型机构中。
这些就是所谓的“大型机”。
statements.english: These were the so-called mainframe machines.
Mainframe computers were very large indeed often occupying whole air-conditioned rooms, employing full-time technicians and run on specially-written software.
statements.chinese: 大型机确实非常大，常常占据整个空调房间，雇用全职技术人员，并运行专门编写的软件。

statements.english: Though these large machines still exist, many of their functions have been taken over by small powerful personal computers, commonly known as PCs.
statements.chinese: 尽管这些大型机器仍然存在，但它们的许多功能已被小型、强大的个人电脑（通常称为PC）所取代。
1975年，一台名为Altair的原始机器在美国问世。
statements.english: In 1975, a primitive machine called the Altair, was launched in the USA.

statements.chinese: 它完全可以被称为第一台“家用电脑”，它指明了未来的方向。
statements.english: It can properly be described as the first 'home computer' and it pointed the way to the future.

statements.chinese: 随后，在20世纪70年代末，一台名为Apple的机器问世。
statements.english: This was followed, at the end of the 1970s, by a machine called an Apple.

statements.chinese: 在20世纪80年代初，电脑巨头IBM生产了世界上第一台个人电脑。
statements.english: In the early 1980s, the computer giant, IBM produced the world's first Personal Computer.
This ran on an 'operating system' called DOS, produced by a then small company named Microsoft.
statements.chinese: 它运行在一个名为DOS的“操作系统”上，由当时一家名为微软的小公司开发。
IBM个人电脑被广泛复制。
statements.english: The IBM Personal Computer was widely copied.
From those humble beginnings, we have seen the development of the user-friendly home computers and multimedia machines which are in common use today.
statements.chinese: 从这些不起眼的开端，我们看到了今天普遍使用的用户友好的家用电脑和多媒体机器的发展。

statements.english: Considering how recent these developments are, it is even more remarkable that as long ago as the 1960s, an Englishman, Leon Bagrit, was able to predict some of the uses of computers which we know today.
statements.chinese: 考虑到这些发展是如此之新，更令人称奇的是，早在20世纪60年代，一位名叫莱昂·巴格里特的英国人就能预言我们今天所知道的一些电脑用途。
巴格里特驳斥了电脑会学会“独立思考”并“统治世界”的观点，这在当时是人们喜欢相信的。
statements.english: Bagrit dismissed the idea that computers would learn to 'think' for themselves and would 'rule the world', which people liked to believe in those days.

Bagrit foresaw a time when computers would be small enough to hold in the hand, when they would be capable of providing information about traffic jams and suggesting alterative routes, when they would be used in hospitals to help doctors to diagnose illnesses, when they would relieve office workers and accountants of dull, repetitive clerical work.
statements.chinese: 巴格里特预见到一个时代，那时电脑会小到可以手持，能够提供交通堵塞信息并建议替代路线，在医院里用来帮助医生诊断疾病，解放办公室职员和会计师们枯燥、重复的文书工作。
所有这些电脑用途都已变得司空见惯。
statements.english: All these computer uses have become commonplace.

Of course, Leon Bagrit couldn't possibly have foreseen the development of the Internet, the worldwide system that enables us to communicate instantly with anyone in any part of the world by using computers linked to telephone networks.
statements.chinese: 当然，莱昂·巴格里特不可能预见到互联网的发展，这个全球性的系统使我们能够通过连接到电话网络的电脑与世界任何地方的任何人即时交流。

statements.english: Nor could he have foreseen how we could use the Internet to obtain information on every known subject, so we can read it on a screen in our homes and even print it as well if we want to.
statements.chinese: 他也无法预见到我们如何利用互联网获取所有已知主题的信息，以便我们可以在家中屏幕上阅读，如果需要甚至可以打印出来。
电脑变得越来越小，越来越强大，也越来越便宜。
statements.english: Computers have become smaller and smaller, more and more powerful and cheaper and cheaper.

statements.chinese: 这就是莱昂·巴格里特的预测显得格外引人注目的原因。
statements.english: This is what makes Leon Bagrit's predictions particularly remarkable.

statements.chinese: 如果他，或者像他一样的人，今天还活着，他或许能告诉我们未来五十年会发生什么。
statements.english: If he, or someone like him, were alive today, he might be able to tell us what to expect in the next fifty years.

courses.title: Lesson 52: Mud is Mud
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 30 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 哈里为什么决定放弃他那个小把戏呢？
statements.english: Why did Harry decide to give up his little game?

statements.chinese: 我的表兄哈里在他书房里长期陈列着一个硕大而形状奇特的瓶子。
statements.english: My cousin, Harry, keeps a large curiously-shaped bottle on permanent display in his study.
Despite the fact that the bottle is tinted a delicate shade of green, an observant visitor would soon notice that it is filled with what looks like a thick, greyish substance.
statements.chinese: 尽管瓶子是淡绿色的，细心的来访者很快就会注意到瓶子里盛满了像厚厚的灰白色物质。
如果你问哈里瓶子里装的是什么，他会告诉你里面装的是香泥。
statements.english: If you were to ask Harry what was in the bottle, he would tell you that it contained perfumed mud.

statements.chinese: 如果你表示怀疑或惊奇，他会立刻请你闻一闻，然后让你往皮肤上擦一些。
statements.english: If you expressed doubt or surprise, he would immediately invite you to smell it and then to rub some into your skin.

statements.chinese: 这一短暂的试验会打消你可能有的任何疑虑。
statements.english: The brief experiment would dispel any further doubts she might have.

statements.chinese: 瓶子里确实盛有香泥。
statements.english: The bottle really does contain perfumed mud.

statements.chinese: 哈里是如何得到这种稀奇古怪的东西的，说来话长，他本人也乐于讲述。
statements.english: How Harry came into the possession of this outlandish stuff makes an interesting story which he is fond of relating.

statements.chinese: 此外，得到这个瓶子还纠正了他多年来养成的一个坏习惯。
statements.english: Furthermore, the acquisition of this bottle cured him of a bad habit he had been developing for years.

statements.chinese: 哈里过去认为，到高级化妆品商店去提出一些闻所未闻的要求，寻找一些根本不存在的商品，是一种莫大的乐趣。
statements.english: Harry used to consider it a great joke to go into expensive cosmetic shops and make outrageous requests for goods that do not exist.

statements.chinese: 他会当场编造一些新奇的名称。
statements.english: He would invent fanciful names on the spot.
On entering a shop, he would ask for a new perfume called 'Scented Shadow' or for 'insoluble bath cubes'.
statements.chinese: 一进商店，他会要求买一种叫“香影”的新型香水，或“不溶性浴块”。
如果店员告诉他从未听说过，他便会装出相当不悦的样子。
statements.english: If a shop assistant told him she had not heard of it, he would pretend to be considerably put out.
He loved to be told that one of his imaginary products was temporarily out of stock and he would faithfully promise to call again at some future date, but of course he never did.
statements.chinese: 他喜欢听人说他臆造的商品暂时缺货，他会信誓旦旦地答应改日再来，当然他从来也没有去过。
哈里在做这些表演时是如何能不露出笑容的，我简直无法理解。
statements.english: How Harry managed to keep a straight face during these performances is quite beyond me.

statements.chinese: 哈里无需别人提醒就会讲他是如何买到那珍贵的泥巴瓶的。
statements.english: Harry does not need to be prompted to explain how he bought his precious bottle of mud.

statements.chinese: 有一天，他去了伦敦一家高级商店，要买“美妙来特”。
statements.english: One day, he went to an exclusive shop in London and asked for 'Myrolite'.

statements.chinese: 店员看上去很迷惑，哈里便重复了一遍这个词，并慢慢地重读每个音节。
statements.english: The shop assistant looked puzzled and Harry repeated the word, slowly stressing each syllable.
When the woman shook her head in bewilderment, Harry went on to explain that 'myrolite' was a hard, amber-like substance which could be used to remove freckles.
statements.chinese: 当那个店员困惑地摇了摇头时，哈里接着解释说，“美妙来特”是一种硬的、琥珀状物质，可以用来消除雀斑。
这种解释显然使那个店员明白了一些什么，她便搜寻了一个又一个的货架。
statements.english: This explanation evidently conveyed something to the woman who searched shelf after shelf.

statements.chinese: 她拿出了各种稀奇古怪的混合物，但没有一样符合哈里的要求。
statements.english: She produced all sorts of weird concoctions, but none of them met with Harry's requirements.

statements.chinese: 当哈里装出有点不高兴的样子时，店员答应为他订购一些。
statements.english: When Harry put on his act of being mildly annoyed, the assistant promised to order some for him.

statements.chinese: 哈里成功后有点得意忘形，接着要买香泥。
statements.english: Intoxicated by his success, Harry then asked for perfumed mud.

statements.chinese: 他原以为店员会目瞪口呆地看着他。
statements.english: He expected the assistant to look at him in blank astonishment.
However, it was his turn to be surprised, for the woman's eyes immediately lit up and she fetched several bottles which she placed on the counter for Harry to inspect.
statements.chinese: 然而，这次轮到他吃惊了，因为店员的眼睛立刻亮了起来，拿来了好几瓶放在柜台上让哈里检查。
哈里只好承认这次是自己输了。
statements.english: For once, Harry had to admit defeat.

statements.chinese: 他拿起看似最小的一瓶，悄悄地问了问价格。
statements.english: He picked up what seemed to be the smallest bottle and discreetly asked the price.

statements.chinese: 他庆幸只花了区区20英镑就脱身了，他赶忙溜走，把那瓶宝贝紧紧地夹在胳膊下。
statements.english: He was glad to get away with a mere twenty pounds and he beat a hasty retreat, clutching the precious bottle under his arm.

statements.chinese: 从那以后，哈里认为他发明的这个小把戏可能代价太大。
statements.english: From then on, Harry decided that this little game he had invented might prove to be expensive.

statements.chinese: 现在他书房书柜上陈列的那个奇特的瓶子是他最后一次购买这种稀奇化妆品。
statements.english: The curious bottle which now adorns the bookcase in his study was his first and last purchase of rare cosmetics.

courses.title: Lesson 53: In the Public Interest
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 28 条逐句练习

statements.english: The Scandinavian countries are much admired all over the world for their enlightened social policies.
statements.chinese: 斯堪的纳维亚国家因其开明的社会政策而受到全世界的钦佩。

statements.english: Sweden has evolved an excellent system for protecting the individual citizen from high-handed or incompetent public offices.
statements.chinese: 瑞典已经建立了一个出色的系统，用于保护公民个人免受专横或不称职的公职人员的侵害。

statements.english: The system has worked so well that it has been adopted in other countries like Denmark, Norway, Finland and New Zealand.
statements.chinese: 该系统运作得如此出色，以至于被其他国家采用，如丹麦、挪威、芬兰和新西兰。

statements.english: Even countries with large populations like Britain and the United States are seriously considering imitating the Swedes.
statements.chinese: 即使是英国和美国这样人口众多的国家，也在认真考虑效仿瑞典人。

statements.english: The Swedes were the first to recognize that public officials like civil servants, police officers, health inspectors or tax collectors can make mistakes or act over-zealously in the belief that they are serving the public.
statements.chinese: 瑞典人率先认识到，公职人员，如公务员、警察、卫生检查员或税务员，可能会犯错误，或者行动过于热情，尽管他们相信自己是在为公众服务。

statements.english: As long ago as 1809, the Swedish Parliament introduced a scheme to safeguard the interest of the individual.
statements.chinese: 早在1809年，瑞典议会就引入了一项计划，以维护个人利益。

statements.english: A parliamentary committee, representing all political parties, appoints a person who is suitably qualified to investigate private grievances against the state.
statements.chinese: 一个议会委员会，代表所有政党，任命一名具有适当资格的人，调查针对国家的私人申诉。

statements.english: The official title of the person is Justitieombudsmannen.
statements.chinese: 这个人的正式头衔是司法监察官（Justitieombudsmannen）。
但瑞典人通常称他为JO或监察官。
statements.english: But the Swedes commonly refer to him as the JO or Ombudsman.

statements.chinese: 监察官不受政治压力。
statements.english: The Ombudsman is not subject to political pressure.
He investigates complaints, large and small, that come to him from all levels of society.
statements.chinese: 他调查大大小小的投诉，这些投诉来自社会各个阶层。

statements.english: As complaints must be made in writing, the Ombudsman receives an average of 1,200 letters a year.
statements.chinese: 由于投诉必须以书面形式提出，监察官每年平均收到1200封信。

statements.english: He has eight lawyer assistants to help him, and he examines every single letter in detail.
statements.chinese: 他有八名律师助理协助他，他详细审查每一封信。

statements.english: There is nothing secretive about the Ombudsman's work, for his correspondence is open to public inspection.
statements.chinese: 监察官的工作没有任何秘密可言，因为他的往来信件对公众开放查阅。

statements.english: If a citizen's complaint is justified, the Ombudsman will act on his behalf.
statements.chinese: 如果公民的投诉有道理，监察官将代表他采取行动。

statements.english: The action he takes varies according to the nature of the complaint.
statements.chinese: 他所采取的行动有所不同，取决于投诉的性质。

statements.english: He may gently reprimand an official or even suggest to Parliament that a law be altered.
statements.chinese: 他可能会温和地训斥一名官员，甚至建议议会修改法律。
以下案例是监察官工作的一个典型例子。
statements.english: The following case is a typical example of the Ombudsman's work.
A foreigner living in a Swedish village wrote to the Ombudsman, complaining that he had been ill-treated by the police simply because he was a foreigner.
statements.chinese: 一位居住在瑞典村庄的外国人写信给监察官，抱怨他受到了警察的虐待，仅仅因为他是一个外国人。

statements.english: The Ombudsman immediately wrote to the chief of police in the district, asking him to send a record of the case.
statements.chinese: 监察官立即写信给该地区的警察局长，要求他送交案件记录。

statements.english: There was nothing in the record to show that the foreigner's complaint was justified, and the chief of police stoutly denied the accusation.
statements.chinese: 记录中没有显示该外国人的投诉是正当的，并且警察局长坚决否认了指控。
监察官无法采取行动。
statements.english: It was impossible for the Ombudsman to take action.
But when he received a similar complaint from another foreigner in the same village, he immediately sent one of his lawyers to investigate the matter.
statements.chinese: 但是当他收到一封类似的投诉时，来自同一个村庄的另一名外国人，他立即派他的一名律师去调查此事。
律师查明，确有一名警察曾多次粗暴对待外国人。
statements.english: The lawyer ascertained that a policeman had indeed dealt roughly with foreigners on several occasions.
The fact that the policeman was prejudiced against foreigners could not be recorded in the official files.
statements.chinese: 警察对外国人存有偏见的事实无法在官方文件中记录。

statements.english: It was only possible for the Ombudsman to find this out by sending one of his representatives to check the facts.
statements.chinese: 监察官之所以能够发现这一点，是通过派遣他的一名代表去核实事实。

statements.english: The policeman in question was severely reprimanded and was informed that if any further complaints were lodged against him, he would be prosecuted.
statements.chinese: 这名涉事警察受到了严厉训斥，并被告知，如果再有针对他的投诉，他将受到起诉。

statements.english: The Ombudsman's prompt action at once put an end to an unpleasant practice which might have gone unnoticed.
statements.chinese: 监察官的迅速行动立刻终止了一种不愉快的做法，这种做法可能本会被忽视。

courses.title: Lesson 54: Instinct or Cleverness
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 32 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 我们从小就被教导要害怕昆虫。
statements.english: We have been brought up to fear insects.
We regard them as unnecessary creatures, that do more harm than good.
statements.chinese: 我们认为它们是不必要的生物，弊大于利。
人类不断地与它们作战。
statements.english: Man continually wages war on them.
For they contaminate his food, carry diseases, or devour his crops.
statements.chinese: 因为它们污染食物，传播疾病，或者吞噬他的庄稼。
它们无缘无故地蜇人或咬人。
statements.english: They sting or bite without provocation.
They fly uninvited into our rooms on summer nights, or beat against our lighted windows.
statements.chinese: 它们在夏夜不请自来地飞进我们的房间，或者撞击我们点亮的窗户。

statements.english: We live in dread not only of unpleasant insects, like spiders or wasps, but of quite harmless ones like moths.
statements.chinese: 我们不仅害怕令人不快的昆虫，比如蜘蛛或黄蜂，也害怕那些完全无害的昆虫，比如飞蛾。
阅读关于它们的资料会增加我们的理解，但不会消除我们的恐惧。
statements.english: Reading about them increases our understanding without dispelling our fears.

Knowing that the industrious ant lives in a highly organised society does nothing to prevent us from being filled with revulsion when we find hordes of them crawling over a carefully prepared picnic lunch.
statements.chinese: 知道勤劳的蚂蚁生活在一个高度组织化的社会中，也无法阻止我们感到厌恶，当我们发现成群的蚂蚁爬满精心准备的野餐时。

statements.english: No matter how much we like honey, or how much we have read about the uncanny sense of direction which bees possess, we have a horror of being stung.
statements.chinese: 不管我们多么喜欢蜂蜜，或者我们阅读了多少关于蜜蜂拥有不可思议的方向感，我们仍然害怕被蜇。
我们大多数的恐惧都是不合理的。
statements.english: Most of our fears are unreasonable.

statements.chinese: 但它们是不可能消除的。
statements.english: But they are impossible to erase.
At the same time, however, insects are strangely fascinating.
statements.chinese: 然而，与此同时，昆虫却有着奇特的魅力。

statements.english: We enjoy reading about them, especially when we find that, like the praying mantis, they lead perfectly horrible lives.
statements.chinese: 我们喜欢阅读关于它们的资料，尤其是当我们发现它们，像螳螂一样，过着完全可怕的生活。

statements.english: We enjoy staring at them, entranced as they go about their business, unaware, we hope, of our presence.
statements.chinese: 我们喜欢凝视它们，当它们忙碌时，我们着迷不已，我们希望它们没有察觉，我们的存在。

statements.english: Who has not stood in awe at the sight of a spider pouncing on a fly, or a column of ants triumphantly bearing home an enormous dead beetle.
statements.chinese: 谁没有敬畏地看着一只蜘蛛扑向一只苍蝇，或者一队蚂蚁凯旋地将一只巨大的死甲虫搬回家。

statements.english: Last summer, I spent days in the garden, watching thousands of ants crawling up the trunk of my prize peach tree.
statements.chinese: 去年夏天，我在花园里待了几天，看着成千上万的蚂蚁爬上我那珍贵的桃树树干。
这棵树长在房子避风处的一面暖墙旁边。
statements.english: The tree has grown against a warm wall on a sheltered side of the house.
I am especially proud of it, not only because it has survived several severe winters, but because it occasionally produces luscious peaches.
statements.chinese: 我特别为此自豪，不仅因为它熬过了几个严酷的冬天，还因为它偶尔会结出甜美的桃子。

statements.english: During the summer, I noticed that the leaves of the tree were beginning to wither.
statements.chinese: 夏天的时候，我注意到树叶开始枯萎。

statements.english: Clusters of tiny insects called aphis were to be found on the underside of the leaves.
statements.chinese: 成群的微小昆虫，叫做蚜虫，出现在叶子的背面。

statements.english: They were visited by a large colony of ants, which obtained a sort of honey from them.
statements.chinese: 一大群蚂蚁来拜访它们，从它们那里获取一种蜜露。

statements.english: I immediately embarked on an experiment, which even though it failed to get rid of the ants, kept me fascinated for 24 hours.
statements.chinese: 我立即开始了一个实验，即使它未能摆脱蚂蚁，却让我着迷了24小时。

statements.english: I bound the base of the tree with sticky tape, making it impossible for the ants to reach the aphis.
statements.chinese: 我用胶带缠住了树的底部，使得蚂蚁无法接近蚜虫。

statements.english: The tape was so sticky that they did not dare to cross it.
statements.chinese: 胶带非常粘，它们不敢越过。
很长一段时间，我看着它们困惑地在树底周围奔跑。
statements.english: For a long time, I watched them scurrying around the base of the tree in bewilderment.
I even went out at midnight with a torch, and noted with satisfaction—and surprise—that the ants were still swarming around the sticky tape without being able to do anything about it.
statements.chinese: 我甚至在午夜带着手电筒出去，并满意地——且惊讶地——注意到，蚂蚁们仍然在粘性胶带周围聚集，却无能为力。

statements.english: I got up early next morning, hoping to find that the ants had given up in despair.
statements.chinese: 第二天早上我早早起床，希望发现蚂蚁已经绝望地放弃了。
相反，我看到它们发现了一条新路线。
statements.english: Instead, I saw that they had discovered a new route.
They were climbing up the wall of the house and then onto the leaves of the tree.
statements.chinese: 它们正爬上房子的墙壁，然后爬到树叶上。
我伤心地意识到，我完全被它们的足智多谋打败了。
statements.english: I realised sadly that I had been completely defeated by their ingenuity.

statements.chinese: 蚂蚁很快就找到了我那完全不科学方法的对策。
statements.english: The ants had been quick to find an answer to my thoroughly unscientific methods.

courses.title: Lesson 55: From the Earth Greetings
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 28 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 哪些生命形式最有可能在遥远的行星上发展？
statements.english: Which life forms are most likely to develop on a distant planet?

statements.chinese: 天文学的最新发展使得在我们自己的银河系和其他星系中探测行星成为可能。
statements.english: Recent developments in astronomy have made it possible to detect planets in our own Milky Way and in other galaxies.

statements.chinese: 这是一个重大成就，因为相对而言，行星非常小且不发光。
statements.english: This is a major achievement because, in relative terms, planets are very small and do not emit light.

statements.chinese: 发现行星已经够难了，但在行星上发现生命将是无限困难的。
statements.english: Finding planets is proving hard enough, but finding life on them will prove infinitely more difficult.

statements.chinese: 首先要回答的问题是，一个行星是否真的能够支持生命。
statements.english: The first question to answer is whether a planet can actually support life.

statements.chinese: 例如，在我们自己的太阳系中，金星太热，火星太冷，都无法支持生命。
statements.english: In our own solar system, for example, Venus is far to hot and Mars is far too cold to support life.

statements.chinese: 只有地球提供了理想的条件，即使在这里，植物和动物生命也用了超过40亿年才得以进化。
statements.english: Only the Earth provides ideal conditions, and even here it has taken more than four billion years for plant and animal life to evolve.

statements.chinese: 行星是否能支持生命取决于其恒星，也就是它的“太阳”的大小和亮度。
statements.english: Whether a planet can support life depends on the size and brightness of its star, that is its 'sun'.

statements.chinese: 想象一颗比我们自己的太阳大20倍、亮20倍、热20倍的恒星。
statements.english: Imagine a star up to twenty times larger, brighter and hotter than our own sun.

statements.chinese: 一个行星必须离它非常遥远才能支持生命。
statements.english: A planet would have to be a very long way from it to be capable of supporting life.
Alternatively, if the star were small, the life-supporting planet would have to have a close orbit round it and also provide the perfect conditions for life forms to develop.
statements.chinese: 另一方面，如果恒星很小，支持生命的行星就必须围绕它近距离运行，并且提供生命形式发展的完美条件。
但是我们如何才能找到这样一个行星呢？
statements.english: But how would we find such a planet?

statements.chinese: 目前，还没有任何望远镜能够探测到生命的存在。
statements.english: At present, there is no telescope in existence that is capable of detecting the presence of life.

statements.chinese: 这种望远镜的开发将是21世纪伟大的天文学项目之一。
statements.english: The development of such a telescope will be one of the great astronomical projects of the 21st century.

statements.chinese: 使用基于地球的望远镜来寻找其他行星上的生命是不可能的。
statements.english: It is impossible to look for life on another planet using earth-based telescopes.
Our own warm atmosphere and the heat generated by the telescope would make it impossible to detect objects as small as planets.
statements.chinese: 我们温暖的大气层和望远镜产生的热量将使我们不可能探测到像行星一样小的物体。

statements.english: Even a telescope in orbit round the earth, like the very successful Hubble telescope, would not be suitable because of the dust particles in our solar system.
statements.chinese: 即使是像非常成功的哈勃望远镜那样围绕地球轨道运行的望远镜，也不会适用，因为我们太阳系中有尘埃颗粒。

statements.english: A telescope would have to be as far away as the planet Jupiter to look for life in outer space, because the dust becomes thinner the further we travel towards the outer edges of our own solar system.
statements.chinese: 望远镜必须远达木星才能在外太空寻找生命，因为我们越往太阳系外围移动，尘埃就越稀薄。

statements.english: Once we detected a planet, we would have to find a way of blotting out the light from its star, so that we would be able to 'see' the planet properly and analyse its atmosphere.
statements.chinese: 一旦我们探测到一颗行星，我们就必须找到一种方法来遮挡其恒星的光线，这样我们才能清楚地“看清”这颗行星并分析其大气层。
首先，我们将寻找植物生命，而不是“小绿人”。
statements.english: In the first instance, we would be looking for plant life, rather than 'little green men'.

statements.chinese: 最有可能在行星上发展的生命形式将是细菌。
statements.english: The life forms most likely to develop on a planet would be bacteria.

statements.chinese: 是细菌产生了我们地球上呼吸的氧气。
statements.english: It is bacteria that have generated the oxygen we breathe on earth.

statements.chinese: 在地球的大部分历史中，它们一直是地球上唯一的生命形式。
statements.english: For most of the earth's history they have been the only form of life on our planet.

statements.chinese: 作为地球居民，我们总是怀着这样的希望：我们会受到小绿人的拜访，并能与他们交流。
statements.english: As Earth-dwellers, we always cherish the hope that we will be visited by little green men and that we will be able to communicate with them.

statements.chinese: 但这种希望始终停留在科幻小说的范畴。
statements.english: But this hope is always in the realms of science fiction.

statements.chinese: 如果我们能在另一个行星上发现像细菌这样低级的生命形式，它将彻底改变我们对自身的看法。
statements.english: If we were able to discover lowly forms of life like bacteria on another planet, it would completely change our view of ourselves.

statements.chinese: 正如美国宇航局的丹尼尔·戈尔丁所观察到的，“在别处发现生命将改变一切。
statements.english: As Daniel Goldin of NASA observed, 'Finding life elsewhere would change everything.

statements.chinese: 任何人类的努力或思想都不会因此而保持不变。”
statements.english: No human endeavour or thought would be unchanged by it.'

courses.title: Lesson 56: Our Neighbour, the River
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 24 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 邻居们为什么离开了他们的农场？
statements.english: Why had the neighbours left their farm?

statements.chinese: 构成了我们农场东部边界的河流，在我们的生活中一直扮演着重要的角色。
statements.english: The river which forms the eastern boundary of our farm has always played an important part in our lives.

statements.chinese: 没有它，我们就无法谋生。
statements.english: Without it we could not make a living.

statements.chinese: 泉水仅够供应房屋使用，所以农场用水必须从河里抽。
statements.english: There is only enough spring water to supply the needs of the house so we have to pump from the river for farm use.

statements.chinese: 我们向河流倾诉我们所有的秘密。
statements.english: We tell the river all our secrets.
We know instinctively, just as beekeepers with their bees, that misfortune might overtake us if the important events of our lives were not related to it.
statements.chinese: 我们本能地知道，就像养蜂人对他们的蜜蜂一样，如果我们生活中的重要事件不与河流相关，不幸可能会降临到我们身上。
夏天我们会在河边举行特别的生日派对。
statements.english: We have special river birthday parties in the summer.

Sometimes we go upstream to a favourite backwater, sometimes we have our party at the boathouse, which a predecessor of ours at the farm built in the meadow hard by the deepest pool for swimming and diving.
statements.chinese: 有时我们逆流而上到我们最喜欢的一个回水湾，有时我们会在船屋举行派对，那是我们在农场的前任在草地边上，紧邻最深的游泳和跳水池建造的。
在热浪来袭时，我们选择举行午夜生日派对，那是所有派对中最令人兴奋的。
statements.english: In a heat wave we choose a midnight birthday party and that is the most exciting of all.

We welcome the seasons by the riverside, crowning the youngest girl with flowers in the spring, holding a summer festival on Midsummer Eve, giving thanks for the harvest in the autumn, and throwing a holly wreath into the current in the winter.
statements.chinese: 我们在河边迎接季节，春天给最小的女孩戴上花冠，在仲夏夜举行夏季节庆，秋天感谢丰收，冬天则将冬青花环抛入水流中。
经过长时间的降雨，河流可能会泛滥。
statements.english: After a long period of rain the river may overflow its banks.

statements.chinese: 这很少发生，因为我们这里的气候很少出现极端情况。
statements.english: This is a rare occurrence as our climate seldom goes to extremes.

We are lucky in that only the lower fields, which make up a very small proportion of our farm, are affected by flooding, but other farms are less favourably sited, and flooding can sometimes spell disaster for their owners.
statements.chinese: 我们很幸运，只有较低的田地，这只占我们农场很小的一部分，会受到洪水的影响，但其他农场的位置不太好，洪水有时会给他们的主人带来灾难。
一个糟糕的冬天，我们看着河水悄悄漫上了低洼的草地。
statements.english: One bad winter we watched the river creep up the lower meadows.

statements.chinese: 所有的牛都已移入畜栏，我们几乎没什么损失。
statements.english: All the cattle had been moved into stalls and we stood to lose little.

statements.chinese: 然而，我们担心我们最近的邻居，他们的农场地势低洼，而且他们是这个地区的新来者。
statements.english: We were, however, worried about our nearest neighbours, whose farm was low lying and who were newcomers to the district.

statements.chinese: 由于洪水导致电话失灵，我们无法了解他们的情况。
statements.english: As the floods had put the telephone out of order, we could not find out how they were managing.
From an attic window we could get a sweeping view of the river where their land joined ours, and at the most critical juncture we took turns in watching that point.
statements.chinese: 从阁楼窗户，我们可以俯瞰河流，看到他们的土地与我们农场相接之处，在最关键的时刻，我们轮流守望那个地方。
灾难的第一个迹象是一只死羊顺流而下。
statements.english: The first sign of disaster was a dead sheep floating down.
Next came a horse, swimming bravely, but we were afraid that the strength of the current would prevent its landing anywhere before it became exhausted.
statements.chinese: 接着来了一匹马，勇敢地游着，但我们担心水流太急，它在筋疲力尽之前无法靠岸。
突然，一个木筏出现了，看起来很像诺亚方舟，上面载着全家人、几只母鸡、狗、猫和一只笼子里的鸟。
statements.english: Suddenly a raft appeared, looking rather like Noah's ark, carrying the whole family, a few hens, the dogs, a cat, and a bird in a cage.
We realized that they must have become unduly frightened by the rising flood, for their house, which had sound foundations, would have stood stoutly even if it had been almost submerged.
statements.chinese: 我们意识到他们一定是过度被上涨的洪水吓到了，因为他们的房子地基牢固，即使几乎被淹没，也能坚固地屹立不倒。

statements.english: The men of our family waded down through our flooded meadows with boat hooks, in the hope of being able to grapple a corner of the raft and pull it out of the current towrds our bank.
statements.chinese: 我们家的男人们带着船钩，趟过被淹没的草地，希望能钩住木筏的一角，把它从水流中拉到我们这边的岸边。
我们仍然认为他们能做到这一点是个奇迹。
statements.english: We still think it a miracle that they were able to do so.

courses.title: Lesson 57: Back in the Old Country
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 33 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 叙述者找到他母亲的坟墓了吗？
statements.english: Did the narrater find his mother's grave?

statements.chinese: 我停车让车冷却下来，并研究地图。
statements.english: I stopped to let the car cool off and to study the map.

statements.chinese: 我本以为现在应该离目的地很近了，但周围的一切对我来说仍然很陌生。
statements.english: I had expected to be near my objective by now, but everything still seemed alien to me.

statements.chinese: 我父亲带我出国时我才五岁，那已经是十八年前的事了。
statements.english: I was only five when my father had taken me abroad, and that was eighteen years ago.

statements.chinese: 母亲在一场悲惨的事故中去世后，他未能很快从震惊和孤独中恢复过来。
statements.english: When my mother had died after a tragic accident, he did not quickly recover from the shock and loneliness.

statements.chinese: 他周围的一切都充满了她的气息，不断地撕开他的伤口。
statements.english: Everything around him was full of her presence, continually reopening the wound.

statements.chinese: 所以他决定移民。
statements.english: So he decided to emigrate.

statements.chinese: 在新的国家，他全心投入为我们俩创造新生活，于是他渐渐停止了悲伤。
statements.english: In the new country he became absorbed in making a new life for the two of us, so that he gradually ceased to grieve.

statements.chinese: 他没有再婚，我是在没有女性关爱的情况下长大的；但我什么都不缺，因为他既是我的父亲也是我的母亲。
statements.english: He did not marry again and I was brought up without a woman's care; but I lacked for nothing, for he was both father and mother to me.

statements.chinese: 他一直打算有一天回去，但不是为了留下。
statements.english: He always meant to go back one day, but not to stay.

statements.chinese: 他和我的根基都已在新土地上扎得太深了。
statements.english: His roots and mine had become too firmly embedded in the new land.

statements.chinese: 但他想再见见老乡们，并去我母亲的坟墓看看。
statements.english: But he wanted to see the old folk again and to visit my mother's grave.

statements.chinese: 在我们计划动身前的几个月，他得了绝症，当他知道自己快要去世时，他让我答应独自前往。
statements.english: He became mortally ill a few months before we had planned to go and, when he knew that he was dying, he made me promise to go on my own.
I hired a car the day after landing and bought a comprehensive book of maps, which I found most helpful on the cross-country journey, but which I did not think I should need on the last stage.
statements.chinese: 降落的第二天，我租了一辆车，买了一本详尽的地图册，我发现这本地图册在跨国旅途中非常有用，但我不认为在最后一段路程中我还需要它。
并不是我真的记得任何东西。
statements.english: It was not that I actually remembered anything at all.
But my father had described over and over again what we should see at every milestone after leaving the nearest town, so that I was positive I should recognize it as familiar territory.
statements.chinese: 但父亲曾一遍又一遍地描述，离开最近的城镇后，每过一个里程碑我们会看到什么，所以我确信我会认出那是熟悉的土地。
嗯，我错了，因为我现在迷路了。
statements.english: Well, I had been wrong, for I was now lost.

statements.chinese: 我看了看地图，然后看了看里程表。
statements.english: I looked at the map and then at the milometer.

I had come ten miles since leaving the town and at this point, according to my father, I should be looking at farms and cottages in a valley, with the spire of the church of our village showing in the far distance.
statements.chinese: 我离开城镇已经走了十英里，按照我父亲的说法，在这个地方，我应该能看到山谷里的农场和小屋，远处还能看到我们村教堂的尖顶。
我看不到山谷，看不到农场，看不到小屋，也看不到教堂尖顶——只有一片湖。
statements.english: I could see no valley, no farms, no cottages and no church spire-only a lake.

statements.chinese: 我断定我一定是在某个地方拐错了弯。
statements.english: I decided that I must have taken a wrong turning somewhere.

statements.chinese: 于是我开车回到城镇，开始按原路返回，并不时地看一眼地图。
statements.english: So I drove back to the town and began to retrace the route, taking frequent glances at the map.

statements.chinese: 我最终还是回到了同一个路口。
statements.english: I landed up at the same corner.

statements.chinese: 奇怪的是，地图上并没有标示这片湖。
statements.english: The curious thing was that the lake was not marked on the map.

statements.chinese: 我感觉自己好像偶然闯入了一个噩梦般的国度，就像你在梦中有时会遇到的那样。
statements.english: I felt as if I had stumbled into a nightmare country, as you sometimes do in dreams.

statements.chinese: 就像在噩梦中一样，四周没有人能帮助我。
statements.english: And, as in a nightmare, there was nobody in sight to help me.
Fortunately for me, as I was wondering what to do next, there appeared on the horizon a man on horseback, riding in my direction.
statements.chinese: 幸运的是，正当我不知下一步该怎么办的时候，地平线上出现了一位骑马的人，正朝我这个方向骑来。
我等到他走近，然后问他去我们那个老村子的路。
statements.english: I waited till he came near, then I asked him the way to our old village.

statements.chinese: 他说现在已经没有那个村子了。
statements.english: He said that there was now no village.

statements.chinese: 我以为他一定是误解了我的意思，所以我又重复了一遍村子的名字。
statements.english: I thought he must have misunderstood me, so I repeated its name.

statements.chinese: 这次他指向了湖面。
statements.english: This time he pointed to the lake.

statements.chinese: 那个村子已经不复存在了，因为它连同整个山谷都被淹没了。
statements.english: The village no longer existed because it had been submerged, and all the valley too.

statements.chinese: 那片湖不是天然形成的，而是一个人工水库。
statements.english: The lake was not a natural one, but a man-made reservoir.

courses.title: Lesson 58: A Spot of Bother
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 21 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 老太太回家后发现了什么？
statements.english: What did the old lady find when she got home?

statements.chinese: 老太太很高兴回到她住的公寓楼。
statements.english: The old lady was glad to be back at the block of flats where she lived.

statements.chinese: 购物让她感到疲惫，回家的每一步都让她手里的篮子变得更沉。
statements.english: Her shopping had tired her and her basket had grown heavier with every step of the way home.
In the lift her thoughts were on lunch and a good rest; but when she got out at her own floor, both were forgotten in her sudden discovery that her front door was open.
statements.chinese: 在电梯里，她想着午餐和好好休息；但当她走出电梯到达自己的楼层时，她突然发现前门开着，午餐和休息都被抛到了脑后。

statements.english: She was thinking that she must reprimand her home help the next morning for such a monstrous piece of negligence, when she remembered that she had gone shopping after the home help had left and she knew that she had turned both keys in their locks.
statements.chinese: 她心想，明天早上一定要训斥她的家政人员，因为她如此严重的疏忽，但她随即想起，家政人员离开后她才去购物，而且她确定自己把两把钥匙都锁好了。

statements.english: She walked slowly into the hall and at once noticed that all the room doors were open, yet following her regular practice she had shut them before going out.
statements.chinese: 她慢慢地走进门厅，立刻注意到所有的房门都开着，然而按照她的习惯，出门前她都会关好门。
往客厅里一看，她看到写字台附近一片混乱。
statements.english: Looking into the drawing room, she saw a scene of confusion over by her writing desk.

statements.chinese: 这时，她才明白，在她外出期间，窃贼破门而入了，这简直是明摆着的事。
statements.english: It was as clear as daylight then that burglars had forced an entry during her absence.

Her first impulse was to go round all the rooms looking for the thieves, but then she decided that at her age it might be more prudent to have someone with her, so she went to fetch the porter from his basement.
statements.chinese: 她最初的冲动是把所有房间都找一遍，看看有没有小偷，但后来她觉得，以她的年纪，找个人陪着会更稳妥，于是她下楼去地下室找看门人。
这时她的双腿开始颤抖，于是她坐下来，喝了一杯很浓的茶，看门人则打电话报了警。
statements.english: By this time her legs were beginning to tremble, so she sat down and accepted a cup of very strong tea, while he telephoned the police.

statements.chinese: 恢复镇定后，她在看门人的协助下准备出发，搜寻可能仍藏在她公寓里的不速之客。
statements.english: Then, her composure regained, she was ready to set off with the porter's assistance to search for any intruders who might still be lurking in her flat.
They went through the rooms, being careful to touch nothing, as they did not want to hinder the police in their search for fingerprints.
statements.chinese: 他们检查了各个房间，小心翼翼地不碰任何东西，因为他们不想妨碍警方寻找指纹。
现场一片狼藉，简直难以置信。
statements.english: The chaos was inconceivable.
She had lived in the flat for thirty years and was a veritable magpie at hoarding: and it seemed as though everything she possessed had been tossed out and turned over and over.
statements.chinese: 她在这间公寓住了三十年，是个名副其实的“喜鹊”，喜欢囤积物品：似乎她所有的东西都被翻了出来，翻了个底朝天。
至少，现在整理那些她几年前就该扔掉的东西变得容易多了。
statements.english: At least sorting out the things she should have discarded years ago was now being made easier for her.

statements.chinese: 随后，一名警督带着一名警员赶到，她向他们讲述了她发现公寓被洗劫一空的情况。
statements.english: Then a police inspector arrived with a constable and she told them of her discovery of the ransacked flat.

The inspector began to look for fingerprints, while the constable checked that the front door locks had not been forced, thereby proving that the burglars had either used skeleton keys or entered over the balcony.
statements.chinese: 警督开始寻找指纹，而警员则检查前门锁是否没有被撬，这证明窃贼要么使用了万能钥匙，要么是从阳台进入的。
没有指纹痕迹，但警督发现了一个脏兮兮的红色包裹，里面装着珠宝，老太太说那不是她的。
statements.english: There was no trace of fingerprints, but the inspector found a dirty red bundle that contained jewellery which the old lady said was not hers.

statements.chinese: 所以他们闯入这间公寓显然不是窃贼当天做的第一起案子，而且他们一定是在作案时受到了惊扰。
statements.english: So their entry into this flat was apparently not the burglars' first job that day and they must have been disturbed.
The inspector then asked the old lady to try to check what was missing by the next day, and advised her not to stay alone in the flat for a few nights.
statements.chinese: 警督随后要求老太太在第二天之前尽量清点一下丢失的物品，并建议她几晚不要独自待在公寓里。

statements.english: The old lady thought he was a fussy creature, but since the porter agreed with him, she rang up her daughter and asked for her help in what she described as a little spot of bother.
statements.chinese: 老太太觉得他是个爱挑剔的人，但看门人也同意他的看法，于是她打电话给女儿，请她帮忙解决她所说的“一点小麻烦”。

courses.title: Lesson 59: Collecting
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 25 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 一个人成为一名真正的收藏家后，他或她究竟获得了什么？
