statements.english: What in particular does a person gain when he or she becomes a serious collector?

statements.chinese: 人们倾向于积累财产，有时甚至没有意识到自己在这样做。
statements.english: People tend to amass possessions, sometimes without being aware of doing so.

statements.chinese: 事实上，当他们发现一些自己并不知道拥有的有用物品时，他们会感到惊喜。
statements.english: Indeed they can have a delightful surprise when they find something useful which they did not know they owned.

statements.chinese: 那些从不搬家的人成了不加选择的收藏者，而他们的收藏只能被称为杂物。
statements.english: Those who never have to move house become indiscriminate collectors of what can only be described as clutter.

statements.chinese: 他们把不用的东西放在抽屉、碗柜和阁楼上好多年，相信总有一天会用上这些东西。
statements.english: They leave unwanted objects in drawers, cupboards and attics for years, in the belief that they may one day need just those very things.
As they grow old, people also accumulate belongings for two other reasons, lack of physical and mental energy, both of which are essential in turning out and throwing away, and sentiment.
statements.chinese: 随着年龄的增长，人们还因为另外两个原因而积累物品：缺少清理和扔掉东西所必需的体力和精力，以及情感因素。

statements.english: Things owned for a long time are full of associations with the past, perhaps with relatives who are dead, and so they gradually acquire a value beyond their true worth.
statements.chinese: 拥有了很久的东西，充满了与过去的联系，也许与已故的亲人有关，因此它们逐渐获得超出其真实价值的价值。
有些东西是人们为了避免浪费而特意在家中收藏的。
statements.english: Some things are collected deliberately in the home in an attempt to avoid waste.
Among these I would list string and brown paper, kept by thrifty people when a parcel has been opened, to save buying these two requisites.
statements.chinese: 在这些东西中，我会列举麻线和牛皮纸，节俭的人在包裹拆开后会把它们留下，以节省购买这两种必需品的钱。
收集小物品很容易变成一种癖好。
statements.english: Collecting small items can easily become a mania.

statements.chinese: 我认识一个人，她总是从报纸上剪下她有钱就想买的服装款式图。
statements.english: I know someone who always cuts sketches out from newspapers of model clothes that she would like to buy if she had the money.
As she is not rich, the chances that she will ever be able to afford such purchases are remote; but she is never sufficiently strongminded to be able to stop the practice.
statements.chinese: 由于她不富裕，她将来能买得起这些东西的可能性很小；但她从没有足够的毅力来停止这种做法。
这是一种无害的习惯，但它把她的书桌弄得一团糟，以至于她每次打开书桌，散乱的纸片都会四处掉落。
statements.english: It is a harmless habit, but it litters up her desk to such an extent that every time she opens it, loose bits of paper fall out in every direction.

statements.chinese: 作为一种严肃的爱好，收藏就完全不同了，它有很多优点。
statements.english: Collecting as a serious hobby is quite different and has many advantages.

statements.chinese: 它为闲暇时间提供了放松，因为仅仅看着自己的珍藏就是一种乐趣。
statements.english: It provides relaxation for leisure hours, as just looking at one's treasures is always a joy.

statements.chinese: 人不必外出寻找乐趣，因为藏品就放在家里。
statements.english: One does not have to go outside for amusement, since the collection is housed at home.

Whatever it consists of, stamps, records, first editions of books, china, glass, antique furniture, pictures, model cars, stuffed birds, toy animals, there is always something to do in connection with it, from finding the right place for the latest addition, to verifying facts in reference books.
statements.chinese: 无论是邮票、唱片、书籍初版、瓷器、玻璃制品、古董家具、画作、模型汽车、填充鸟类、玩具动物，总有与它相关的事情可做，从为最新藏品找到合适的位置，到在参考书中核实事实。
这种爱好不仅能让人们在所选的领域受到教育，还能在与此相关的一般事务上学到知识。
statements.english: This hobby educates one not only in the chosen subject, but also in general matters which have some bearing on it.

statements.chinese: 还有其他好处。
statements.english: There are also other benefits.

statements.chinese: 人们会想结识志同道合的收藏家，以获取建议、交流心得、交换物品、炫耀最新的发现。
statements.english: One wants to meet like-minded collectors, to get advice, to compare notes, to exchange articles, to show off the latest find.

statements.chinese: 这样一来，朋友圈子就扩大了。
statements.english: So one's circle of friends grows.
Soon the hobby leads to travel, perhaps to a meeting in another town, possibly a trip abroad in search of a rare specimen, for collectors are not confined to any one country.
statements.chinese: 很快，这项爱好就会带来旅行，也许是去另一个城市参加会议，也可能是出国旅行寻找稀有标本，因为收藏家并不局限于某个国家。

statements.english: Over the years, one may well become an authority on one's hobby and will very probably be asked to give informal talks to little gatherings and then, if successful, to larger audiences.
statements.chinese: 多年以后，人们很可能成为自己爱好领域的权威人士，并且很可能会被邀请在小型聚会上做非正式的演讲，然后，如果成功，还会面向更多的听众。
这样，自信心就会增长，首先是掌握了一门学科，然后是能够谈论它。
statements.english: In this way self-confidence grows, first from mastering a subject, then from being able to talk about it.

statements.chinese: 收藏，通过如此建设性地占据了业余时间，使人感到满足，没有时间感到无聊。
statements.english: Collecting, by occupying spare time so constructively, makes a person contented, with no time for boredom.

courses.title: Lesson 60: Too Early and Too Late
courses.description: 新概念英语第三册 · 31 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 小女孩为什么错过了火车？
statements.english: Why did the young girl miss the train?

statements.chinese: 在文明社会中，准时是处理一切公共事务的必要习惯。
statements.english: Punctuality is a necessary habit in all public affairs in civilized society.

statements.chinese: 没有它，任何事情都无法成功；一切都将处于混乱之中。
statements.english: Without it, nothing could ever be brought to a conclusion; everything would be in a state of chaos.

statements.chinese: 只有在人口稀少的乡村社区，才有可能忽视它。
statements.english: Only in a sparsely-populated rural community is it possible to disregard it.

statements.chinese: 在日常生活中，对不准时可以有一些宽容。
statements.english: In ordinary living, there can be some tolerance of unpunctuality.

statements.chinese: 正在研究某个深奥问题的知识分子，会把手头的一切事物都协调组织好。
statements.english: The intellectual, who is working on some abstruse problem, has everything coordinated and organized for the matter in hand.

statements.chinese: 因此，如果他赴晚宴迟到了，是可以被原谅的。
statements.english: He is therefore forgiven if late for a dinner party.

statements.chinese: 但人们常常因为不准时而受到指责，尽管他们唯一的过错只是把时间安排得太紧凑。
statements.english: But people are often reproached for unpunctuality when their only fault is cutting things fine.
It is hard for energetic, quick-minded people to waste time, so they are often tempted to finish a job before setting out to keep an appointment.
statements.chinese: 对于精力充沛、头脑敏捷的人来说，浪费时间是很难的，所以他们常常想在赴约之前完成一项工作。
如果路上没有发生意外，比如爆胎、交通改道、突如其来的大雾，他们就会准时到达。
statements.english: If no accidents occur on the way, like punctured tyres, diversions of traffic, sudden descent of fog, they will be on time.

statements.chinese: 他们往往比那些从不迟到的人更勤劳、更有用。
statements.english: They are often more industrious, useful citizens than those who are never late.

statements.chinese: 过分准时的人和不准时的人一样，都会给别人带来麻烦。
statements.english: The over-punctual can be as much a trial to others as the unpunctual.

statements.chinese: 提前半小时到达的客人是最让人讨厌的。
statements.english: The guest who arrives half an hour too soon is the greatest nuisance.

statements.chinese: 我家里有些朋友就有这种令人恼火的习惯。
statements.english: Some friends of my family had this irritating habit.

statements.chinese: 唯一的办法就是请他们比其他客人晚半小时来。
statements.english: The only thing to do was ask them to come half an hour later than the other guests.

statements.chinese: 这样他们就能在我们想要的时候到达。
statements.english: Then they arrived just when we wanted them.

statements.chinese: 如果你要赶火车，最好是提前充足时间，而不是哪怕晚一分钟。
statements.english: If you are catching a train, it is always better to be comfortably early than even a fraction of a minute too late.

Although being early may mean wasting a little time, this will be less than if you miss the train and have to wait an hour or more for the next one; and you avoid the frustration of arriving at the very moment when the train is drawing out of the station and being unable to get on it.
statements.chinese: 尽管提前到达可能会浪费一点时间，但这比你错过火车，不得不等一个多小时才能搭乘下一班车要好；而且你还能避免那种火车正驶出车站而你却无法上车的沮丧。
更令人恼火的情况是，你准时到了站台，却眼睁睁看着火车没有你开走。
statements.english: An even harder situation is to be on the platform in good time for a train and still to see it go off without you.

statements.chinese: 这样的经历就发生在一个年轻女孩身上，那是她第一次独自旅行。
statements.english: Such an experience befell a certain young girl the first time she was travelling alone.

She entered the station twenty minutes before the train was due, since her parents had impressed upon her that it would be unforgivable to miss it and cause the friends with whom she was going to stay to make two journeys to meet her.
statements.chinese: 她在火车到站前20分钟就进了车站，因为她的父母曾告诫她错过火车是不可原谅的，那会让她要去拜访的朋友来接她两次。
她把行李交给一个搬运工，并给他看了她的车票。
statements.english: She gave her luggage to a porter and showed him her ticket.

statements.chinese: 让她吃惊的是，他说她早来了两个小时。
statements.english: To her horror he said that she was two hours too soon.

statements.chinese: 她从手提包里摸索出父亲写下所有旅行细节的纸条，交给了搬运工。
statements.english: She felt in her handbag for the piece of paper on which her father had written down all the details of the journey and gave it to the porter.

statements.chinese: 他承认火车确实在纸上写的时间到达车站，也确实停靠了，但那只是为了装载邮件，而不是载客。
statements.english: He agreed that a train did come into the station at the time on the paper and that it did stop, but only to take on mail, not passengers.

statements.chinese: 女孩要求看时刻表，她确信她父亲不可能犯这样的错误。
statements.english: The girl asked to see a timetable, feeling sure that her father could not have made such a mistake.

The porter went to fetch one and arrived back with the station master, who produced it with a flourish and pointed out a microscopic 'o' beside the time of the arrival of the train at his station; this little 'o' indicated that the train only stopped for mail.
statements.chinese: 搬运工去拿时刻表，回来时带着站长，站长得意地拿出时刻表，指出了他们车站火车到站时间旁边的一个微小的“o”；这个小小的“o”表示火车只停靠装载邮件。
就在那时，火车进站了。
statements.english: Just as that moment the train came into the station.

statements.chinese: 女孩泪流满面，乞求允许她溜进守车。
statements.english: The girl, tears streaming down her face, begged to be allowed to slip into the guard's van.

statements.chinese: 但站长态度坚决：规则不能打破。
statements.english: But the station master was adamant: rules could not be broken.

statements.chinese: 她不得不眼睁睁看着那列火车开往目的地，而她却被留在了原地。
statements.english: And she had to watch that train disappear towards her destination while she was left behind.

packs.title: 新概念英语第四册
packs.description: 获授权教材课程 · 流利英语 · 48 课

courses.title: Lesson 1: Finding Fossil Man
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 12 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 说书人世代相传的传说为什么有用？
statements.english: Why are legends handed down by storytellers useful?
We can read of things that happened 5, 000 years ago in the Near East, where people first learned to write.
statements.chinese: 我们能读到5000年前近东发生的事，那里的人们最早学会了书写。
但世界上的某些地方，即使到现在，人们仍然不会书写。
statements.english: But there are some parts of the world where even now people cannot write.

statements.chinese: 他们保存历史的唯一方法，就是把一代代说书人流传下来的史诗故事讲述出来。
statements.english: The only way that they can preserve their history is to recount it as sagas legends handed down from one generation of storytellers to another.
These legends are useful because they can tell us something about migrations of people who lived long ago, but none could write down what they did.
statements.chinese: 这些传说很有用，因为它们能告诉我们一些关于远古人类迁徙的信息，但没有人能记录下他们的所作所为。
人类学家们想知道，如今居住在太平洋岛屿上的波利尼西亚人的远古祖先来自何方。
statements.english: Anthropologists wondered where the remote ancestors of the Polynesian peoples now living in the Pacific Islandscame from.

statements.chinese: 这些人的史诗记载，他们中的一部分人大约在2000年前从印度尼西亚迁徙而来。
statements.english: The sagas of these people explain that some of them came from Indonesia about 2, 000 years ago.

statements.chinese: 但是，第一批与我们相似的人类生活在如此久远的年代，以至于即使他们曾有史诗，也早已被遗忘。
statements.english: But the first people who were like ourselves lived so long ago that even their sagas, if they had any, are forgotten.

statements.chinese: 因此，考古学家既没有历史记载，也没有传说来帮助他们找出第一批“现代人”的起源。
statements.english: So archaeologists have neither history nor legends to help them to find out where the first 'modern men' came from.
Fortunately, however, ancient men made tools of stone, especially flint, because this is easier to shape than other kinds.
statements.chinese: 然而，幸运的是，远古人类制造了石器，尤其是燧石工具，因为它比其他种类的材料更容易塑形。
他们也可能使用过木头和兽皮，但这些都已经腐烂殆尽了。
statements.english: They may also have used wood and skins, but these have rotted away.

statements.chinese: 石头不会腐烂，因此，即使制造这些工具的人的骨骸早已消失得无影无踪，远古的石器工具依然留存至今。
statements.english: Stone does not decay, and so the tools of long ago have remained when even the bones of the men who made them have disappeared without trace.

courses.title: Lesson 2: Spare That Spider
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 18 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 为什么，你可能会想，蜘蛛应该是我们的朋友？
statements.english: Why, you may wonder, should spiders be our friends?

statements.chinese: 因为它们消灭了如此多的昆虫，而昆虫包括了人类最大的敌人中的一部分。
statements.english: Because they destroy so many insects, and insects include some of the greatest enemies of the human race.

statements.chinese: 昆虫会让我们无法在这个世界上生存。
statements.english: Insects would make it impossible for us to live in the world.

statements.chinese: 它们会吞噬我们所有的庄稼，杀死我们的羊群和牛群。
statements.english: They would devour all our crops and kill our flocks and herds.

statements.chinese: 如果没有食虫动物给我们的保护。
statements.english: If it were not for the protection we get from insect-eating animals.

statements.chinese: 我们非常感谢那些吃昆虫的鸟兽。
statements.english: We owe a lot to the birds and beasts who eat insects.

statements.chinese: 但它们加起来所杀死的昆虫数量，只是蜘蛛所消灭的一小部分。
statements.english: But all of them put together kill only a fraction of the number destroyed by spiders.

statements.chinese: 此外，与其他一些食虫动物不同，蜘蛛从不对我们或我们的财物造成丝毫伤害。
statements.english: Moreover, unlike some of the other insect eaters, spiders never do the least harm to us or our belongings.

statements.chinese: 蜘蛛不是昆虫，正如许多人认为的那样，甚至与它们没有密切关系。
statements.english: Spiders are not insects, as many people think, nor even nearly related to them.

statements.chinese: 人们几乎一眼就能分辨出区别，因为蜘蛛总是有八条腿，而昆虫从不超过六条。
statements.english: One can tell the difference almost at a glance, for a spider always has eight legs, and an insect never more than six.

statements.chinese: 有多少蜘蛛正在为我们做这项工作？
statements.english: How many spiders are engaged in this work on our behalf?
One authority on spiders made a census of the spiders in a grass field in the south of England, and he estimated that there were more than 2,250,000 in one acre.
statements.chinese: 一位研究蜘蛛的权威人士对英格兰南部一片草地上的蜘蛛进行了普查，他估计，一英亩土地上就有超过2,250,000只蜘蛛。
这就像一个足球场上有600万只不同种类的蜘蛛。
statements.english: That is something like 6 million spiders of different kinds on a football pitch.

statements.chinese: 蜘蛛一年中至少有一半时间忙于捕杀昆虫。
statements.english: Spiders are busy for at least half the year in killing insects.
It is impossible to make more than the wildest guess at how many they kill, but they are hungry creatures, not content with only three meals a day.
statements.chinese: 要猜测它们杀死了多少，这是不可能的，只能做最粗略的估计，但它们是饥饿的生物，不满足于一天只吃三餐。

statements.english: It has been estimated that the weight of all the insects destroyed by spiders in Britain in one year would be greater than the total weight of all the human beings in the country.
statements.chinese: 据估计，英国一年内被蜘蛛消灭的所有昆虫的总重量将超过该国所有人类的总重量。
T. H. 吉莱斯皮，《放过那只蜘蛛》。
statements.english: T. H. Gillespie, Spare That Spider.

statements.chinese: 选自《听众》。
statements.english: From The Listener.

courses.title: Lesson 3: Matterhorn Man
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 18 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 现代登山者尝试通过一条能让他们享受运动乐趣的路线来攀登山脉。
statements.english: Modern alpinists try to climb mountains by a route which will give them good sport.

statements.chinese: 难度越大，越受推崇。
statements.english: And the more difficult it is, the more highly it is regarded.

statements.chinese: 然而，在早期开拓阶段，情况并非如此。
statements.english: In the pioneering days, however, this was not the case at all.
The early climbers were looking for the easiest way to the top because the summit was the prize they sought, especially if it had never been attained before.
statements.chinese: 早期登山者寻求登顶最便捷的路线，因为山顶是他们追求的奖赏，尤其是在此前从未有人登顶的情况下。

statements.english: It's true that during their explorations, they often faced difficulties and dangers of the most perilous nature, equipped in a manner which would make a modern climber shudder at the thought.
statements.chinese: 确实，在他们的探险过程中，他们经常面临极其危险的困难和危险，他们的装备简陋到会让现代登山者一想到就颤抖。
但他们并非刻意去寻求这种刺激。
statements.english: But they did not go out of their way to court such excitement.

statements.chinese: 他们只有一个目的，一个单一的目标：登顶。
statements.english: They had a single aim, a solitary goal: the top.

statements.chinese: 如今我们很难体会到，对于那些先驱者来说，那时的登山有多么艰难。
statements.english: It's hard for us to realize nowadays how difficult it was for the pioneers.
Except for one or two places such as Zermat and Chamoni, which had rapidly become popular, Alpine villages tended to be impoverished settlements, cut off from civilization by the high mountains.
statements.chinese: 除了采尔马特和霞慕尼等一两个迅速变得热门的地方，阿尔卑斯山区的村庄往往是贫困的定居点，被高山与文明隔绝。
即使有旅店，通常也是肮脏且跳蚤遍布的。
statements.english: Such inns as there were were generally dirty and flea-ridden.
The food simply local cheese accompanied by bread, often 12 months old, all washed down with coarse wine.
statements.chinese: 食物很简单，就是当地的奶酪配面包，奶酪常常有12个月的历史，所有食物都配着粗劣的葡萄酒。
山谷里常常根本没有旅店，登山者只能随遇而安。
statements.english: Often the valley boasted no inn at all, and climbers found shelter wherever they could.

statements.chinese: 有时他们会和当地的牧师住在一起，牧师通常和他的教区居民一样贫穷。
statements.english: Sometimes with the local priest, who was usually as poor as his paritioners.
Sometimes with the local priest, who was usually as poor as his parishioners.
statements.chinese: 有时与当地牧师同住，牧师通常和他的教区居民一样贫困。
有时和牧羊人或奶酪匠住在一起。
statements.english: Sometimes with shepherds or cheesemakers.

statements.chinese: 毫无例外，那时的环境都是一样的：肮脏和贫困，而且非常不舒服。
statements.english: Invariably, the background was the same: dirt and poverty, and very uncomfortable.

statements.chinese: 对于习惯在家享用七道菜晚餐、睡在精致亚麻床单之间的人来说，来到阿尔卑斯山区的这种改变，确实是极其艰难的。
statements.english: For men accustomed to eating seven-course dinners and sleeping between fine linen sheets at home, a change to the Alps must have been very hard indeed.

statements.chinese: 沃尔特·昂斯沃思，《马特洪峰之人》。
statements.english: Walter Unsworth, Matterhorn Man.

courses.title: Lesson 4: Seeing Hands
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 14 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 近来，苏联报道了几起案例，有人能用手指阅读并识别颜色，甚至能看穿实心门和墙壁。
statements.english: In the Soviet Union, several cases have been reported recently of people who can read and detect colors with their fingers, and even see through solid doors and walls.

statements.chinese: 其中一个案例是一名11岁的小学女生，维拉·彼得罗娃，她视力正常，但也能用皮肤的不同部位感知事物，甚至能看穿实心墙。
statements.english: One case concerns an 11-year-old schoolgirl, Vera Petrova, who has normal vision, but who can also perceive things with different parts of her skin and through solid walls.

statements.chinese: 她的父亲最先发现了这种能力。
statements.english: This ability was first noticed by her father.

statements.chinese: 一天，她走进父亲的办公室，偶然将手放在了一个上锁保险箱的门上。
statements.english: One day, she came into his office and happened to put her hands on the door of a locked safe.

statements.chinese: 突然，她问父亲为什么把那么多旧报纸锁在那里，甚至描述了它们是如何捆扎起来的。
statements.english: Suddenly, she asked her father why he kept so many old newspapers locked away there, and even described the way they were done up in bundles.

statements.chinese: 维拉的这种奇特天赋引起了她居住地附近乌里扬诺夫斯克镇一家科研机构的注意。
statements.english: Vera's curious talent was brought to the notice of a scientific research institute in the town of Ulyanovsk, near where she lives.

statements.chinese: 四月，俄罗斯联邦共和国卫生部的一个特别委员会对她进行了一系列测试。
statements.english: And in April, she was given a series of tests by a special commission of the Ministry of Health of the Russian Federal Republic.

statements.chinese: 在这些测试中，她能够透过不透明的屏幕阅读报纸，更奇怪的是，她通过将肘部移过一个孩子的乐透游戏，能够描述出上面印着的数字和颜色。
statements.english: During these tests, she was able to read a newspaper through an opaque screen, and, stranger still, by moving her elbow over a child's game of lotto, she was able to describe the figures and colors printed on it.

statements.chinese: 在另一个例子中，她穿着丝袜和拖鞋，用脚辨认出藏在地毯下的一幅画的轮廓和颜色。
statements.english: And in another instance, wearing stockings and slippers, to make out with her foot the outlines and colors of a picture hidden under a carpet.

statements.chinese: 其他实验表明，她的膝盖和肩膀也有类似的敏感度。
statements.english: Other experiments showed that her knees and shoulders had a similar sensitivity.

statements.chinese: 在所有这些测试中，维拉都被蒙上了眼睛。
statements.english: During all these tests, Vera was blindfold.

statements.chinese: 事实上，除了被蒙住眼睛的时候，她缺乏用皮肤感知事物的能力。
statements.english: And, indeed, except when blindfold, she lacked the ability to perceive things with her skin.

statements.chinese: 另据发现，尽管她能用手指感知事物，但只要手一湿，这种能力就会消失。
statements.english: It was also found that although she could perceive things with her fingers, this ability ceased the moment her hands were wet.

statements.chinese: 埃里克·德·马尔尼，《会看的手》，摘自《听众》杂志。
statements.english: Eric De Marney, Seeing Hands, from The Listener.

courses.title: Lesson 5: Youth
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 17 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 人们总是在谈论青年的问题。
statements.english: People are always talking about the problem of youth.
If there is one, which I take leave to doubt, then it is older people who create it, not the young themselves.
statements.chinese: 如果确实存在这样的问题，对此我表示怀疑，那么这个问题是老年人制造出来的，而不是青年人自己。

statements.english: Let us get down to fundamentals and agree that the young are, after all, human beings, people, just like their elders.
statements.chinese: 让我们回归基本事实，承认青年人毕竟是人，和他们的长辈一样的人。
老年人和青年人之间只有一个区别。
statements.english: There is only one difference between an old man and a young one.
The young man has a glorious future before him, and the old one has a splendid future behind him.
statements.chinese: 青年人拥有光辉灿烂的前程，而老年人则有一个辉煌的过去。
也许这就是症结所在。
statements.english: And maybe that is where the rub is.
When I was a teenager, I felt that I was just young and uncertain, that I was a new boy in a huge school, and I would have been very pleased to be regarded as something so interesting as a problem.
statements.chinese: 当我还是个少年时，我觉得自己年轻而迷茫，在一个庞大的学校里是个新来的，如果被看作一个问题这样有趣的事物，我会非常高兴。

statements.english: For one thing, being a problem gives you a certain identity, and that is one of the things the young are busily engaged in seeking.
statements.chinese: 首先，成为一个问题能赋予你某种身份，而这正是青年人正在努力寻找的东西之一。
我觉得青年人令人兴奋。
statements.english: I find young people exciting.
They have an air of freedom, and they have not a dreary commitment to mean ambitions or love of comfort.
statements.chinese: 他们有一种自由的气息，他们没有对平庸的抱负或对安逸的乏味执着。

statements.english: They are not anxious social climbers, and they have no devotion to material things.
statements.chinese: 他们不是急功近利的社会攀登者，并且他们不执着于物质。
所有这一切在我看来，都把他们与生命和万物之源联系在一起。
statements.english: All this seems to me to link them with life and the origin of things.

statements.chinese: 他们仿佛在某种意义上是宇宙生命，与我们这些郊区生物形成了强烈而可爱的对比。
statements.english: It's as if they were in some sense cosmic beings in violent and lovely contrast with us suburban creatures.

statements.chinese: 当我遇到一个年轻人时，我心中所想的正是这一切。
statements.english: All that is in my mind when I meet a young person.
He may be conceited, ill-mannered, presumptuous or fatuous, but I do not turn for protection to dreary clichés about respect for elders, as if mere age were a reason for respect.
statements.chinese: 他可能自负、粗鲁、傲慢或愚蠢，但我不会求助于关于尊重长辈的陈腐套话来保护自己，仿佛仅仅年龄就是值得尊敬的理由。

statements.english: I accept that we are equals, and I will argue with him as an equal, if I think he is wrong.
statements.chinese: 我承认我们是平等的，如果我认为他错了，我会以平等的身份与他争辩。

statements.english: Fielding Hues, from Out of the Air, to a listener.
statements.chinese: 菲尔丁·休斯，选自《空中漫谈》，致听众。

courses.title: Lesson 6: The Sporting Spirit
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 10 条逐句练习

statements.english: I'm always amazed when I hear people saying that sport creates goodwill between the nations, and that if only the common peoples of the world could meet one another at football or cricket, they would have no inclination to meet on the battlefield.
statements.chinese: 我总是很惊讶，当我听到人们说体育运动能在国家之间建立友好关系，如果世界各国普通民众能通过足球或板球运动彼此相遇，他们就丝毫没有在战场上相遇的意愿了。

statements.english: Even if one didn't know from concrete examples, the 1936 Olympic Games for instance, that international sporting contests lead to orgies of hatred, one could deduce it from general principles.
statements.chinese: 即使人们不是从具体例子，比如1936年的奥运会中得知，国际体育竞赛会导致极度的仇恨，人们也能从一般原则中推断出这一点。
如今进行的几乎所有体育运动都是竞争性的。
statements.english: Nearly all the sports practiced nowadays are competitive.

statements.chinese: 你为赢而比赛，除非你竭尽全力去赢，否则一场比赛就没有多少意义。
statements.english: You play to win, and a game has little meaning unless you do your utmost to win.

statements.chinese: 在村庄的草地上，你可以随意组队，不涉及地方爱国主义情感，纯粹为了乐趣和锻炼而比赛。
statements.english: On the village green, where you pick up sides and no feeling of local patriotism is involved, it's possible to play simply for the fun and the exercise.

statements.chinese: 但一旦涉及声誉问题，一旦你觉得如果你输了，你和某个更大的集体就会蒙羞，最野蛮的好斗本能就会被激发出来。
statements.english: But as soon as the question of prestige arises, as soon as you feel that you and some larger unit will be disgraced if you lose, the most savage combative instincts are aroused.

statements.chinese: 任何即使参加过学校足球比赛的人都知道这一点。
statements.english: Anyone who's played even in a school football match knows this.

statements.chinese: 在国际层面，体育运动坦率地说就是模拟战争。
statements.english: At the international level, sport is frankly mimic warfare.

But the significant thing is not the behavior of the players, but the attitude of the spectators, and behind the spectators, of the nations who work themselves into furies over these absurd contests and seriously believe, at any rate for short periods, that running, jumping and kicking a ball are tests of national virtue.
statements.chinese: 但重要的不是运动员的行为，而是观众的态度，在观众背后，是那些因为这些荒谬的比赛而变得狂热，并认真相信的民族，至少在短时间内，奔跑、跳跃和踢球是民族美德的考验。
乔治·奥威尔，《体育精神》。
statements.english: George Orwell, The Sporting Spirit.

courses.title: Lesson 7: Bats
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 13 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 蝙蝠的回声定位是如何发挥实用作用的？
statements.english: In what way does echo-location in bats play an utilitarian role?

statements.chinese: 并非所有动物发出的声音都作为语言，我们只需看看蝙蝠回声定位这项非凡的发现，就能明白声音在其中扮演着严格实用性角色的例子。
statements.english: Not all sounds made by animals serve as language, and we have only to turn to that extraordinary discovery of echo-location in bats to see a case in which the voice plays a strictly utilitarian role.

statements.chinese: 要充分理解这意味着什么，我们必须首先了解一些近期的人类发明。
statements.english: To get a full appreciation of what this means we must turn first to some recent human inventions.

statements.chinese: 每个人都知道，如果在墙壁或山边附近大喊，会听到回声。
statements.english: Everyone knows that if he shouts in the vicinity of a wall or a mountainside, an echo will come back.

statements.chinese: 这种坚固障碍物越远，回声返回所需的时间就越长。
statements.english: The further off this solid obstruction, the longer time will elapse for the return of the echo.

statements.chinese: 敲击船体发出的声音会从海底反射回来，通过测量敲击声和收到回声之间的时间间隔，可以计算出该点的海水深度。
statements.english: A sound made by tapping on the hull of a ship will be reflected from the sea bottom, and by measuring the time interval between the taps and the receipt of the echoes the depth of the sea at that point can be calculated.

statements.chinese: 于是，回声测深仪应运而生，现在已普遍用于船只上。
statements.english: So was born the echo-sounding apparatus, now in general use in ships.

statements.chinese: 每个固体物体都会反射声音，其反射效果因物体的大小和性质而异。
statements.english: Every solid object will reflect a sound, varying according to the size and nature of the object.

statements.chinese: 一群鱼也会这样做。
statements.english: A shoal of fish will do this.

statements.chinese: 因此，从定位海底到定位一群鱼，这是一个相对简单的步骤。
statements.english: So it is a comparatively simple step from locating the sea bottom to locating a shoal of fish.

statements.chinese: 凭借经验和改进后的设备，现在不仅可以定位鱼群，还可以通过其回声模式判断它们是鲱鱼、鳕鱼还是其他著名的鱼类。
statements.english: With experience, and with improved apparatus, it is now possible not only to locate a shoal but to tell if it is herring, cod, or other well-known fish, by the pattern of its echo.
It has been found that certain bats emit squeaks and by receiving the echoes, they can locate and steer clear of obstacles -- or locate flying insects on which they feed.
statements.chinese: 人们发现某些蝙蝠会发出吱吱声，并通过接收回声，它们可以定位并避开障碍物——或者定位它们赖以为食的飞行昆虫。
蝙蝠的这种回声定位常与雷达相提并论，两者的原理相似。
statements.english: This echo-location in bats is often compared with radar, the principle of which is similar.

courses.title: Lesson 8: Trading Standards
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 14 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 什么使得富裕国家之间的贸易变得困难？
statements.english: What makes trading between rich countries difficult?

statements.chinese: 布鲁塞尔的官员声称，在美国宰杀的鸡不适合摆上欧洲餐桌。
statements.english: Chickens slaughtered in the United States, claim officials in Brussels, are not fit to grace European tables.

statements.chinese: 不，美国人说：我们的家禽很好，我们只是用不同的方式清洗它们。
statements.english: No, say the Americans: our fowl are fine, we simply clean them in a different way.

statements.chinese: 如今，是各国法规的差异，而不是关税，阻碍了富裕国家之间的贸易。
statements.english: These days, it is differences in national regulations, far more than tariffs, that put sand in the wheels of trade between rich countries.

statements.chinese: 抱怨的不仅仅是农民。
statements.english: It is not just farmers who are complaining.

statements.chinese: 一款符合欧盟安全标准的电动剃须刀，在美国销售前必须通过美国测试员的批准；一台美国制造的透析机，在欧洲上市前需要得到欧盟的许可。
statements.english: An electric razor that meets the European Union's safety standards must be approved by American testers before it can be sold in the United States, and an American-made dialysis machine needs the EU's okay before it hits the market in Europe.

statements.chinese: 碰巧的是，在欧洲安全的剃须刀不太可能电死美国人。
statements.english: As it happens, a razor that is safe in Europe is unlikely to electrocute Americans.

statements.chinese: 因此，大西洋两岸的企业都在问，为什么需要进行两套测试，而一套就足够了？
statements.english: So, ask businesses on both sides of the Atlantic, why have two lots of tests where one would do?

statements.chinese: 政治家们原则上同意这一点，因此美国和欧盟一直在努力达成一项协议，以消除许多产品重复测试的必要性。
statements.english: Politicians agree, in principle, so America and the EU have been trying to reach a deal which would eliminate the need to double-test many products.

statements.chinese: 他们希望能在5月28日美国和欧盟贸易峰会前及时完成。
statements.english: They hope to finish in time for a trade summit between America and the EU on May 28th.

statements.chinese: 尽管谈判代表持乐观态度，但细节足够复杂，他们可能很难达成协议。
statements.english: Although negotiators are optimistic, the details are complex enough that they may be hard-pressed to get a deal at all.

statements.chinese: 为什么？一个困难是构建协议。
statements.english: Why? One difficulty is to construct the agreements.

statements.chinese: 美国人乐意先就医疗器械标准达成一项协议，然后再敲定涵盖电子产品和药品生产等不同协议。
statements.english: The Americans would happily reach one accord on standards for medical devices and then hammer out different pacts covering, say, electronic goods and drug manufacturing.
The EU -- following fine continental traditions -- wants agreement on general principles, which could be applied to many types of products and perhaps extended to other countries.
statements.chinese: 欧盟——遵循优良的欧洲大陆传统——希望就普遍原则达成协议，这些原则可以适用于多种类型的产品，并且可能扩展到其他国家。

courses.title: Lesson 9: Royal Espionage
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 21 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 第2单元，第11篇。
statements.english: Unit 2, Passage 11.
Alfred the Great acted as his own spy, visiting Danish camps disguised as a minstrel.
statements.chinese: 阿尔弗雷德大帝亲自担任间谍，乔装成吟游诗人，拜访丹麦人的营地。
在那些日子里，四处游走的吟游诗人到处都受欢迎。
statements.english: In those days, wandering minstrels were welcome everywhere.
They were not fighting men, and their harp was their passport.
statements.chinese: 他们不是战士，他们的竖琴就是他们的通行证。

statements.english: Alfred had learned many of their ballads in his youth and could vary his program with acrobatic tricks and simple conjuring.
statements.chinese: 阿尔弗雷德年轻时学过他们许多民谣，他可以用杂技和简单的魔术来丰富他的节目。

statements.english: While Alfred's little army slowly began to gather at Athelney, the King himself set out to penetrate the camp of Guthrum, the commander of the Danish invaders.
statements.chinese: 当阿尔弗雷德的小部队慢慢开始在埃塞尼集结时，国王亲自出发，渗透进入丹麦入侵者首领古思伦的营地，丹麦入侵者首领古思伦的营地。
丹麦人在奇彭纳姆安顿下来过冬。
statements.english: These had settled down for the winter at Chippenham.

statements.chinese: 阿尔弗雷德去了那里。
statements.english: Thither Alfred went.
He noticed at once that discipline was slack, the Danes had the self-confidence of conquerors, and their security precautions were casual.
statements.chinese: 他立刻注意到纪律松弛，丹麦人有征服者的自信，他们的安全防范措施很随意。

statements.english: They lived well on the proceeds of raids on neighboring regions.
statements.chinese: 他们靠劫掠邻近地区来过上好日子。

statements.english: There they collected women as well as food and drink, and a life of ease had made them soft.
statements.chinese: 他们在那里掠夺妇女以及食物和饮料，安逸的生活使他们变得柔弱。

statements.english: Alfred stayed in the camp a week before he returned to Athelney.
statements.chinese: 阿尔弗雷德在营地里待了一周，然后才返回埃塞尼。

statements.english: The force there assembled was trivial compared with the Danish horde.
statements.chinese: 与丹麦大军相比，在那里集结的部队微不足道。与丹麦大军相比。

statements.english: But Alfred had deduced that the Danes were no longer fit for prolonged battle, and that their commissariat had no organization, but depended on irregular raids.
statements.chinese: 但阿尔弗雷德推断，丹麦人不再适合持久战，他们的后勤补给没有组织，而是依赖于不规则的劫掠。

statements.english: So faced with the Danish advance, Alfred did not risk open battle, but harried the enemy.
statements.chinese: 因此，面对丹麦人的进攻，阿尔弗雷德没有冒险进行公开决战，而是骚扰敌人。

statements.english: He was constantly on the move, drawing the Danes after him.
statements.chinese: 他不停地移动，引诱丹麦人追赶他。
他的巡逻队阻止了丹麦人的搜刮队。
statements.english: His patrols halted the foraging parties.

statements.chinese: 饥饿袭击了丹麦军队。
statements.english: Hunger assailed the Danish army.
Now Alfred began a long series of skirmishes, and within a month the Danes had surrendered.
statements.chinese: 随后，阿尔弗雷德发起了一系列长期的遭遇战，并在一个月内迫使丹麦人投降。

statements.english: The episode could reasonably serve as a unique epic of royal espionage.
statements.chinese: 这一事件完全可以被视为一部独特的皇家谍报史诗。

statements.english: Benrat Newman, Spies in Britain.
statements.chinese: 本拉特·纽曼，《英国间谍》。

courses.title: Lesson 10: Silicon Valley
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 12 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 除了无序状态，计算机产业还依赖什么才能蓬勃发展？
statements.english: What does the computer industry thrive on apart from anarchy?

statements.chinese: 技术趋势可能将硅谷推向未来。
statements.english: Technology trends may push Silicon Valley back to the future.

statements.chinese: 加州理工学院的集成电路先驱、计算机科学教授卡弗·米德指出，现在工程师可以在他们的办公桌上设计、测试和生产芯片，就像编辑在Macintosh上创建新闻通讯一样。
statements.english: Carver Mead, a pioneer in integrated circuits and a professor of computer science at the California Institute of Technology, notes there are now workstations that enable engineers to design, test and produce chips right on their desks, much the way and editor creates a newsletter on a Macintosh.

statements.chinese: 随着芯片制造的时间和成本降至几天和几百美元，工程师们可能很快就能自由发挥想象力，而不会因昂贵的失败而受到惩罚。
statements.english: As the time and cost of making a chip drop to a few days and a few hundred dollars, engineers may soon be free to let their imaginations soar without being penalized by expensive failures.

Mead predicts that inventors will be able to perfect powerful customized chips over a weekend at the office --spawning a new generation of garage start-ups and giving the U. S. a jump on its foreign rivals in getting new products to market fast.
statements.chinese: 米德预测，发明家将能够在办公室里用一个周末的时间完善功能强大的定制芯片——催生新一代的“车库创业公司”，并使美国在将新产品快速推向市场方面超越其外国竞争对手。
米德观察道：“我们有更多拥有聪明人的车库。”“我们确实在无序状态中茁壮成长。”
statements.english: 'We've got more garages with smart people,' Mead observes. 'We really thrive on anarchy.'

statements.chinese: 还有亚洲人。在许多硅谷公司，东方人和亚裔美国人已经构成了工程技术人员的大多数。
statements.english: And on Asians. Already, orientals and Asian Americans constitute the majority of the engineering staffs at many Valley firms.

statements.chinese: 中国、韩国、菲律宾和印度的工程师正从加州的大学里大量毕业。
statements.english: And Chinese, Korean, Filipino and Indian engineers are graduating in droves from California's colleges.

statements.chinese: 作为下一代创业公司的负责人，这些亚洲创新者可以利用习俗和语言与关键的环太平洋市场建立更紧密的联系。
statements.english: As the heads of next-generation start-ups, these Asian innovators can draw on customs and languages to forge tighter links with crucial Pacific Rim markets.

statements.chinese: 例如，来自香港的斯坦福大学博士Alex Au在台湾设立了一家工厂，以挑战日本在内存芯片市场近乎垄断的地位。
statements.english: For instance, Alex Au, a Stanford Ph. D. from Hong Kong, has set up a Taiwan factory to challenge Japan's near lock on the memory-chip market.

statements.chinese: 去年春天，印度出生的N. Damodar Reddy在密苏里州的资助下，他那小小的加州公司在堪萨斯城重新启用了一家AT&T芯片工厂。
statements.english: India-born N. Damodar Reddy's tiny California company reopened an AT&T chip plant in Kansas City last spring with financing from the state of Missouri.

statements.chinese: 在它成为一个退休村之前，硅谷可能会成为一个建立全球业务的课堂。
statements.english: Before it becomes a retirement village, Silicon Valley may prove a classroom for building a global business.

courses.title: Lesson 11: How to Grow Old
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 17 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 有些老年人被死亡的恐惧所压迫。
statements.english: Some old people are oppressed by the fear of death.

statements.chinese: 在年轻人身上，这种感觉有其正当理由。
statements.english: In the young, there is a justification for this feeling.

statements.chinese: 有理由担心会在战场上被杀害的年轻人，有理由感到痛苦，因为他们认为自己被剥夺了生命所能提供的最好的一切。
statements.english: Young men who have reason to fear that they will be killed in battle, may justifiably feel bitter in the thought that they have been cheated of the best things that life has to offer.

statements.chinese: 但对于一个经历过人间悲欢离合、完成了自己力所能及的所有工作的老年人来说，对死亡的恐惧则显得有些卑劣和可耻。
statements.english: But in an old man who has known human joys and sorrows, and has achieved whatever work it was in him to do, the fear of death is somewhat abject and ignoble.

statements.chinese: 克服它的最佳方法，至少在我看来是这样，是逐渐拓宽你的兴趣，使其更加超然，直到一点一点地，自我的围墙后退，你的生命越来越融入到普遍的生命之中。
statements.english: The best way to overcome it, so at least it seems to me, is to make your interests gradually wider and more impersonal, until bit by bit, the walls of the ego recede, and your life becomes increasingly merged in the universal life.

statements.chinese: 个体的生命应该像一条河流。
statements.english: An individual human existence should be like a river.

statements.chinese: 最初很小，被狭窄的河岸限制，然后充满激情地冲过巨石，越过瀑布。
statements.english: Small at first, narrowly contained within its banks, and rushing passionately past boulders and over waterfalls.

statements.chinese: 渐渐地，河流变得越来越宽阔。
statements.english: Gradually, the river grows wider.

statements.chinese: 河岸向后退去。
statements.english: The banks recede.

statements.chinese: 河水流淌得更加平静。
statements.english: The waters flow more quietly.

statements.chinese: 最终，在没有任何明显的断裂的情况下，它们汇入大海，毫无痛苦地失去了它们的个体存在。
statements.english: And in the end, without any visible break, they become merged in the sea, and painlessly lose their individual being.

statements.chinese: 一个人，在老年时能这样看待自己的生命，就不会被死亡的恐惧所困扰。
statements.english: The man who, in old age, can see his life in this way, will not suffer from the fear of death.

statements.chinese: 因为他所关心的事物将继续存在。
statements.english: Since the things he cares for will continue.

statements.chinese: 而且，如果随着生命力的衰退，疲惫感增加，那么休息的念头将不会不受欢迎。
statements.english: And if, with the decay of vitality, weariness increases, the thought of rest will be not unwelcome.

statements.chinese: 我希望能在我仍在工作时死去，知道其他人会继续我无法再做的事情，并满足于这样的想法：凡是可能的都已完成。
statements.english: I should wish to die while still at work, knowing that others will carry on what I can no longer do, and content in the thought that what was possible has been done.

statements.chinese: 伯特兰·罗素。
statements.english: Bertrand Russell.

statements.chinese: 《如何变老》，选自《记忆中的肖像》。
statements.english: How to grow old, from Portraits from Memory.

courses.title: Lesson 12: Banks and Their Customers
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 15 条逐句练习

statements.english: When anyone opens a current account at a bank, he's lending the bank money.
statements.chinese: 当任何人在银行开设往来账户时，他是在向银行贷款。

statements.english: Repayment of which he may demand at any time, either in cash or by drawing a check in favor of another person.
statements.chinese: 他可以随时要求偿还这笔款项，无论是现金支付还是开具支票给他人。
从根本上讲，银行与客户的关系是债权人与债务人的关系。
statements.english: Primarily, the bank-customer relationship is that of debtor and creditor.
Who is which, depending on whether the customer's account is in credit or is overdrawn.
statements.chinese: 谁是哪一方，取决于客户的账户是贷方余额还是透支。

statements.english: But, in addition to that basic simple concept, the bank and its customer owe a large number of obligations to one another.
statements.chinese: 但是，除了那个基本的简单概念之外，银行及其客户彼此之间还负有大量义务。
这些义务中的许多都可能引发问题和复杂情况。
statements.english: Many of these obligations can give rise to problems and complications.
But a bank customer, unlike, say, a buyer of goods, cannot complain that the law is loaded against him.
statements.chinese: 但银行客户，不像，比如说，商品买家，不能抱怨法律对他不利。

statements.english: The bank must obey its customer's instructions, and not those of anyone else.
statements.chinese: 银行必须遵守客户的指示，而非其他任何人的指示。

statements.english: When, for example, a customer first opens an account, he instructs the bank to debit his account only in respect of checks drawn by himself.
statements.chinese: 例如，当客户首次开户时，他指示银行仅对由他本人开出的支票进行借记。

statements.english: He gives the bank specimens of his signature, and there's a very firm rule that the bank has no right or authority to pay out a customer's money on a check on which its customer's signature has been forged.
statements.chinese: 他向银行提供了他的签名样本，并且有一条非常明确的规定，即银行无权或无权限在支票上，如果客户的签名是伪造的，银行不得支付客户的款项。
即使伪造手段非常高明，这也没有区别。
statements.english: It makes no difference that the forgery may have been a very skillful one.

statements.chinese: 银行必须识别其客户的签名。
statements.english: The bank must recognize its customer's signature.
For this reason, there is no risk to the customer in the modern practice adopted by some banks of printing the customer's name on his checks.
statements.chinese: 因此，在现代实践中，对于客户来说没有风险，一些银行采纳了在支票上打印客户姓名的做法。
如果这方便了伪造，那么损失的是银行，而不是客户。
statements.english: If this facilitates forgery, it is the bank which will lose, not the customer.
Gordon Bawry and Aubrey L. Diamond, The Consumer Society and the Law.
statements.chinese: 戈登·鲍里和奥布里·L·戴蒙德，《消费者社会与法律》。

courses.title: Lesson 13: The Search for Oil
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 14 条逐句练习

statements.english: The deepest holes of all are made for oil, and they go down to as much as 25,000 feet.
statements.chinese: 所有最深的孔都是为石油而钻的，深度可达25,000英尺。

statements.english: But we do not need to send men down to get the oil out, as we must with other mineral deposits.
statements.chinese: 但我们不需要派人下去把油取出来，就像我们处理其他矿藏一样。
这些孔只是钻孔，直径不到一英尺。
statements.english: The holes are only borings, less than a foot in diameter.
My particular experience is largely in oil, and the search for oil has done more to improve deep drilling than any other mining activity.
statements.chinese: 我的特殊经验主要是在石油领域，寻找石油的工作比任何其他采矿活动都更能改善深井钻探。

statements.english: When it has been decided where we are going to drill, we put up at the surface an oil derrick.
statements.chinese: 当决定好在哪里钻探时，我们会在地表搭建一个采油井架。

statements.english: It has to be tall because it is like a giant block and tackle, and we have to lower into the ground and haul out of the ground great lengths of drill pipe, which are rotated by an engine at the top, and are fitted with a cutting bit at the bottom.
statements.chinese: 它必须很高，因为它就像一个巨大的滑轮组，我们必须将很长的钻杆下入地下并从地下吊出，这些钻杆由顶部的发动机旋转，底部装有钻头。
地质学家需要知道钻头到达了哪些岩石。
statements.english: The geologist needs to know what rocks the drill has reached.

statements.chinese: 因此，每隔一段时间，就会用取心钻头获取一个样本。
statements.english: So every so often a sample is obtained with a coring bit.

statements.chinese: 它切下一块干净的圆柱形岩石，从中可以看到钻头穿过的地层。
statements.english: It cuts a clean cylinder of rock from which can be seen the strata the drill has been cutting through.

statements.chinese: 一旦我们到达石油层，它通常会流到地表，因为巨大的压力，无论是来自气体还是水，都在推动它。
statements.english: Once we get down to the oil, it usually flows to the surface because great pressure, either from gas or water, is pushing it.
This pressure must be under control, and we control it by means of the mud which we circulate down the drill pipe.
statements.chinese: 这种压力必须受到控制，我们通过在钻杆中循环泥浆来控制它。
我们努力避免那种浪费石油和天然气的老式喷井的浪漫想法。
statements.english: We endeavor to avoid the old romantic idea of a gusher which wastes oil and gas.

statements.chinese: 我们希望它留在井下，直到我们能以受控的方式将其引出。
statements.english: We want it to stay down the hole until we can lead it off in a controlled manner.
T.F. Gaskel, The Search for the Earth's Minerals, from Discovery.
statements.chinese: T.F. 加斯科尔，《地球矿藏的探索》，选自《发现》。

courses.title: Lesson 14: The Butterfly Effect
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 13 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 为什么小的误差会使得准确预测天气系统变得不可能？
statements.english: Why do small errors make it impossible to predict the weather system with a high degree of accuracy?
Beyond two or three days, the world's best weather forecasts are speculative, and beyond six or seven they are worthless.
statements.chinese: 超过两三天，世界上最好的天气预报都是推测性的，超过六七天，它们就毫无价值了。
蝴蝶效应就是原因。
statements.english: The Butterfly Effect is the reason.
For small pieces of weather--and to a global forecaster, small can mean thunderstorms and blizzards--any prediction deteriorates rapidly.
statements.chinese: 对于局部天气——对于全球预报员来说，局部可能意味着雷暴和暴风雪——任何预测都会迅速恶化。

statements.english: Errors and uncertainties multiply, cascading upward through a chain of turbulent features, from dust devils and squalls up to continent-size eddies that only satellites can see.
statements.chinese: 误差和不确定性倍增，通过一系列湍流特征向上级联，从尘卷风和飑线直到只有卫星才能看到的洲际大小的涡流。

statements.english: The modern weather models work with a grid of points of the order of sixty miles apart, and even so, some starting data has to be guessed, since ground stations and satellites cannot see everywhere.
statements.chinese: 现代天气模型采用相距约六十英里的网格点，即便如此，一些初始数据也必须是猜测的，因为地面站和卫星无法看到所有地方。

statements.english: But suppose the earth could be covered with sensors spaced one foot apart, rising at one-foot intervals all the way to the top of the atmosphere.
statements.chinese: 但是假设地球可以被间隔一英尺的传感器覆盖，并以一英尺的间隔一直上升到大气的顶端。

statements.english: Suppose every sensor gives perfectly accurate readings of temperature, pressure, humidity, and any other quantity a meteorologist would want.
statements.chinese: 假设每个传感器都能提供完全准确的温度读数，压力、湿度以及气象学家想要的任何其他量。

statements.english: Precisely at noon an infinitely powerful computer takes all the data and calculates what will happen at each point at 12.01, then 12.02, then 12.03...
statements.chinese: 正午时分，一台无限强大的计算机获取所有数据，并计算出每个点将发生什么，在12点01分，然后12点02分，然后12点03分……
这台计算机仍然无法预测一个月后新泽西州普林斯顿是晴天还是雨天。
statements.english: The computer will still be unable to predict whether Princeton, New Jersey, will have sun or rain on a day one month away.
At noon the spaces between the sensors will hide fluctuations that the computer will not know about, tiny deviations from the average.
statements.chinese: 中午时，传感器之间的空间会隐藏计算机不知道的波动，那些与平均值微小的偏差。
到12点01分，这些波动就已经在离传感器一英尺的地方造成了小误差。
statements.english: By 12.01, those fluctuations will already have created small errors one foot away.

statements.chinese: 很快，这些误差将倍增到十英尺的尺度，并以此类推，直到全球范围。
statements.english: Soon the errors will have multiplied to the ten-foot scale, and so on up to the size of the globe.

courses.title: Lesson 15: Secrecy in Industry
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 11 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 为什么保密在化学工业中尤其重要？
statements.english: Why is secrecy particularly important in the chemical industries?

statements.chinese: 有两个因素严重阻碍了工业中科学研究的有效性。
statements.english: Two factors weigh heavily against the effectiveness of scientific research in industry.
One is the general atmosphere of secrecy in which it is carried out, the other the lack of freedom of the individual research worker.
statements.chinese: 一个是它所进行的普遍保密氛围，另一个是单个研究人员缺乏自由。

statements.english: In so far as any inquiry is a secret one, it naturally limits all those engaged in carrying it out from effective contact with their fellow scientists either in other countries or in universities, or even, often enough, in other departments of the same firm.
statements.chinese: 只要任何一项调查是秘密的，它自然会限制所有从事这项工作的人与他们在其他国家或大学的同行科学家进行有效接触，甚至，在很多情况下，与同一公司的其他部门也无法有效接触。
保密程度自然差异很大。
statements.english: The degree of secrecy naturally varies considerably.
Some of the bigger firms are engaged in researches which are of such general and fundamental nature that it is a positive advantage to them not to keep them secret.
statements.chinese: 一些大公司从事的研究具有普遍性和基础性，因此不保密对他们来说是一种积极的优势。
然而，许多依赖此类研究的工艺在专利可以申请之前，都以完全保密的方式进行探索。
statements.english: Yet a great many processes depending on such research are sought for with complete secrecy until the stage at which patents can be taken out.

statements.chinese: 甚至更多的工艺根本不申请专利，而是作为秘密工艺保存。
statements.english: Even more processes are never patented at all but kept as secret processes.
This applies particularly to chemical industries, where chance discoveries play a much larger part than they do in physical and mechanical industries.
statements.chinese: 这尤其适用于化学工业，因为在化学工业中，偶然发现所起的作用远大于在物理和机械工业中。
有时保密程度如此之高，以至于整个研究的性质都不能被提及。
statements.english: Sometimes the secrecy goes to such an extent that the whole nature of the research cannot be mentioned.

Many firms, for instance have great difficulty in obtaining technical or scientific books from libraries because they are unwilling to have their names entered as having taken out such and such a book, for fear the agents of other firms should be able to trace the kind of research they are likely to be undertaking.
statements.chinese: 举例来说，许多公司在从图书馆获取技术或科学书籍时面临很大困难，因为他们不愿留下借阅某某书籍的记录，唯恐其他公司的代理人能够据此追踪他们可能正在进行的研究类型。

courses.title: Lesson 16: The Modern City
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 11 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 作者关于现代城市的主要论点是什么？
statements.english: What is the author's main argument about the modern city?

statements.chinese: 在工业生活的组织中，工厂对工人生理和心理状态的影响已被完全忽视。
statements.english: In the organization of industrial life the influence of the factory upon the physiological and mental state of the workers has been completely neglected.
Modern industry is based on the conception of the maximum production at lowest cost, in order that an individual or a group of individuals may earn as much money as possible.
statements.chinese: 现代工业建立在以最低成本实现最大产量的概念上，以便个人或群体能够尽可能多地赚钱。

statements.english: It has expanded without any idea of the true nature of the human beings who run the machines, and without giving any consideration to the effects produced on the individuals and on their descendants by the artificial mode of existence imposed by the factory.
statements.chinese: 它的扩张，完全没有考虑到操作机器的人类的真实本性，也完全没有考虑到工厂强加的人工生存模式对个体及其后代产生的影响。
那些大城市的建设完全没有考虑到我们。
statements.english: The great cities have been built with no regard for us.

The shape and dimensions of the skyscrapers depend entirely on the necessity of obtaining the maximum income per square foot of ground, and of offering to the tenants offices and apartments that please them.
statements.chinese: 摩天大楼的形状和尺寸完全取决于每平方英尺土地获取最大收入的需要，以及向租户提供令他们满意的办公室和公寓。
这导致了巨型建筑的建造，大量人类被拥挤在一起。
statements.english: This caused the construction of gigantic buildings where too large masses of human beings are crowded together.

statements.chinese: 文明人喜欢这样的生活方式。
statements.english: Civilized men like such a way of living.

statements.chinese: 当他们享受着住所的舒适和平庸的奢华时，却没有意识到他们被剥夺了生活必需品。
statements.english: While they enjoy the comfort and banal luxury of their dwelling, they do not realize that they are deprived of the necessities of life.

The modern city consists of monstrous edifices and of dark, narrow streets full of petrol fumes and toxic gases, torn by the noise of the taxicabs, lorries and buses, and thronged ceaselessly by great crowds.
statements.chinese: 现代城市由怪诞的建筑和充满汽油烟雾和有毒气体的黑暗狭窄街道组成，被出租车、卡车和公共汽车的噪音撕裂，并不断被大量人群挤满。
显然，它的规划并非为了居民的福祉。
statements.english: Obviously, it has not been planned for the good of its inhabitants.

courses.title: Lesson 17: A Man-made Disease
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 17 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 是什么因素帮助传播了黏液瘤病？
statements.english: What factor helped to spread the disease of myxomatosis?

statements.chinese: 在澳大利亚早期定居时，富有进取心的定居者不明智地引进了欧洲兔。
statements.english: In the early days of the settlement of Australia, enterprising settlers unwisely introduced the European rabbit.

statements.chinese: 这种兔子在大洋洲没有天敌，因此它以兔子特有的滥交放纵方式大量繁殖。
statements.english: This rabbit had no natural enemies in the Antipodes, so that it multiplied with that promiscuous abandon characteristic of rabbits.

statements.chinese: 它遍布了整个大陆。
statements.english: It overran a whole continent.

statements.chinese: 它通过挖洞和吞食草料造成了破坏，这些草料本可以养活数百万只绵羊和牛。
statements.english: It caused devastation by burrowing and by devouring the herbage which might have maintained millions of sheep and cattle.

statements.chinese: 科学家发现，这种特殊品种的兔子（显然没有其他动物）易感染一种致命的病毒性疾病——黏液瘤病。
statements.english: Scientists discovered that this particular variety of rabbit (and apparently no other animal) was susceptible to a fatal virus disease, myxomatosis.

statements.chinese: 通过感染动物并将它们释放到洞穴中，可以制造这种疾病的局部流行。
statements.english: By infecting animals and letting them loose in the burrows, local epidemics of this disease could be created.

statements.chinese: 后来发现有一种蚊子充当这种疾病的载体，并将其传播给兔子。
statements.english: Later it was found that there was a type of mosquito which acted as the carrier of this disease and passed it on to the rabbits.

statements.chinese: 因此，当世界其他地方都在努力消灭蚊子时，澳大利亚却在鼓励这种蚊子。
statements.english: So while the rest of the world was trying to get rid of mosquitoes, Australia was encouraging this one.

statements.chinese: 它有效地将疾病传播到整个大陆，并大幅减少了兔子数量。
statements.english: It effectively spread the disease all over the continent and drastically reduced the rabit population.
It later became apparent that rabbits were developing a degree of resistance to this disease, so that the rabbit population was unlikely to be completely exterminated.
statements.chinese: 后来，很明显兔子对这种疾病正在产生一定程度的抵抗力，因此兔子种群不太可能被完全消灭。
然而，人们希望兔子的（鼠害）问题能够变得可控。
statements.english: There were hopes, however, that the problem of the rabbit would become manageable.

statements.chinese: 具有讽刺意味的是，欧洲将兔子作为害虫遗赠给澳大利亚，现在却将这种人为的疾病视为一场瘟疫。
statements.english: Ironically, Europe, which had bequeathed the rabbit as a pest to Australia, acquired this man-made disease as a pestilence.

statements.chinese: 一位法国医生决定清除自己庄园里的野兔，并引入了黏液瘤病。
statements.english: A French physician decided to get rid of the wild rabbits on his own estate and introduced myxomatosis.

statements.chinese: 然而，它并没有局限于这个庄园。
statements.english: It did not, however, remain within the confines of this estate.

It spread through France, where wild rabbits are not generally regarded as a pest but as a sport and a useful food supply, and it spread to Britain where wild rabbits are regarded as a pest but where domesticated rabbits, equally susceptible to the disease, are the basis of a profitable fur industry.
statements.chinese: 它传播到法国，在那里野兔通常不被视为害虫，而是作为一项运动和有用的食物来源，并传播到英国，在那里野兔被视为害虫，但家养兔子，同样易受这种疾病感染，却是利润丰厚的毛皮产业的基础。
问题变成了人类是否能够控制他所制造的疾病。
statements.english: The question became one of whether Man could control the disease he had invented.

courses.title: Lesson 18: Porpoises
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 19 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 你认为海豚的主要特征是什么？
statements.english: What would you say is the main characteristic of porpoises?
There has long been a superstition among mariners that porpoises will save drowning men by pushing them to the surface, or protect them from sharks by surrounding them in defensive formation.
statements.chinese: 长期以来，水手们中间一直流传着一种迷信，认为海豚会把溺水的人托到水面，从而救他们的命，或者通过组成防御队形来保护他们免受鲨鱼的袭击。

statements.english: Marine Studio biologists have pointed out that, however intelligent they may be, it is probably a mistake to credit dolphins with any motive of life-saving.
statements.chinese: 海洋生物研究所的生物学家指出，无论海豚多么聪明，把它们任何行为都归结为救生动机，那可能是一种误解。

statements.english: On the occasions when they have pushed to shore an unconscious human being they have much more likely done it out of curiosity or for sport, as in riding the bow waves of a ship.
statements.chinese: 在它们把不省人事的人推到岸边时，它们很可能只是出于好奇或玩耍，就像它们在船头波浪中冲浪一样。
1928年，有人拍摄到一些海豚像海狸一样辛勤地把一张浸透了水的褥垫推到岸边。
statements.english: In 1928 some porpoises were photographed working like beavers to push ashore a waterlogged mattress.
If, as has been reported, they have protected humans from sharks, it may have been because curiosity attracted them and because the scent of a possible meal attracted the sharks.
statements.chinese: 如果像报道所说，它们保护过人类免遭鲨鱼袭击，那可能是因为好奇心吸引了海豚，而一顿美餐的气味吸引了鲨鱼。
海豚和鲨鱼是天敌。
statements.english: Porpoises and sharks are natural enemies.

statements.chinese: 在这种情况下，很可能发生了一场战斗，鲨鱼被赶跑或杀死。
statements.english: It is possible that upon such an occasion a battle ensued, with the sharks being driven away or killed.

statements.chinese: 无论是鸟、鱼还是野兽，海豚对任何有生命的东西都充满好奇。
statements.english: Whether it be bird, fish or beast, the porpoise is intrigued with anything that is alive.

statements.chinese: 它们总是追逐海龟，而海龟则平静地忍受着各种羞辱。
statements.english: They are constantly after the turtles, who peacefully submit to all sorts of indignities.
One young calf especially enjoyed raising a turtle to the surface with his snout, and then shoving him across the tank like an aquaplane.
statements.chinese: 有一只幼年海豚特别喜欢用它的鼻子把海龟顶到水面，然后像水上飞机一样把海龟推着穿过水箱。
几乎每天都能看到一只幼年海豚试图把一只300磅重的海龟翻过来，它把鼻子伸到海龟壳的边缘下面，拼命地往上顶。
statements.english: Almost any day a young porpoises may be seen trying to turn a 300-pound sea turtle over by sticking his snout under the edge of his shell and pushing up for dear life.

statements.chinese: 这并不容易，可能需要两只海豚一起合作。
statements.english: This is not easy, and may require two porpoises working together.

statements.chinese: 在另一个游戏中，当海龟游过海洋馆时，第一只海豚从上方猛扑下来，用肚子撞击它的壳。
statements.english: In another game, as the turtle swims across the oceanarium, the first porpoise swoops down from above and butts his shell with his belly.

statements.chinese: 这把海龟撞下去好几英尺。
statements.english: This knocks the turtle down several feet.

statements.chinese: 它刚恢复平衡，下一只海豚就过来又撞它一下。
statements.english: He no sooner recovers his equilibrium than the next porpoises comes along and hits him another crack.

statements.chinese: 最终，海龟被一直撞到了水箱底部。
statements.english: Eventually the turtle has been butted all the way down to the floor of the tank.

statements.chinese: 它现在只满足于试图站起来，但它刚一站起来，一只海豚又把它撞倒。
statements.english: He is now satisfied merely to try to stand up, but as soon as he does so a porpoise knocks him flat.

statements.chinese: 海龟最终放弃了，它把脚缩进壳里，游戏结束。
statements.english: The turtle at last gives up by pulling his feet under his shell and the game is over.

courses.title: Lesson 19: The Stuff of Dreams
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 18 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 睡眠期肯定具有某种功能。
statements.english: It's fairly clear that the sleeping period must have some function.

statements.chinese: 而且由于睡眠期很长，这种功能似乎很重要。
statements.english: And because there is so much of it, the function would seem to be important.

statements.chinese: 关于其性质的猜测已经持续了几千年。
statements.english: Speculations about its nature have been going on for literally thousands of years.

statements.chinese: 一个令人费解的奇怪发现是，睡眠似乎不仅仅是让身体休息。
statements.english: And one odd finding that makes the problem puzzling is that it looks very much as if sleeping is not simply a matter of giving the body a rest.

statements.chinese: 肌肉放松等方面的休息可以通过短暂的躺卧甚至坐着来实现。
statements.english: Rest in terms of muscle relaxation and so on can be achieved by a brief period lying or even sitting down.

statements.chinese: 身体的组织在一定程度上是自我修复和自我恢复的，并且在或多或少持续活动时功能最佳。
statements.english: The body's tissues are self-repairing and self-restoring to a degree and function best when more or less continuously active.

statements.chinese: 事实上，睡眠期间会发生一定程度的运动，这尤其与防止肌肉不活动有关。
statements.english: In fact, a basic amount of movement occurs during sleep, which is specifically concerned with preventing muscle inactivity.

statements.chinese: 如果这不是身体休息的问题，那么也许是大脑需要休息。
statements.english: If it is not a question of resting the body, then perhaps it's the brain that needs resting.

statements.chinese: 如果不是因为两个因素，这可能是一个合理的假设。
statements.english: This might be a plausible hypothesis, would it not for two factors.

First, the electroencephalograph, which is simply a device for recording the electrical activity of the brain by attaching electrodes to the scalp, shows that while there is a change in the pattern of activity during sleep, there is no evidence that the total amount of activity is any less.
statements.chinese: 首先，脑电图仪，它只是一个通过将电极连接到头皮来记录大脑电活动的设备，表明虽然睡眠期间活动模式发生变化，但没有证据表明总活动量有所减少。
第二个因素更有趣，也更根本。
statements.english: The second factor is more interesting and more fundamental.

statements.chinese: 1960 年，一位名叫威廉·德门特的美国精神病学家发表了关于记录睡眠期间眼球运动的实验。
statements.english: In 1960, an American psychiatrist named William Dement published experiments dealing with the recording of eye movements during sleep.

statements.chinese: 他表明，平均每个人的睡眠周期都伴随着独特的眼球运动爆发，有些漂移缓慢，有些则抽搐快速。
statements.english: He showed that the average individual sleep cycle is punctuated with peculiar bursts of eye movements, some drifting and slow, others jerky and rapid.

statements.chinese: 在这些眼球运动期间被唤醒的人通常报告说他们一直在做梦。
statements.english: People woken during these periods of eye movements generally reported that they had been dreaming.

statements.chinese: 在其他时间被唤醒时，他们报告说没有梦。
statements.english: When woken at other times, they reported no dreams.

statements.chinese: 如果一组人在连续几个晚上从眼球运动睡眠中被干扰，而另一组人在相同的时间段内被干扰，但当他们没有表现出眼球运动时，第一组开始表现出一些人格障碍，而另一组则或多或少没有受到影响。
statements.english: If one group of people were disturbed from their eye movement sleep for several nights on end, and another group were disturbed for an equal period of time, but when they were not exhibiting eye movements, the first group began to show some personality disorders, while the others seemed more or less unaffected.

statements.chinese: 所有这一切的含义是，重要的不是睡眠的干扰，而是做梦的干扰。
statements.english: The implications of all this were that it was not the disturbance of sleep that mattered, but the disturbance of dreaming.

statements.chinese: 克里斯托弗·埃文斯，《听众》中的梦境内容。
statements.english: Christopher Evans, the stuff of dreams from the listener.

courses.title: Lesson 20: Snake Poison
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 27 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 蛇是如何制造毒液的，至今仍是一个谜。
statements.english: How it came about that snakes manufactured poison is a mystery.

statements.chinese: 经过漫长的时期，它们的唾液——一种像我们自己的消化液一样温和的液体——转化为一种毒液，即使在今天也难以分析其成分。
statements.english: Over the periods, their saliva, a mild digestive juice just like our own, was converted into a poison that defies analysis even today.

statements.chinese: 这并非是生存竞争强加给它们的。
statements.english: It was not forced upon them by the survival competition.

statements.chinese: 它们完全可以在不使用毒液的情况下捕捉猎物并以此为生，就像成千上万的无毒蛇现在仍在做的那样。
statements.english: They could have caught and lived on prey without using poison, just as the thousands of non-poisonous snakes still do.

statements.chinese: 对于蛇来说，毒液只是一种奢侈品。
statements.english: Poison to a snake is merely a luxury.

statements.chinese: 它让蛇能够不费吹灰之力地获取食物，只需一口即可。
statements.english: It enables it to get its food with very little effort, no more effort than one bite.

statements.chinese: 那么，为什么只有蛇会制造毒液呢？
statements.english: And why only snakes?

statements.chinese: 例如，猫如果拥有毒液将大有帮助。
statements.english: Cats for instance would be greatly helped.

statements.chinese: 不用与凶猛的大老鼠搏斗，也不用与成年兔子纠缠。
statements.english: No running fights with large fierce rats or tussles with grown rabbits.

statements.chinese: 只需一口，便无需再费力气。
statements.english: Just a bite and no more effort needed.

statements.chinese: 事实上，对于所有的食肉动物来说，毒液都会有所帮助，尽管当它们自相残杀时，这将是一把双刃剑。
statements.english: In fact, it would be an assistance to all the Carnivora, though it would be a two-edged weapon when they fought each other.

statements.chinese: 然而在脊椎动物中，不可预测的大自然只选择了蛇和一种蜥蜴。
statements.english: But of the vertebrates, unpredictable nature selected only snakes and one lizard.

statements.chinese: 人们还想知道，为什么大自然让某些蛇制造出如此剧毒的毒液。
statements.english: One wonders also if why nature with some snakes concocted poison of such extreme potency.

statements.chinese: 在唾液转化为毒液的过程中，人们可能会认为发生了一个固定的过程。
statements.english: In the conversion of saliva into poison, one might suppose that a fixed process took place.

statements.chinese: 事实并非如此。
statements.english: It did not.

statements.chinese: 有些蛇制造的毒液在各个方面都与其他蛇的不同。
statements.english: Some snakes manufactured a poison different in every respect from that of others.

statements.chinese: 就像砷与士的宁一样截然不同，而且具有不同的效果。
statements.english: As different as arsenic is from strychnine and having different effects.

statements.chinese: 一种毒液作用于神经，另一种作用于血液。
statements.english: One poison acts on the nerves, the other on the blood.

statements.chinese: 神经毒液的制造者包括曼巴蛇和眼镜蛇，它们的毒液被称为神经毒素。
statements.english: The maker of the nerve poison includes the mambas and the cobras and their venom is called neurotoxic.

statements.chinese: 蝰蛇、蝮蛇和响尾蛇制造血液毒液，这种毒液被称为溶血毒素。
statements.english: Vipers, adders, and rattlesnakes manufacture the blood poison, which is known as hemolytic.

statements.chinese: 两种毒液都不好，但更糟糕的无疑是血液毒液。
statements.english: Both poisons are unpleasant, but by far the more unpleasant is the blood poison.

statements.chinese: 据说神经毒液是两者中更原始的一种。
statements.english: It is said that the nerve poison is the more primitive of the two.

statements.chinese: 而血液毒液，可以说是一种经过改良配方的新产品。
statements.english: That the blood poison is, so to speak, a newer product from an improved formula.

statements.chinese: 尽管如此，神经毒液对人类的作用比血液毒液要快得多。
statements.english: Be that as it may, the nerve poison does its business with man far more quickly than the blood poison.

statements.chinese: 然而，这并不意味着什么。
statements.english: This however means nothing.

statements.chinese: 蛇获得毒液并非为了对抗人类，而是为了对抗老鼠等猎物，而蝰蛇毒液对这些猎物的作用几乎是立竿见影的。
statements.english: Snakes did not acquire their poison for use against man, but for use against prey such as rats and mice, and the effects on these of viperine poison is almost immediate.

statements.chinese: 约翰·克朗普顿，《蛇》。
statements.english: John Crompton, The Snake.

courses.title: Lesson 21: William S. Hart and the Early Western Film
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 10 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 威廉·哈特的童年是怎样为他在西部片中的表演做准备的？
statements.english: How did William Hart's childhood prepare him for his acting role in Western films?
William S.Hart was, perhaps, the greatest of all Western stars, for unlike Gary Cooper and John Wayne he appeared in nothing but Westerns.
statements.chinese: 威廉·S·哈特也许是所有西部片明星中最伟大的。因为他不像加里·库珀和约翰·韦恩那样，他只出演西部片。
从1914到1924年，他独领风骚，无人能及。
statements.english: From 1914 to 1924 he was supreme and unchallenged.

It was Hart who created the basic formula of the Western film, and devised the protagonist he played in every film he made, the good-bad man, the accidental, noble outlaw, or the honest, but framed cowboy, or the sheriff made suspect by vicious gossip; in short, the individual in conflict with himself and his frontier environment.
statements.chinese: 是哈特创造了西部片的基本模式，并设计了他所主演的每部影片中的主角，亦正亦邪的好坏人，偶然成为的正直的歹徒，或是诚实但遭诬陷的牛仔，或是因流言蜚语而受到怀疑的警长；简而言之，就是与自己和其边疆环境相冲突的个体。

statements.english: Unlike most of his contemporaries in Hollywood, Hart actually knew something of the old West.
statements.chinese: 与他在好莱坞的大多数同时代演员不同，哈特确实了解一些旧西部。

statements.english: He had lived in it as a child when it was already disappearing, and his hero was firmly rooted in his memories and experiences, and in both the history and the mythology of the vanished frontier, And although no period or place in American history has been more absurdly romanticized, myth and reality did join hands in at least one arena, the conflict between the individual and encroaching civilization.
statements.chinese: 他小时候曾生活在那个已经逐渐消失的西部，他的英雄人物深深扎根于他的记忆和经历中，以及在消逝边疆的历史和神话中。尽管美国历史上没有任何一个时期或地方比西部更被荒谬地浪漫化，但神话和现实至少在一个领域联手了，那就是个体与入侵文明之间的冲突。

statements.english: Men accustomed to struggling for survival against the elements and Indians were bewildered by politicians, bankers and businessmen, and unhorsed by fences, laws and alien taboos.
statements.chinese: 习惯于与自然元素和印第安人斗争求生的人们，被政客、银行家和商人搞得手足无措，被篱笆、法律和陌生的禁忌所限制。

statements.english: Hart's good-bad man was always an outsider, always one of the disinherited, and if he found it necessary to shoot a sheriff or rob a bank along the way, his early audiences found it easy to understand and forgive, especially when it was Hart who, in the end, overcame the attacking Indians.
statements.chinese: 哈特的“亦正亦邪的好坏人”总是一个局外人，一个被剥夺继承权的人，如果他觉得有必要射杀一名警长或沿途抢劫一家银行，他的早期观众很容易理解并原谅，尤其当最终是哈特击败了来犯的印第安人时。

statements.english: Audiences in the second decade of the twentieth century found it pleasant to escape to a time when life, though hard, was relatively simple.
statements.chinese: 二十世纪第二个十年的观众乐于逃到一个虽然艰辛但相对简单的时代。

statements.english: We still do; living in a world in which undeclared aggression, war, hypocrisy, chicanery, anarchy and impending immolation are part of our daily lives, we all want a code to live by.
statements.chinese: 我们现在仍然如此；生活在一个不宣而战的侵略、战争、虚伪、诡计、无政府状态和即将到来的毁灭是我们日常生活一部分的世界里，我们都渴望有一个行为准则。

courses.title: Lesson 22: Knowledge and Progress
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 18 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 为什么进步的观念在现代世界中如此突出？
statements.english: Why does the idea of progress loom so large in the modern world?

statements.chinese: 当然是因为某种特定类型的进步正在我们身边发生，并且变得越来越明显。
statements.english: Surely because progress of a particular kind is actually taking place around us and is becoming more and more manifest.

statements.chinese: 尽管人类在智力或道德方面没有普遍进步，但在知识积累方面却取得了非凡的进展。
statements.english: Although mankind has undergone no general improvement in intelligence or morality, it has made extraordinary progress in the accumulation of knowledge.

statements.chinese: 知识的增长始于个体思想可以通过言语传播给他人。
statements.english: Knowledge began to increase as soon as the thoughts of one individual could be communicated to another by means of speech.

statements.chinese: 随着文字的发明，取得了巨大的进步，因为知识不仅可以传播，还可以储存。
statements.english: With the invention of writing, a great advance was made, for knowledge could then be not only communicated but also stored.

statements.chinese: 图书馆使教育成为可能，而教育反过来又增加了图书馆的藏书。
statements.english: Libraries made education possible, and education in its turn added to libraries.

statements.chinese: 知识的增长遵循一种复利法则，这通过印刷术的发明而大大增强。
statements.english: The growth of knowledge followed a kind of compound interest law, which was greatly enhanced by the invention of printing.

statements.chinese: 所有这一切都相对缓慢，直到科学的到来，节奏才突然加快。
statements.english: All this was comparatively slow until, with the coming of science, the tempo was suddenly raised.

statements.chinese: 然后知识开始按照系统的计划积累。
statements.english: Then knowledge began to be accumulated according to a systematic plan.

statements.chinese: 涓涓细流汇成小溪，小溪如今已成洪流。
statements.english: The trickle became a stream, the stream has now become a torrent.

statements.chinese: 此外，一旦获得新知识，它现在就被付诸实际应用。
statements.english: Moreover, as soon as new knowledge is acquired, it is now turned to practical account.

statements.chinese: 所谓的现代文明，并非人类所有本性均衡发展的结果，而是将累积的知识应用于实际生活。
statements.english: What is called modern civilization is not the result of a balanced development of all man's nature, but of accumulated knowledge applied to practical life.

statements.chinese: 人类现在面临的问题是，所有这些知识将如何处理。
statements.english: The problem now facing humanity is what is going to be done with all this knowledge.

statements.chinese: 正如人们常指出的那样，知识是一把双刃剑，既可用于善，也可用于恶。
statements.english: As is so often pointed out, knowledge is a two-edged weapon, which can be used equally for good or evil.

statements.chinese: 它现在被不加区分地用于两者。
statements.english: It is now being used indifferently for both.

statements.chinese: 例如，还有什么比炮兵利用科学摧毁人体，而近在咫尺的医生却用它来修复人体更令人毛骨悚然又异想天开的景象呢？
statements.english: Could any spectacle, for instance, be more grimly whimsical than that of gunners using science to shatter men's bodies, while close at hand, surgeons use it to restore them?

statements.chinese: 我们必须非常认真地问自己，如果这种知识的双重用途及其日益增长的力量继续下去，将会发生什么。
statements.english: We have to ask ourselves very seriously what will happen if this twofold use of knowledge with its ever-increasing power continues.

statements.chinese: G.N.M. 泰勒，《人的个性》。
statements.english: G.N.M. Tyrrell, The Personality of Man.

courses.title: Lesson 23: Bird Flight
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 16 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 没有哪两种鸟的飞行方式是完全相同的。
statements.english: No two sorts of birds practice quite the same sort of flight.

statements.chinese: 种类繁多，但大致可分为两类。
statements.english: The varieties are infinite, but two classes may be roughly seen.
Any ship that crosses the Pacific is accompanied for many days by the smaller albatross, which may keep company with the vessel for an hour without visible or more than occasional movement of wing.
statements.chinese: 任何横渡太平洋的船只，都会有多日受到较小的信天翁的陪伴，它可以陪伴船只一个小时，而翅膀没有明显的，或只是偶尔的摆动。

statements.english: The currents of air that the walls of the ship direct upwards, as well as in the line of its course, are enough to give the great bird with its immense wings sufficient sustenance and progress.
statements.chinese: 船壁向上引导的气流，以及沿着船只航线的气流，足以让这只拥有巨大翅膀的大鸟获得足够的支撑和前进动力。

statements.english: The albatross is the king of the gliders, the class of flyers which harness the air to their purpose, but must yield to its opposition.
statements.chinese: 信天翁是滑翔鸟之王，它们是利用空气达到目的的飞行者，但必须顺从空气的阻力。
在相反的学派中，鸭子是至高无上的。
statements.english: In the contrary school, the duck is supreme.

statements.chinese: 它更接近于人类征服空气所使用的引擎，正如人类所夸耀的那样。
statements.english: It comes nearer to the engines with which man has conquered the air, as he boasts.

statements.chinese: 鸭子，与鸽子不同，被赋予了钢铁般的肌肉，占了鸟体重量的很大一部分。
statements.english: Duck, unlike them the pigeons, are endowed with steel-like muscles that are a good part of the weight of the bird.

statements.chinese: 它们会以不可抗拒的力量扇动短小的翅膀，即使在逆风中也能长距离飞行，直到筋疲力尽。
statements.english: And these will ply the short wings with irresistible power that can bear them for long distances through an opposite gale before exhaustion follows.

statements.chinese: 它们更卑微的追随者，如鹧鸪，也有类似的强大推进力，但很快就会疲劳。
statements.english: Their humbler followers, such as partridges, have a like power of strong propulsion, but soon tire.

statements.chinese: 如果海风驱使它们进行长途旅行，你可能会发现它们筋疲力尽地倒下。
statements.english: You may pick them up in utter exhaustion if wind over the sea has driven them to a long journey.

statements.chinese: 燕子兼具两派的优点，表现出色。
statements.english: The swallow shares the virtues of both schools in highest measure.

It tires not, nor does it boast of its power, but belongs to the air, traveling it may be 6,000 miles to and from its northern nesting home, feeding its flown young as it flies, and slipping through a medium that seems to help its passage even when the wind is adverse.
statements.chinese: 它不知疲倦，也不炫耀自己的力量，它属于天空，也许会在其北方巢穴之间来回飞行6000英里，一边飞行一边喂养飞翔的雏鸟，在似乎有助于其前进的介质中穿梭，即使风向不利。
这样的鸟对我们有益。
statements.english: Such birds do us good.
Though we no longer take omens from the flight on this side and that, and even the most superstitious villagers no longer take off their hats to the magpie and wish it good morning.
statements.chinese: 虽然我们不再从这边的飞行和那边的飞行中占卜吉凶，即使是最迷信的村民也不再向喜鹊脱帽致敬，祝它早上好。

statements.english: William Beach Thomas, A Countryman's Creed.
statements.chinese: 威廉·比奇·托马斯，《一个乡下人的信条》。

courses.title: Lesson 24: Beauty
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 13 条逐句练习

statements.english: A young man sees a sunset, and, unable to understand or to express the emotion that it rouses in him, concludes that it must be the gateway to a world that lies beyond.
statements.chinese: 一个年轻人看到日落，却无法理解或表达它在他心中唤起的情感，从而得出结论，这一定是通往一个世界的大门，那个世界超越了此地。

statements.english: It's difficult for any of us in moments of intense aesthetic experience to resist the suggestion that we are catching a glimpse of a light that shines down to us from a different realm of existence, different, and because the experience is intensely moving, in some way higher.
statements.chinese: 在强烈的美学体验时刻，我们任何人，都难以抗拒这样一种暗示：我们正在瞥见一道光芒，它从一个不同的存在领域照耀着我们，那是不同的，并且由于体验是极其动人的，在某种程度上是更高的存在。

statements.english: And though the gleams blind and dazzle, yet do they convey a hint of beauty and serenity greater than we have known or imagined.
statements.chinese: 尽管那些微光令人目眩神迷，它们却传达出一种我们从未体验过或想象过的更大的美丽与宁静。

statements.english: Greater too than we can describe, for language, which was invented to convey the meanings of this world, cannot readily be fitted to the uses of another.
statements.chinese: 同时也比我们能描述的更伟大，因为语言，是为了传达这个世界的意义而发明的，无法轻易地适用于另一个世界的用途。

statements.english: That all great art has this power of suggesting a world beyond is undeniable.
statements.chinese: 所有伟大的艺术都具有暗示一个超越此地世界的力量，这是无可否认的。
在某些心境下，大自然也分享着这种力量。
statements.english: In some moods nature shares it.
There is no sky in June so blue that it does not point forward to a bluer, no sunset so beautiful that it does not waken the vision of a greater beauty.
statements.chinese: 六月的天空没有一片蓝得不像在指向更蓝的天空；没有一个日落美丽得不像在唤醒对更伟大美的憧憬。

statements.english: A vision which passes before it is fully glimpsed, and in passing leaves an indefinable longing and regret.
statements.chinese: 这种憧憬在被充分瞥见之前便已消逝，在消逝中留下一种难以言喻的渴望和遗憾。

statements.english: But, if this world is not merely a bad joke, life a vulgar shlaire, a bit the cruel radiance of the stars, an existence an empty laugh braying across the mysteries, if these intimations of a something behind and beyond are not evil humor born of indigestion or whimsies, sent by the devil to mock and madness, if, in a word, beauty means something, yet we must not seek to interpret the meaning.
statements.chinese: 但是，如果这个世界不仅仅是一个糟糕的玩笑，生命不是庸俗的玩笑，而星星残酷的光芒，存在不是穿越神秘的空洞笑声，如果这些关于“某种存在”于其后和其外的暗示，不是消化不良或心血来潮产生的恶意幽默，不是魔鬼派来嘲弄和制造疯狂的，换句话说，如果美有意义，那么我们绝不能试图去诠释它的意义。

statements.english: If we glimpse the unutterable, it is unwise to try to utter it.
statements.chinese: 如果我们瞥见了不可言喻之物，试图说出它是不明智的。

statements.english: Nor should we seek to invest with significance that which we cannot grasp.
statements.chinese: 我们也不应试图赋予其意义，那些我们无法掌握的东西。

statements.english: Beauty in terms of our human meaning is meaningless.
statements.chinese: 从我们人类的意义来看，美是毫无意义的。

statements.english: C. A. M. Joad, Pieces of Mind.
statements.chinese: C. A. M. 乔德，《思想片段》。

courses.title: Lesson 25: Non-Auditory Effects of Noise
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 23 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 第二部分。
statements.english: Part two.

statements.chinese: 第4单元，第31篇文章。
statements.english: Unit 4, Passage 31.
Many people in industry and the services who've practically experienced of noise, regard any investigation of this question as a waste of time.
statements.chinese: 许多在工业和服务业中亲身经历过噪音的人，都认为调查这个问题是浪费时间。
他们甚至不愿承认噪音会影响人的可能性。
statements.english: They're not prepared even to admit the possibility that noise affects people.

statements.chinese: 另一方面，那些不喜欢噪音的人有时会利用最不充分的证据来支持他们对一个更安静社会的要求。
statements.english: On the other hand, those who dislike noise will sometimes use most inadequate evidence to support their pleas for a quieter society.
This is a pity because noise abatement really is a good cause, and it's likely to be discredited if it gets to be associated with bad science.
statements.chinese: 这很遗憾，因为噪音消除确实是一项很好的事业，如果它与糟糕的科学联系在一起，它很可能会失去信誉。
常见的一种指控是噪音会导致精神疾病。
statements.english: One allegation often made is that noise produces mental illness.

A recent article in a weekly newspaper, for instance, was headed with a striking illustration of a lady in a state of considerable distress with the caption she was yet another victim reduced to a screaming wreck.
statements.chinese: 例如，最近一份周报上的一篇文章，配有一幅醒目的插图，描绘了一位处于极度痛苦中的女士，标题写道：她是又一个被折磨得尖叫不止的受害者。

statements.english: On turning eagerly to the text, one learns that the lady was a typist who found the sound of office typewriters worried her more and more until eventually, she had to go into a mental hospital.
statements.chinese: 当人们急切地翻阅文本时，发现这位女士是一名打字员，她发现办公室打字机的声音让她越来越烦恼，直到最终，她不得不住进精神病院。
这种轶事的症结当然在于无法区分因果关系。
statements.english: Now, the snag in this sort of anecdote is of course that one cannot distinguish cause and effect.
Was the noise a cause of the illness, or were the complaints about noise merely a symptom?
statements.chinese: 噪音是疾病的原因，还是对噪音的抱怨仅仅是一种症状？
另一位病人也可能会抱怨她的邻居合伙诽谤和迫害她。
