statements.english: Another patient might equally well complain that her neighbors were combining to slander her and persecute her.

statements.chinese: 然而，人们可能会对相信这种说法持谨慎态度。
statements.english: And yet one might be cautious about believing this statement.
What is needed in the case of noise is a study of large numbers of people living under noisy conditions to discover whether they are mentally ill more often than other people are.
statements.chinese: 对于噪音，我们需要做的是研究大量在嘈杂环境中生活的人，发现他们是否比其他人更容易患精神疾病。
例如，美国海军最近检查了大量在航空母舰上工作的男性。
statements.english: The United States Navy, for instance, recently examined a very large number of men working on aircraft carriers.

statements.chinese: 这项研究被称为“阿纳欣项目”。
statements.english: The study was known as Project Anahin.

statements.chinese: 即使住在离机场几英里远的地方也会让人不舒服。
statements.english: It can be unpleasant to live even several miles from an aerodrome.
If you think what it must be like to share the deck of a ship with several squadrons of jet aircraft, you will realize that a modern Navy is a good place to study noise.
statements.chinese: 如果你想到与几个中队的喷气式飞机共享一艘船的甲板会是什么样子，你就会意识到现代海军是研究噪音的好地方。
但无论是精神病学访谈还是客观测试，都未能显示出对这些美国水兵的任何影响。
statements.english: But neither psychiatric interviews nor objective tests were able to show any effects upon these American sailors.

statements.chinese: 这一结果仅仅证实了早些时候美国和英国的研究。
statements.english: This result merely confirms earlier American and British studies.
If there is any effect of noise upon mental health, it must be so small that present methods of psychiatric diagnosis cannot find it.
statements.chinese: 如果噪音对精神健康有任何影响，那也一定微乎其微，以至于目前的精神病诊断方法无法发现它。

statements.english: That does not prove that it does not exist, but it does mean that noise is less dangerous than say being brought up in an orphanage, which really is a mental health hazard.
statements.chinese: 这并不能证明它不存在，但它确实意味着噪音的危险性不如在孤儿院长大，那才真正是精神健康隐患。
D.E.布罗德本特，《噪音的非听觉效应》，选自《科学调查》。
statements.english: D. E. Broadbent, Non-Auditory Effects of Noise, from Science Survey.

courses.title: Lesson 26: The Past Life of the Earth
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 17 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 生活在水边或水中的动物和植物的遗骸最有可能被保存下来，因为保存的必要条件之一是快速埋藏。
statements.english: It is animals and plants which lived in or near water, whose remains are most likely to be preserved, for one of the necessary conditions of preservation is quick burial.

statements.chinese: 只有在海洋、河流以及有时是湖泊中，泥沙不断沉积的地方，尸体等才能迅速被覆盖并保存下来。
statements.english: And it is only in the seas and rivers, and sometimes lakes, where mud and silt have been continuously deposited, that bodies and the like can be rapidly covered over and preserved.

statements.chinese: 但即使在最有利的情况下，死亡的生物中也只有一小部分能以这种方式保存下来，免于腐烂，或者，更有可能的是，在被食腐动物吃掉之前。
statements.english: But even in the most favorable circumstances, only a small fraction of the creatures that die are preserved in this way before decay sets in, or, even more likely, before scavengers eat them.

statements.chinese: 毕竟，所有生物都靠捕食其他生物而生，无论是植物还是动物，死的还是活的，只有偶然才能避免这种命运。
statements.english: After all, all living creatures live by feeding on something else, whether it be plant or animal, dead or alive, and it is only by chance that such fate is avoided.

statements.chinese: 生活在陆地上的动植物遗骸很少能被保存下来，因为很少有东西能覆盖它们。
statements.english: The remains of plants and animals that lived on land are much more rarely preserved, for there is seldom anything to cover them over.

statements.chinese: 当你想到空中飞舞的无数鸟类，更不用说那些你看不到的同样多的像野鼠和鼢鼠那样的小动物时，你很少会遇到一具尸体，当然，除了在公路上。
statements.english: When you think of the innumerable birds that one sees flying about, not to mention the equally numerous small animals like field mice and voles, which you do not see, it is very rarely that one comes across a dead body, except, of course, on the roads.

statements.chinese: 它们会腐烂，并很快被天气破坏或被其他生物吃掉。
statements.english: They decompose and are quickly destroyed by the weather or eaten by some other creature.

statements.chinese: 陆地动物的痕迹之所以能保存下来，几乎总是由于一些非常特殊的情况，例如坠入无法进入的洞穴或冰缝中，就像西伯利亚猛犸象一样，有时整个动物都能像在冰箱里一样被保存下来。
statements.english: It is almost always due to some very special circumstances that traces of land animals survive, as by falling into inaccessible caves or into an ice crevice, like the Siberian mammoths, when the whole animal is sometimes preserved as in a refrigerator.

statements.chinese: 这就是著名的别列佐夫卡猛犸象的遭遇，它被发现时保存完好。
statements.english: This is what happened to the famous Berezovka mammoth, which was found preserved and in good condition.

statements.chinese: 它的嘴里有冷杉树的残骸，那是它在掉进裂缝摔断脊骨之前的最后一餐。
statements.english: In his mouth were the remains of fir trees, the last meal that he had before he fell into the crevice and broke his back.

statements.chinese: 这只猛犸象现在已在列宁格勒的古生物学博物馆中修复。
statements.english: The mammoth has now been restored in the paleontological museum in Leningrad.

statements.chinese: 其他动物则被困在焦油坑中，比如大象、剑齿虎，以及在拉布雷亚牧场发现的许多其他生物，拉布雷亚牧场现在只是洛杉矶的一个郊区。
statements.english: Other animals were trapped in tar pits, like the elephants, saber-toothed cats, and numerous other creatures that are found at Rancho La Brea, which is now just a suburb of Los Angeles.

statements.chinese: 显然，发生的情况是水聚集在这些焦油坑上，像大象这样的大型动物冒险走到看似坚实的表面喝水，然后迅速陷入焦油中。
statements.english: Apparently, what happened was that water collected on these tar pits, and the bigger animals like the elephants ventured out onto the apparently firm surface to drink and were promptly bogged in the tar.

statements.chinese: 然后，当它们死亡后，像剑齿虎和巨型狼这样的食肉动物出来进食，也遭受了同样的命运。
statements.english: And then, when they were dead, the carnivores, like the saber-toothed cats and the giant wolves, came out to feed and suffered exactly the same fate.

statements.chinese: 焦油中也有无数只鸟。
statements.english: There are also endless numbers of birds in the tar as well.

statements.chinese: 埃罗尔·怀特。
statements.english: Errol White.

statements.chinese: 选自《发现》。
statements.english: From Discovery.

courses.title: Lesson 27: The vasa
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 21 条逐句练习

statements.english: From the 17th century Empire of Sweden, the story of a galleon that sank at the start of her maiden voyage in 1628 must be one of the strangest tales of the sea.
statements.chinese: 从17世纪瑞典帝国，一艘于1628年首航时沉没的加利恩帆船的故事一定是海上最奇怪的故事之一。

statements.english: For nearly three and a half centuries, she lay at the bottom of Stockholm Harbor until her discovery in 1956.
statements.chinese: 近三个半世纪以来，她一直躺在斯德哥尔摩港的底部，直到1956年被发现。
这就是瓦萨号，大帝国舰队的皇家旗舰。
statements.english: This was the Vasa, royal flagship of the Great Imperial Fleet.
King Gustavus Adolphus, the Northern Hurricane, then at the height of his military success in the 30 years war, had dictated her measurements and armament.
statements.chinese: 国王古斯塔夫二世·阿道夫，北方的飓风，当时正值三十年战争军事胜利的巅峰，曾亲自指定了它的尺寸和武装。
三层炮甲板上装备了64门青铜大炮。
statements.english: Triple gun decks mounted 64 bronze cannon.

statements.chinese: 她旨在瑞典日益壮大的国力中扮演重要角色。
statements.english: She was intended to play a leading role in the growing might of Sweden.
As she was prepared for her maiden voyage on August the 10th, 1628, Stockholm was in ferment.
statements.chinese: 当她于1628年8月10日准备首航时，斯德哥尔摩一片沸腾。

statements.english: As she was prepared for her maiden voyage on August the 10th, 1628, Stockholm was in a ferment.
statements.chinese: 当她于1628年8月10日准备首航时，斯德哥尔摩一片沸腾。

statements.english: From the Skepsbron and surrounding islands, the people watched this thing of beauty begin to spread her sails and catch the wind.
statements.chinese: 从谢普斯布隆和周围的岛屿上，人们看着这艘美丽的船，开始扬帆起航，乘风破浪。
他们辛勤劳作了三年，才造出了这件浮动的艺术品。
statements.english: They had labored for three years to produce this floating work of art.

statements.chinese: 她比以往任何一艘船都雕刻得更华丽，装饰得更精美。
statements.english: She was more richly carved and ornamented than any previous ship.

The high stern castle was a riot of carved gods, demons, knights, kings, warriors, mermaids, cherubs, and zoomorphic animal shapes ablaze with red and gold and blue, symbols of courage, power and cruelty, were portrayed to stir the imaginations of the superstitious sailors of the day.
statements.chinese: 高耸的船尾楼雕满了众神、恶魔、骑士、国王、战士、美人鱼、小天使，以及红、金、蓝三色交织的动物形态，它们是勇气、力量和残酷的象征，被描绘出来以激发当时迷信水手的想象力。

statements.english: Then the cannons of the anchored warships thundered a salute, to which the Vasa fired in reply.
statements.chinese: 接着，停泊的战舰大炮轰鸣致敬，瓦萨号也开炮回应。

statements.english: As she emerged from her drifting cloud of gun smoke, with the water churned to foam beneath her bow, her flags flying, pennants waving, sails filling in the breeze, and the red and gold of her superstructure ablaze with color, she presented a more majestic spectacle than Stockholmers had ever seen before.
statements.chinese: 当她从漂浮的硝烟中现身时，船头下方的水翻腾成泡沫，旗帜飘扬，三角旗招展，风帆在微风中鼓起，船体上层建筑的红金色熠熠生辉，她展现出比斯德哥尔摩居民以往所见更宏伟的景象。
所有炮门都已打开，炮口凶恶地从中探出。
statements.english: All gun ports were open, and the muzzles peeped wickedly from them.
As the wind freshened, there came a sudden squall, and the ship made a strange movement listing to port.
statements.chinese: 当风力增强时，突然一阵狂风袭来，船体向左舷倾斜，做出了一个奇怪的动作。

statements.english: The ordinance officer ordered all the port cannon to be heaved to starboard to counteract the list, but the steepening angle of the decks increased.
statements.chinese: 军械官命令所有左舷大炮移至右舷以抵消倾斜，但甲板倾斜的角度越来越大。

statements.english: Then the sound of rumbling thunder reached the watchers on the shore, as cargo, ballast, ammunition, and 400 people went sliding and crashing down to the port side of the steeply listing ship.
statements.chinese: 随后，隆隆的雷声传到岸上的观望者耳中，货物、压舱物、弹药，以及400人滑落并砸向严重倾斜船只的左舷。

statements.english: The lower gun ports were now below water, and the inrushed sea sealed the ship's fate.
statements.chinese: 下层炮门此时已在水下，涌入的海水注定了这艘船的命运。

statements.english: In that first glorious hour, the mighty Vasa, which was intended to rule the Baltic, sank with all flags flying in the harbor of her birth.
statements.chinese: 在那第一个辉煌的时刻，强大的瓦萨号，本应称霸波罗的海，却在她的诞生地港口，伴随着所有旗帜的飘扬沉没了。

statements.english: Roy Saunders, The Raising of the Vasa from The Listener.
statements.chinese: 罗伊·桑德斯，《听众》中的《瓦萨号的打捞》。

courses.title: Lesson 28: Patients and Doctors
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 11 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 病人看医生时在寻找什么？
statements.english: What are patients looking for when they visit the doctor?

This is a sceptical age, but although our faith in many of the things in which our forefathers fervently believed has weakened, our confidence in the curative properties of the bottle of medicine remains the same as theirs.
statements.chinese: 这是一个怀疑的时代，尽管我们对先辈们曾笃信的许多事物的信念已动摇，但我们对瓶装药物疗效的信心却和他们一样坚定。

statements.english: This modern faith in medicines is proved by the fact that the annual drug bill of the Health Services is mounting to astronomical figures.
statements.chinese: 对药物的这种现代信念由以下事实得到证明：医疗服务机构每年的药品费用正在攀升至天文数字，
而且目前没有停止增长的迹象。
statements.english: and shows no signs at present of ceasing to rise.

The majority of the patients attending the medical out-patients departments of our hospitals feel that they have not received adequate treatment unless they are able to carry home with them some tangible remedy in the shape of a bottle of medicine, a box of pills, or a small jar of ointment, and the doctor in charge of the department is only too ready to provide them with these requirements.
statements.chinese: 在我们医院门诊部就诊的大多数病人觉得，除非他们能带回家一些具体可见的治疗方法，比如一瓶药水、一盒药片或一小罐药膏，否则他们就没有得到充分的治疗。而负责该部门的医生也非常乐意满足他们的这些要求。

statements.english: There is no quicker method of disposing of patients than by giving them what they are asking for, and since most medical men in the Health Services are overworked and have little time for offering time-consuming and little-appreciated advice on such subjects as diet, right living, and the need for abandoning bad habits etc., the bottle, the box, and the jar are almost always granted them.
statements.chinese: 没有比给病人他们所要求的东西更能迅速打发他们的方法了，而且由于医疗服务机构的大多数医务人员工作过度，很少有时间提供耗时且不被重视的建议，比如关于饮食、正确生活方式以及改掉坏习惯等，所以药水、药片和药膏几乎总是会给他们。
并非只有无知和受教育程度不高的人才对瓶装药水有如此大的信心。
statements.english: Nor is it only the ignorant and ill-educated person who has such faith in the bottle of medicine.

It is recounted of Thomas Carlyle that when he heard of the illness of his friend, Henry Taylor, he went off immediately to visit him, carrying with him in his pocket what remained a bottle of medicine formerly prescribed for an indisposition of Mrs. Carlyle's.
statements.chinese: 据记载，托马斯·卡莱尔听说他的朋友亨利·泰勒生病时，立刻前去探望他，口袋里带着一瓶他妻子卡莱尔夫人以前因病服用后剩下的药水。

statements.english: Carlyle was entirely ignorant of what the bottle in his pocket contained, of the nature of the illness from which his friend was suffering, and of what had previously been wrong with his wife, but a medicine that had worked so well in one form of illness would surely be of equal benefit in another, and comforted by the thought of the help he was bringing to his friend, he hastened to Henry Taylor's house.
statements.chinese: 卡莱尔完全不知道他口袋里的药瓶装着什么，也不知道他的朋友患的是什么病，更不知道他妻子以前得了什么病，但他认为一种疾病疗效显著的药，对另一种病也肯定同样有效，想到他能给朋友带来帮助，便感到欣慰，于是他匆匆赶往亨利·泰勒家。
历史上没有记载他的朋友是否接受了他的医疗帮助，但很可能他接受了。
statements.english: History does not relate whether his friend accepted his medical help, but in all probability he did.

The great advantage of taking medicine is that it makes no demands on the taker beyond that of putting up for a moment with a disgusting taste, and that is what all patients demand of their doctors--to be cured at no inconvenience to themselves.
statements.chinese: 服药的最大优点在于它对服药者没有任何要求，除了忍受一小会儿难闻的味道之外，而这正是所有病人对医生提出的要求——在自己不感到任何不便的情况下被治愈。

courses.title: Lesson 29: The Hovercraft
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 21 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 在我们这个世纪里，许多新奇的交通工具相继问世。
statements.english: Many strange new means of transport have been developing in our century.

statements.chinese: 其中最奇特的可能要数气垫船了。
statements.english: The strangest of them being perhaps the hovercraft.

In 1953, a former electronics engineer in his 50s, Christopher Cockerell, who had turned to boat building on the Norfolk Broads, suggested an idea on which he had been working for many years to the British government and industrial circles.
statements.chinese: 1953年，一位50多岁的前电子工程师克里斯托弗·科克雷尔，他当时已转行在诺福克湖区造船，向英国政府和工业界提出了一个他已研究多年的想法。
他的想法是，用一个低压气垫支撑船只，气垫周围环绕着一个高压气垫。
statements.english: It was the idea of supporting a craft on a pad or cushion of low-pressure air, ringed with a cushion of high-pressure air.
Ever since, people have had difficulty in deciding whether the craft should be ranged among ships, planes or land vehicles, or is something in between a boat and an aircraft.
statements.chinese: 从那时起，人们就很难确定这种交通工具究竟应该归入船舶、飞机还是陆地车辆，还是介于船和飞机之间的一种东西。

statements.english: As a shipbuilder, Cockerell was trying to find a solution to the problem of the wave resistance, which wastes a good deal of a surface ship's power and limits its speed.
statements.chinese: 作为一名造船师，科克雷尔试图找到解决波浪阻力问题的方法，波浪阻力会消耗水面船只大量的动力并限制其速度。
他的解决方案是，让船只浮在厚度不超过一两英尺的气垫上，从而使其离开水面。
statements.english: His answer was to lift the vessel out of the water by making it ride on a cushion of air no more than one or two feet thick.

statements.chinese: 这是通过船底大量的环形喷气口来实现的。
statements.english: This is done by a great number of ring-shaped air jets on the bottom of the craft.

statements.chinese: 因此，它能飞行，但不能飞得太高。
statements.english: It flies, therefore, but it cannot fly higher.

statements.chinese: 它的运动取决于它所行驶的水面或地面。
statements.english: Its action depends on the surface, water or ground, over which it rides.

statements.chinese: 1959年在索伦特海峡进行的首次试验引起了轰动。
statements.english: The first tests on the Solent in 1959 caused a sensation.

statements.chinese: 气垫船先是在水面上航行，然后登上沙滩，爬上沙丘，最后停在路上。
statements.english: The hovercraft traveled first over the water, then mounted the beach, climbed up the dunes and sat down on a road.

statements.chinese: 后来，它跨越了英吉利海峡，平稳地在海浪上行驶，毫无问题。
statements.english: Later, it crossed the Channel, riding smoothly over the waves which presented no problem.
Since that time, various types of hovercraft have appeared and taken up regular service, cruises on the Thames in London, for instance, have become an annual attraction.
statements.chinese: 从那时起，各种类型的气垫船相继出现并投入定期服务，例如，伦敦泰晤士河上的游船已成为一年一度的景点。
但我们只是处于一项可能彻底改变水陆交通的发展的开端。
statements.english: But we are only at the beginning of a development that may transform sea and land transport.

statements.chinese: 克里斯托弗·科克雷尔的气垫船可以在通信条件差的广阔地区建立交通网络，例如非洲或澳大利亚。
statements.english: Christopher Cockerell's craft can establish transport networks in large areas with poor communications, such as Africa or Australia.

statements.chinese: 它可以成为一种飞行的水果船，将香蕉从种植园运到港口。
statements.english: It can become a flying fruit-boat carrying bananas from the plantations to the ports.

statements.chinese: 巨型气垫船客轮可以横跨大西洋。
statements.english: Giant hovercraft liners could span the Atlantic.

statements.chinese: 而未来的铁路很可能是气垫列车，它以每小时300英里的速度，在气垫上沿单轨行驶，永不触及轨道。
statements.english: And the railways of the future may well be the hover train riding on its air cushion over a single rail which it never touches at speeds up to 300 miles per hour.

statements.chinese: 可能性似乎是无限的。
statements.english: The possibilities appear unlimited.

statements.chinese: 埃贡·拉尔森，《飞马发明家之书》。
statements.english: Egon Larson, the Pegasus Book of Inventors.

courses.title: Lesson 30: Exploring the Sea-Floor
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 13 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 在海底被勘测之前，人们可能如何想象它？
statements.english: How did people probably imagine the sea-floor before it was investigated?

Our knowledge of the oceans a hundred years ago was confined to the two-dimensional shape of the sea surface and the hazards of navigation presented by the irregularities in depth of the shallow water close to the land.
statements.chinese: 一百年前，我们对海洋的了解仅限于海面的二维形状以及陆地附近浅水区深度不规则所带来的航行危险。

statements.english: The open sea was deep and mysterious, and anyone who gave more than a passing thought to the bottom confines of the oceans probably assumed that the sea-bed was flat.
statements.chinese: 开阔的海洋深邃而神秘，任何对海洋底部边界稍加思考的人可能都认为海床是平坦的。

statements.english: Sir James Clark Ross had obtained a sounding of over 2, 400 fathoms in 1839, but it was not until 1869, when H.M.S. Porcupine was put at the disposal of the Royal Society for several cruises that a series of deep soundings was obtained in the Atlantic and the first samples were collected by dredging the bottom.
statements.chinese: 詹姆斯·克拉克·罗斯爵士于1839年测得超过2400噚的深度，但直到1869年，当“豪猪号”军舰被皇家学会征用进行数次航行时，才在大西洋获得了一系列深海探测数据，并通过海底拖网收集了第一批样本。

statements.english: Shortly after this the famous H.M.S. Challenger expedition established the study of the sea-floor as a subject worthy of the most qualified physicists and geologists.
statements.chinese: 此后不久，著名的“挑战者号”军舰远征队确立了海底研究成为值得最合格的物理学家和地质学家研究的课题。

statements.english: A burst of activity associated with the laying of submarine cables soon confirmed the Challenger's observation that many parts of the ocean were two to three miles deep, and the existence of underwater features of considerable magnitude.
statements.chinese: 随之而来的海底电缆铺设热潮很快证实了“挑战者号”的观测结果：海洋许多地方深达两到三英里，并存在着规模巨大的水下特征。

statements.english: Today, enough soundings are available to enable a relief map of the Atlantic to be drawn and we know something of the great variety of the sea bed's topography.
statements.chinese: 如今，已有的测深数据足以绘制出大西洋的浮雕地图，我们对海底地形的巨大多样性有了一定的了解。

statements.english: Since the sea covers the greater part of the earth's surface, it is quite reasonable to regard the sea floor as the basic form of the crust of the earth, with superimposed upon it the continents, together with the islands and other features of the oceans.
statements.chinese: 由于海洋覆盖了地球表面的大部分，将海底视为地壳的基本形态是相当合理的，大陆、以及岛屿和海洋的其他特征都叠加其上。
大陆形成了崎岖不平的高原，它们比开阔海洋的海底高出近三英里。
statements.english: The continents form rugged tablelands which stand nearly three miles above the floor of the open ocean.
From the shore line, out to a distance which may be anywhere from a few miles to a few hundred miles, runs the gentle slope of the continental shelf, geologically part of the continents.
statements.chinese: 从海岸线向外延伸，距离可能从几英里到几百英里不等，是大陆架的平缓斜坡，它在地质学上属于大陆的一部分。
大陆和海洋的真正分界线出现在一个更陡峭的斜坡底部。
statements.english: The real dividing line between continents and oceans occurs at the foot of a steeper slope.
This continental slope usually starts at a place somewhere near the 100-fathom mark and in the course of a few hundred miles reaches the true ocean floor at 2, 500-3, 500 fathoms.
statements.chinese: 这个大陆坡通常始于100噚标记附近的某个地方，并在几百英里的延伸中到达2500-3500噚的真正海底。

statements.english: The slope averages about 1 in 30, but contains steep, probably vertical, cliffs, and gentle sediment-covered terraces, and near its lower reaches there is a long tailing-off which is almost certainly the result of material transported out to deep water after being eroded from the continental masses.
statements.chinese: 该斜坡平均坡度约为1:30，但包含陡峭的、可能是垂直的悬崖，以及平缓的被沉积物覆盖的阶地，在其下部区域，有一个长长的逐渐减缓的坡段，这几乎肯定是由于物质从大陆块体被侵蚀后输送到深水区的结果。

courses.title: Lesson 31: The Sculptor Speaks
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 16 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 要欣赏雕塑，你必须具备什么能力？
statements.english: What do you have to be able to do to appreciate sculpture?

statements.chinese: 欣赏雕塑取决于能够感知三维形态的能力。
statements.english: Appreciation of sculpture depends upon the ability to respond to form in 3 dimensions.

That is perhaps why sculpture has been described as the most difficult of all arts; certainly it is more difficult than the arts which involve appreciation of flat forms, shape in only two dimensions.
statements.chinese: 这也许就是为什么雕塑被描述为所有艺术中最难的；当然，它比那些涉及欣赏平面形态（仅二维形状）的艺术要难。
相比色盲，更多的人是“形盲”。
statements.english: Many more people are 'form-blind' than colour-blind.

statements.chinese: 孩子在学习看东西时，首先只能辨别二维形状；它无法判断距离和深度。
statements.english: The child learning to see, first distinguishes only two-dimensional shape; it cannot judge distances, depths.

statements.chinese: 后来，为了自身的安全和实际需要，它必须培养（部分通过触摸）粗略判断三维距离的能力。
statements.english: Later, for its personal safety and practical needs, it has to develop (partly by means of touch) the ability to judge roughly 3-dimensonal distances.

statements.chinese: 但是，在满足了实际需要的要求之后，大多数人就不会再深入了。
statements.english: But having satisfied the requirements of practical necessity, most people go no further.
Though they may attain considerable accuracy in the perception of flat form, they do not make the further intellectual and emotional effort needed to comprehend form in its full spatial existence.
statements.chinese: 尽管他们可能在感知平面形态方面达到相当高的准确度，但他们不会付出进一步的智力和情感努力，来理解形态的完整空间存在。
这就是雕塑家必须做的事情。
statements.english: This is what the sculptor must do.

statements.chinese: 他必须不断努力思考和运用形态的完整空间性。
statements.english: He must strive continually to think of and use, form in its full spatial completeness.

statements.chinese: 他仿佛将固体形状置于脑中——无论大小，他都将其视作完全握在掌中。
statements.english: He gets the solid shape as it were, inside his head--he thinks of it, whatever its size, as if he were holding it completely enclosed in the hollow of his hand.

He mentally visualizes a complex form from all round itself; he knows while he looks at one side what the other side is like; he identifies himself with its centre of gravity, its mass, its weight; he realizes its volume as the space that the shape displaces in the air.
statements.chinese: 他在脑海中从各个方向观察复杂的形态；当他看一面时，他就知道另一面是什么样子；他将自己与它的重心、质量、重量联系起来；他将它的体积理解为形状在空气中排开的空间。
并且，敏感的雕塑观察者也必须学会将形状单纯地感受为形状，而不是描述或回忆。
statements.english: And the sensitive observer of sculpture must also learn to feel shape simply as shape, not as description or reminiscence.
He must, for example, perceive an egg as a simple single solid shape quite apart from its significance as food, or from the literary idea that it will become a bird.
statements.chinese: 例如，他必须将一个鸡蛋视为一个简单、单一的固体形状，完全脱离它作为食物的意义，或脱离它会变成一只鸟的文学观念。

statements.english: And so with solids such as a shell, a nut, a plum, a pear, a tadpole, a mushroom, a mountain peak, a kidney, a carrot, a tree-trunk, a bird, a bud, a lark, a ladybird, a bulrush, a bone.
statements.chinese: 对于诸如贝壳、坚果、李子、梨、蝌蚪、蘑菇、山峰、肾脏、胡萝卜、树干、鸟、花蕾、百灵鸟、瓢虫、香蒲、骨头等固体也是如此。
从这些事物中，他可以进一步欣赏更复杂的形态或多种形态的组合。
statements.english: From these he can go on to appreciate more complex forms or combinations of several forms.

courses.title: Lesson 32: Galileo Reborn
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 14 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 近年来，是什么改变了我们对伽利略的传统看法？
statements.english: What has modified our traditional view of Galileo in recent times?

In his own lifetime Galileo was the centre of violent controversy, but the scientific dust has long since settled, and today we can see even his famous clash with the Inquisition in something like its proper perspective.
statements.chinese: 伽利略在他有生之年一直处于剧烈争议的中心，但科学上的尘埃早已落定，今天我们甚至可以用一种恰当的视角来看待他与宗教裁判所的著名冲突。
然而，与此相反，只是到了现代，伽利略才成了科学史家们的一个难题。
statements.english: But, in contrast, it is only in modern times that Galileo has become a problem child for historians of science.

statements.chinese: 对伽利略的旧观点是简单明了的。
statements.english: The old view of Galileo was delightfully uncomplicated.

He was, above all, a man who experimented: who despised the prejudice and book learning of the Aristotelians, who put his questions to nature instead of to the ancients, and who drew his conclusions fearlessly.
statements.chinese: 首先，他是一个实验家：他鄙视亚里士多德学派的偏见和书本知识，他向自然而不是向古人提问，并无所畏惧地得出结论。

statements.english: He had been the first to turn a telescope to the sky, and he had seen there evidence enough to overthrow Aristotle and Ptolemy together.
statements.chinese: 他是第一个把望远镜对准天空的人，他在那里看到了足以推翻亚里士多德和托勒密的证据。

statements.english: He was the man who climbed the Leaning Tower of Pisa and dropped various weights from the top, who rolled balls down inclined planes, and then generalized the results of his many experiments into the famous law of free fall.
statements.chinese: 他曾登上比萨斜塔，从塔顶扔下各种重量的物体，他曾将球滚下斜面，然后将其众多实验的结果概括为著名的自由落体定律。

statements.english: But a closer study of the evidence, supported by a deeper sense of the period, and particularly by a new consciousness of the philosophical undercurrents in the scientific revolution, has profoundly modified this view of Galileo.
statements.chinese: 然而，对证据的更深入研究，加上对那个时代更深刻的理解，特别是对科学革命中哲学暗流的新认识，已经深刻地修正了对伽利略的这一看法。

statements.english: Today, although the old Galileo lives on in many popular writings, among historians of science a new and more sophisticated picture has emerged.
statements.chinese: 如今，尽管旧的伽利略形象依然存在于许多流行著作中，但在科学史家之间，一个更复杂、更精密的形象已经出现。
同时，我们对伽利略反对者的同情也有所增加。
statements.english: At the same time our sympathy for Galileo's opponents has grown somewhat.

His telescopic observations are justly immortal; they aroused great interest at the time, they had important theoretical consequences, and they provided a striking demonstration of the potentialities hidden in instruments and apparatus.
statements.chinese: 他的望远镜观测是理所当然的不朽之举；它们在当时引起了巨大的兴趣，它们产生了重要的理论结果，它们有力地展示了仪器和设备中蕴藏的潜力。

statements.english: But can we blame those who looked and failed to see what Galileo saw, if we remember that to use a telescope at the limit of its powers calls for long experience and intimate familiarity with one's instrument?
statements.chinese: 但是，我们能责怪那些看了却没看到伽利略所见之人吗，如果我们考虑到要充分利用望远镜的极限功能需要长时间的经验和对仪器的深入熟悉？

statements.english: Was the philosopher who refused to look through Galileo's telescope more culpable than those who alleged that the spiral nebulae observed with Lord Rosse's great telescope in the 1840s were scratches left by the grinder?
statements.chinese: 那些拒绝通过伽利略的望远镜观察的哲学家，是否比那些声称19世纪40年代用罗斯勋爵的大望远镜观察到的螺旋星云是研磨器留下的划痕的人更应受到谴责呢？

statements.english: We can perhaps forgive those who said the moons of Jupiter were produced by Galileo's spyglass if we recall that in his day, as for centuries before, curved glass was the popular contrivance for producing not truth but illusion, untruth; and if a single curved glass would distort nature, how much more would a pair of them?
statements.chinese: 我们或许可以原谅那些说木星卫星是伽利略的望远镜制造出来的人，如果我们回想起在他那个时代，就像几个世纪以前一样，曲面玻璃是制造幻觉、谎言而非真相的流行手段；那么，如果一块曲面玻璃会扭曲自然，两块又会怎样呢？

courses.title: Lesson 33: Education
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 18 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 为什么在没有书籍的部落社会中，教育是民主的？
statements.english: Why is education democratic in bookless tribal societies?

statements.chinese: 教育是我们这个时代的一个关键词。
statements.english: Education is one of the key words of our time.
A man without an education, many of us believe, is an unfortunate victim of adverse circumstances, deprived of one of the greatest twentieth-century opportunities.
statements.chinese: 许多人认为，一个没有受过教育的人是不幸境遇的受害者，被剥夺了20世纪最伟大的机会之一。

statements.english: Convinced of the importance of education, modern states 'invest' in institutions of learning to get back 'interest' in the form of a large group of enlightened young men and women who are potential leaders.
statements.chinese: 现代国家深信教育的重要性，因此“投资”于学习机构，以期“回报”一大批开明的青年男女，他们是潜在的领导者。

statements.english: Education, with its cycles of instruction so carefully worked out, punctuated by textbooks--those purchasable wells of wisdom--what would civilization be like without its benefits?
statements.chinese: 教育，有着精心设计的教学周期，以教科书——那些可以购买的智慧源泉——作为点缀，如果没有它的益处，文明会是什么样子？

statements.english: So much is certain: that we would have doctors and preachers, lawyers and defendants marriages and births--but our spiritual outlook would be different.
statements.chinese: 有一点是肯定的：我们会有医生和传教士，律师和被告，婚姻和生育——但我们的精神观念会大相径庭。

statements.english: We would lay less stress on 'facts and figures' and more on a good memory, on applied psychology, and on the capacity of a man to get along with his fellow-citizens.
statements.chinese: 我们会更少强调“事实和数据”，而更多地关注良好的记忆力，关注应用心理学，以及一个人与同胞和睦相处的能力。
如果我们的教育体系仿效其没有书籍的过去，我们就会拥有 imaginable 最民主的“大学”形式。
statements.english: If our educational system were fashioned after its bookless past we would have the most democratic form of 'college' imaginable.
Among tribal people all knowledge inherited by tradition is shared by all; it is taught to every member of the tribe so that in this respect everybody is equally equipped for life.
statements.chinese: 在部落民族中，所有通过传统继承的知识都由所有人共享；它被传授给部落的每一个成员，因此在这方面，每个人都同样具备了生活的能力。
这是“平等起步”的理想条件，只有我们最进步的现代教育形式才试图重新获得。
statements.english: It is the ideal condition of the 'equal start' which only our most progressive forms of modern education try to regain.

statements.chinese: 在原始文化中，寻求和接受传统教育的义务对所有人都有约束力。
statements.english: In primitive cultures the obligation to seek and to receive the traditional instruction is binding to all.

There are no'illiterates' --if the term can be applied to peoples without a script--while our own compulsory school attendance became law in Germany in 1642, in France in 1806, and in England in 1876 and is still nonexistent in a number of 'civilized' nations.
statements.chinese: 没有“文盲”——如果这个词可以用来指没有文字的民族的话——而我们自己的义务入学制度于1642年在德国成为法律，1806年在法国，1876年在英国，并且在一些“文明”国家仍然不存在。

statements.english: This shows how long it was before we deemed it necessary to make sure that all our children could share in the knowledge accumulated by the 'happy few' during the past centuries.
statements.chinese: 这表明我们花了多长时间才认为有必要确保我们的所有孩子都能分享过去几个世纪由“少数幸运儿”积累的知识。
荒野中的教育并非金钱问题。
statements.english: Education in the wilderness is not a matter of monetary means.

statements.chinese: 所有人都有权获得平等的起步。
statements.english: All are entitled to an equal start.

statements.chinese: 那里没有我们社会中常常阻碍一个成长中的人格充分发展的匆忙。
statements.english: There is none of the hurry which, in our society, often hampers the full development of a growing personality.
There, a child grows up under the everpresent attention of his parents; therefore the jungles and the savannahs know of no 'juvenile delinquency'.
statements.chinese: 在那里，孩子在父母无时无刻的关怀下成长；因此，丛林和热带草原上没有“青少年犯罪”。
没有离家谋生的必要导致儿童被忽视，也没有父亲面临无法为孩子“购买”教育的困境。
statements.english: No necessity of making a living away from home results in neglect of children, and no father is confronted with his inability to 'buy' an education for his child.

courses.title: Lesson 34: Adolescence
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 14 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 青少年尊重父母什么？
statements.english: What do adolescents respect in parents?

Parents are often upset when their children praise the homes of their friends and regard it as a slur on their own cooking, or cleaning, or furniture, and often are foolish enough to let the adolescents see that they are annoyed.
statements.chinese: 当孩子们赞美朋友家，并将其视为对自己烹饪、清洁或家具的诋毁时，父母常常感到不安，并且常常愚蠢到让青少年看出他们很恼火。
他们甚至可能指责孩子们不忠，或者对朋友的父母说些恶毒的话。
statements.english: They may even accuse them of disloyalty, or make some spiteful remark about the friends' parents.

Such a loss of dignity and descent into childish behaviour on the part of the adults deeply shocks the adolescents, and makes them resolve that in future they will not talk to their parents about the places or people they visit.
statements.chinese: 这种成年人丧失尊严、行为幼稚的举动深深地震惊了青少年，并使他们决心将来不再和父母谈论他们去过的地方或见过的人。

statements.english: Before very long the parents will be complaining that the child is so secretive and never tells them anything, but they seldom realize that they have brought this on themselves.
statements.chinese: 不久之后，父母就会抱怨孩子如此守口如瓶，从不告诉他们任何事情，但他们很少意识到这是他们自找的。

statements.english: Disillusionment with the parents, however good and adequate they may be both as parents and as individuals, is to some degree inevitable.
statements.chinese: 对父母的幻灭，无论他们作为父母和个人有多么优秀和称职，在某种程度上都是不可避免的。

statements.english: Most children have such a high ideal of their parents, unless the parents themselves have been unsatisfactory, that it can hardly hope to stand up to a realistic evaluation.
statements.chinese: 大多数孩子对父母抱有如此高的期望，除非父母本身表现不尽人意，否则这种期望几乎不可能经受住现实的评估。

statements.english: Parents would be greatly surprised and deeply touched if they realized how much belief their children usually have in their character and infallibility, and how much this faith means to a child.
statements.chinese: 如果父母意识到孩子们通常对他们的品格和不犯错抱有多大的信念，他们会大吃一惊并深受感动，以及这种信念对一个孩子意味着什么。

statements.english: If parents were prepared for this adolescent reaction, and realized that was a sign that the child was growing up and developing valuable powers of observation and independent judgment, they would not be so hurt, and therefore would not drive the child into opposition by resenting and resisting it.
statements.chinese: 如果父母对这种青春期反应有所准备，并且意识到这是孩子正在成长并发展出宝贵的观察力和独立判断力的迹象，他们就不会那么受伤，因此也不会因为怨恨和抵制而把孩子推向对立面。

statements.english: The adolescent, with his passion for sincerity, always respects a parent who admits that he is wrong, or ignorant, or even that he has been unfair or unjust.
statements.chinese: 青少年，怀着对真诚的热情，总是尊重承认自己错了、无知，甚至不公平或不公正的父母。
孩子不能原谅的是，如果孩子知道这些指控是真的，父母却拒绝承认。
statements.english: What the child cannot forgive is the parents' refusal to admit these charges if the child knows them to be true.

Victorian parents believed that they kept their dignity by retreating behind an unreasoning authoritarian attitude in fact they did nothing of the kind, but children were then too cowed to let them know how they really felt.
statements.chinese: 维多利亚时代的父母认为，通过退缩到一种不讲道理的专制态度背后，他们能保持自己的尊严，事实上他们根本没有这样做，但那时的孩子过于害怕，不敢让他们知道自己真实感受。

statements.english: Today we tend to go to the other extreme, but on the whole this is a healthier attitude both for the child and the parent.
statements.chinese: 今天我们倾向于走向另一个极端，但总的来说，这对孩子和父母都是一种更健康的态度。
面对现实总是更明智和更安全的，无论当下它可能多么痛苦。
statements.english: It is always wiser and safer to face up to reality, however painful it may be at the moment.

courses.title: Lesson 35: Space Odyssey
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 19 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 我们什么时候才能认真考虑在火星上殖民？
statements.english: When will it be possible for us to think seriously about colonising Mars?
The Moon is likely to become the industrial hub of the Solar System supplying the rocket fuels for its ships, easily obtainable from the lunar rocks in the form of liquid oxygen.
statements.chinese: 月球很可能成为太阳系的工业中心，为其飞船提供火箭燃料，这些燃料以液氧的形式，可轻易地从月球岩石中获得。
原因在于它的重力。
statements.english: The reason lies in its gravity.

Because the Moon has only an eightieth of the Earth's mass, it requires 97% less energy to travel the quarter of a million miles from the Moon to Earth-orbit than the 200 mile-journey from Earth's surface into orbit!
statements.chinese: 因为月球的质量只有地球的八十分之一，它所需的能量要少97%，即使是从月球到地球轨道25万英里的旅程，也比从地球表面进入轨道200英里的旅程所需的能量少得多！
这听起来可能很不可思议，但它很容易计算出来。
statements.english: This may sound fantastic, but it is easily calculated.

statements.chinese: 要乘坐火箭逃离地球，必须以每秒7英里的速度飞行。
statements.english: To escape from the Earth in a rocket, one must travel at seven miles per second.

statements.chinese: 而从月球逃离的可比速度仅为每秒1.5英里。
statements.english: The comparable speed from the Moon is only 1.5 miles per second.

Because the gravity on the Moon's surface is only a sixth of Earth's (remember how easily the Apollo astronauts bounded along), it takes much less energy to accelerate to that 1.5mps than it does on Earth.
statements.chinese: 因为月球表面的重力只有地球的六分之一（还记得阿波罗宇航员在月球上跳跃得多轻松吗？），因此，在月球上加速到每秒1.5英里所需的能量比在地球上少得多。
月球居民将能够以其地球表亲进行类似旅程所需成本的3%在太空中飞行。
statements.english: Moon dwellers will be able to fly in space at only three percent of the cost of similar journeys by their terrestrial cousins.
Arthur C.Clark once suggested a revolutionary idea passes through three phases: 1. 'It's impossible--don't waste my time.'
statements.chinese: 亚瑟·C·克拉克曾提出，一个革命性的想法会经历三个阶段：1. “这不可能——别浪费我的时间。”
2. “这有可能，但不值得做。”
statements.english: 2. 'It's possible, but not worth doing.'

statements.chinese: 3. “我一直都说这是个好主意。”
statements.english: 3. 'I said it was a good idea all along.'

The idea of colonising Mars--a world 160 times more distant than the Moon--will move decisively from the second phase to the third, when a significant number of people are living permanently in space.
statements.chinese: 殖民火星——一个比月球远160倍的世界——的设想，将决定性地从第二阶段迈向第三阶段，那将是当大量人口永久居住在太空中的时候。
火星对未来的航海家们有着非凡的吸引力。
statements.english: Mars has an extraordinary fascination for would-be voyagers.

statements.chinese: 美国、俄罗斯和欧洲都充满了热情的人士——其中许多是认真而资深的科学家，他们梦想着将人类送上火星。
statements.english: America, Russia and Europe are filled with enthusiasts--many of them serious and senior scientists who dream of sending people to it.

statements.chinese: 他们的目标是可以理解的。
statements.english: Their aim is understandable.

statements.chinese: 它是太阳系中与地球最相似的星球。
statements.english: It is the one world in the Solar System that is most like the Earth.

It is a world of red sandy deserts (hence its name--the Red Planet), cloudless skies, savage sandstorms, chasms wider than the Grand Canyon and at least one mountain more than twice as tall as Everest.
statements.chinese: 这是一个红色的沙质沙漠世界（因此得名——红色星球），有着无云的天空、狂暴的沙尘暴、比大峡谷还宽的裂谷，以及至少一座比珠穆朗玛峰高两倍多的山峰。
它似乎非常适合居住。
statements.english: It seems ideal for settlement.

courses.title: Lesson 36: The Cost of Government
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 18 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 无论在政府还是企业中，降低运营成本最重要的因素是什么？
statements.english: What's the most important factor, both in government or business, for keeping running costs low?

statements.chinese: 如果一个国家本质上是分裂的，就只能由政府来维系它的统一。
statements.english: If a nation is essentialy disunited, it is left to the government to hold it together.

statements.chinese: 这增加了政府开支，并相应减少了可用于国家发展的经济资源。
statements.english: This increases the expense of government, and reduces correspondingly the amount of economic resources that could be used for developing the country.

statements.chinese: 而且不应忘记，在一个贫穷落后的国家，这些资源是多么微薄。
statements.english: And it should not be forgotten how small those resources are in a poor and backward country.

statements.chinese: 政府开支高的地方，发展资源也相应地少。
statements.english: Where the cost of government is high, resources for development are correspondingly low.

statements.chinese: 这可以通过比较一个国家与一个私营企业的情况来说明。
statements.english: This may be illustrated by comparing the position of a nation with that of a private business enterprise.

statements.chinese: 一个企业为了维持经营，必须承担一定的成本和开支。
statements.english: An enterprise has to incur certain costs and expenses in order to stay in business.

statements.chinese: 就我们的目的而言，我们只关注一种成本——管理和经营企业的成本。
statements.english: For our purposes, we are concerned only with one kind of cost--the cost of managing and administering the business.

statements.chinese: 企业中的此类行政管理费用类似于一个国家中的政府开支。
statements.english: Such administrative overheads in a business are analogous to the cost of government in a nation.
The administrative overheads of a business are low to the extent that everyone working in the business can be trusted to behave in a way that best promotes the interests of the firm.
statements.chinese: 企业的行政管理费用之所以低，是因为企业中的每个人都可以被信任，以最有利于公司利益的方式行事。

statements.english: If they can each be trusted to take such responsibilities, and to exercise such initiative as falls within their sphere, then administrative overheads will be low.
statements.chinese: 如果每个人都可以被信任来承担这些责任，并在其职责范围内发挥主动性，那么行政管理费用就会很低。

statements.english: It will be low because it will be necessary to have only one man looking after each job without having another man to check upon what he is doing, keep him in line, and report on him to someone else.
statements.chinese: 之所以低，是因为只需要一个人负责一项工作，而不需要另一个人来检查他正在做什么，约束他，并向其他人汇报他的情况。

statements.english: But if no one can be trusted to act in a loyal and responsible manner towards his job, then the business will require armies of administrators, checkers and foremen and administrative overheads will rise correspondingly.
statements.chinese: 但如果没人能被信任以忠诚负责的态度对待自己的工作，那么企业将需要大量的管理人员、检查员和工头，行政管理费用也将相应地增加。

statements.english: As administrative overheads rise, so the earnings of the business after meeting the expense of administration, will fall; and the business will have less money to distribute as dividends or invest directly in its future progress and development.
statements.chinese: 随着行政管理费用的增加，企业在支付行政开支后的收益将下降；企业将没有足够的资金来分配股息，或直接投资于其未来的发展。
一个国家也是如此。
statements.english: It is precisely the same with a nation.
To the extent that the people can be relied on to behave in a loyal and responsible manner, the government does not require armies of police and civil servants to keep them in order.
statements.chinese: 只要人民能够被信任以忠诚负责的方式行事，政府就不需要大批警察和公务员来维持秩序。

statements.english: But if a nation is disunited, the government cannot be sure that the actions of the people will be in the interests of the nation; and it will have to watch, check, and control the people accordingly.
statements.chinese: 但如果一个国家是分裂的，政府就不能确定人民的行为是否符合国家利益；它就必须相应地监视、检查和控制人民。
因此，一个分裂的国家必然会产生过高的政府开支。
statements.english: A disunited nation therefore has to incur unduly high costs of government.

courses.title: Lesson 37: The Process of Ageing
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 19 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 随着年龄的增长，我们对自己最不愉快的发现之一是什么？
statements.english: What is one of the most unpleasant discoveries we make about ourselves as we get older?

statements.chinese: 在十二岁时，人体处于最旺盛的状态。
statements.english: At the age of twelve years, the human body is at its most vigorous.

statements.chinese: 它尚未达到完全的体型和力量，其主人也尚未达到完全的智力：但在此时，死亡的可能性最小。
statements.english: It has yet to reach its full size and strength, and its owner his or her full intelligence: but at this age the likelihood of death is least.

Earlier, we were infants and young children, and consequently more vulnerable; later, we shall undergo a progressive loss of our vigour and resistance which, though imperceptible at first will finally become so steep that we can live no longer, however well we look after ourselves, and however well society, and our doctors, look after us.
statements.chinese: 早些时候，我们是婴儿和幼儿，因此更容易受到伤害；之后，我们将经历活力和抵抗力的逐渐丧失，这起初虽然难以察觉，但最终会变得如此迅速，以至于我们无法再活下去，无论我们如何精心照顾自己，也无论社会和医生如何精心照顾我们。
随着时间的推移，这种活力的衰退被称为衰老。
statements.english: This decline in vigour with the passing of time is called ageing.

It is one of the most unpleasant discoveries which we all make that we must decline in this way, that if we escape wars, accidents and diseases we shall eventually 'die of old age', and that this happens at a rate which differs little from person to person, so that there are heavy odds in favour of our dying between the ages of 65 and 80.
statements.chinese: 我们都发现了一个最令人不快的现实，那就是我们必然会以这种方式衰老，如果我们能够幸免于战争、事故和疾病，最终我们将“老死”，而且这个过程的速度人与人之间差异很小，因此，我们很可能在65到80岁之间去世。
我们中有些人会更早去世，少数人会活得更久——进入第九或第十个十年。
statements.english: Some of us will die sooner, a few will live longer -- on into a ninth or tenth decade.
But the chances are against it, and there is a virtual limit on how long we can hope to remain alive, however lucky and robust we are.
statements.chinese: 但这种机会渺茫，而且我们能期望活多久，无论我们多么幸运和健壮，都有一个实际的限制。
除非被提醒，否则常人往往会忘记这个过程。
statements.english: Normal people tend to forget this process unless and until they are reminded of it.

We are so familiar with the fact that man ages, that people have for years assumed that the process of losing vigour with time, of becoming more likely to die the older we get, was something self-evident like the cooling of a hot kettle or the wearing-out of a pair of shoes.
statements.chinese: 我们对人会衰老这一事实非常熟悉，以至于人们多年来一直认为，随着时间流逝而失去活力，年纪越大越可能死亡的过程，是理所当然的事情，就像热水壶变凉或鞋子磨损一样。

statements.english: They have also assumed that all animals, and probably other organisms such as trees, or even the universe itself, must in the nature of things 'wear out'.
statements.chinese: 他们还假设所有动物，以及其他生物，如树木，甚至宇宙本身，按照事物的本性都必然会“耗尽”。

statements.english: Most animals we commonly observe do in fact age as we do, if given the chance to live long enough; and mechanical systems like a wound watch, or the sun, do in fact run out of energy in accordance with the second law of thermodynamics (whether the whole universe does so is a moot point at present).
statements.chinese: 我们通常观察到的大多数动物，如果活得足够长，确实会像我们一样衰老；而像上弦的钟表或太阳这样的机械系统，确实会根据热力学第二定律耗尽能量（整个宇宙是否如此，目前尚无定论）。
但这些与人类衰老时发生的情况并不相似。
statements.english: But these are not analogous to what happens when man ages.

statements.chinese: 一只停走的表仍然是一只表，可以重新上弦。
statements.english: A run-down watch is still a watch and can be rewound.

statements.chinese: 相比之下，一只旧表会变得磨损不堪，不可靠，最终不值得修理。
statements.english: An old watch, by contrast, becomes so worn and unreliable that it eventually is not worth mending.

statements.chinese: 但是表永远无法自我修复——它不包含活体部分，只有金属，金属会因摩擦而磨损。
statements.english: But a watch could never repair itself--it does not consist of living parts, only of metal, which wears away by friction.

statements.chinese: 我们曾经能够自我修复——至少足以克服除了最即刻致命的疾病和事故之外的所有情况。
statements.english: We could, at one time, repair ourselves--well enough, at least, to overcome all but the most instantly fatal illnesses and accidents.
Between twelve and eighty years we gradually lose this power; an illness which at 12 would knock us over, at 80 can knock us out, and into our grave.
statements.chinese: 在十二岁到八十岁之间，我们逐渐失去这种能力；一种在12岁时会让我们病倒的疾病，在80岁时可能就会让我们倒下，并送入坟墓。

statements.english: If we could stay as vigorous as we are at twelve, it would take about 700 years for half of us to die, and another 700 for the survivors to be reduced by half again.
statements.chinese: 如果我们能像十二岁时那样充满活力，大约需要700年我们中一半的人才会去世，再过700年，幸存者数量才会再次减少一半。

courses.title: Lesson 38: Water and the Traveller
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 22 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 雕塑的欣赏取决于在三维空间中对形态做出反应的能力。
statements.english: Appreciation of sculpture depends upon the ability to respond to form in three dimensions.

statements.chinese: 这也许就是为什么雕塑被描述为所有艺术中最难的一种。
statements.english: That is perhaps why sculpture has been described as the most difficult of all arts.
Certainly, it is more difficult than the arts which involve appreciation of flat forms, shape in only two dimensions.
statements.chinese: 当然，它比涉及欣赏平面形态的艺术更难，只有二维的形状。
更多的人是形盲而不是色盲。
statements.english: Many more people are form blind than color blind.

statements.chinese: 学习看东西的孩子首先只能区分二维形状。
statements.english: The child learning to see first distinguishes only two-dimensional shape.

statements.chinese: 它无法判断距离、深度。
statements.english: It cannot judge distances, depths.
Later, for its personal safety and practical needs, it has to develop, partly by means of touch, the ability to judge roughly three-dimensional distances.
statements.chinese: 后来，为了自身的安全和实际需求，它必须发展，部分通过触摸，判断大致三维距离的能力。
但是，在满足了实际需求的条件后，大多数人就不再深入了。
statements.english: But having satisfied the requirement of practical necessity, most people go no further.
Though they may attain considerable accuracy in the perception of flat form, they do not make the further intellectual and emotional effort needed to comprehend form in its full spatial existence.
statements.chinese: 尽管他们可能在平面形态的感知上达到相当高的准确性，但他们没有付出进一步的智力和情感努力来理解其完整空间存在的形态。
这就是雕塑家必须做的。
statements.english: This is what the sculptor must do.

statements.chinese: 他必须不断努力思考和运用其完整空间性的形态。
statements.english: He must strive continually to think of and use form in its full spatial completeness.

statements.chinese: 他仿佛在脑海中获得了立体的形状。
statements.english: He gets the solid shape, as it were, inside his head.

statements.chinese: 他思考它，无论其大小，就好像他把它完全握在他的手掌中一样。
statements.english: He thinks of it, whatever its size, as if he were holding it completely enclosed in the hollow of his hand.

statements.chinese: 他在脑海中从各个角度构想出一个复杂的形态。
statements.english: He mentally visualizes a complex form from all around itself.

statements.chinese: 他知道，当他看着一面时，另一面是什么样子。
statements.english: He knows, while he looks at one side, what the other side is like.

statements.chinese: 他将自己与它的重心、它的质量、它的重量联系起来。
statements.english: He identifies himself with its center of gravity, its mass, its weight.
He realizes its volume, as the space that the shape displaces in the air.
statements.chinese: 他认识到它的体积，即形状在空气中排开的空间。

statements.english: And the sensitive observer of sculpture must also learn to feel shape simply as shape, not as description or reminiscence.
statements.chinese: 而敏感的雕塑观察者也必须学会将形状简单地感受为形状，而不是描述或回忆。

statements.english: He must, for example, perceive an egg as a simple, single, solid shape, quite apart from its significance as food, or from the literary idea that it will become a bird.
statements.chinese: 例如，他必须将一个鸡蛋视为一个简单、单一的立体形状，完全不考虑它作为食物的意义，也不考虑它会变成一只鸟的文学想象。

statements.english: And so with solids such as a shell, a nut, a plum, a pear, a tadpole, a mushroom, a mountain peak, a kidney, a carrot, a tree trunk, a bird, a bud, a lark, a ladybird, a bulrush, a bone.
statements.chinese: 对于诸如贝壳、坚果、李子、梨、蝌蚪、蘑菇、山峰、肾脏、胡萝卜、树干、鸟、芽、云雀、瓢虫、香蒲、骨头。
从这些，他可以进而欣赏更复杂的形态，或多种形态的组合。
statements.english: From these he can go on to appreciate more complex forms, or combinations of several forms.
Henry Moore The sculptor speaks From The Listener.
statements.chinese: 亨利·摩尔雕塑家说选自《听众》。

courses.title: Lesson 39: What Every Writer Wants
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 21 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 维多利亚时代的人们意识到，人类最大的幸福莫过于拥有一桩幸福的婚姻，因此他们竭力假装自己的所有婚姻都是幸福的。
statements.english: The Victorians, realizing that the greatest happiness accorded to man, is that provided by a happy marriage, endeavoured to pretend that all their marriages were happy.

We for our part, admitting the fact that no feat of intelligence and character is so exacting as that required of two people who desire to live permanently together on a basis of amity, are obsessed by the problem of how to render the basic facts of cohabitation simpler and more reasonable, in order that unhappy marriages may less frequently result.
statements.chinese: 而我们，则承认这样一个事实：没有任何一项智力和性格上的壮举，比两个人希望在友好的基础上永久地生活在一起所要求的更为严苛，我们为如何使共同生活的根本事实变得更简单、更合理而烦恼不已，以便减少不幸婚姻的发生。
如果有人指出每十桩婚姻中只有四桩不是被迫的奴役，维多利亚时代的人们会觉得这既痛苦又令人不快。
statements.english: The Victorians would have considered it painful or unpleasant, were one to point out that only four marriages out of every ten are anything but forced servitudes.

statements.chinese: 我们自己正是从这一假设出发，并试图在此基础上建立一种更明智的两性关系理论。
statements.english: We ourselves start from this very assumption, and try to build from it a theory of more sensible relations between the sexes.

statements.chinese: 在所有彻头彻尾的不诚实形式中，维多利亚时代的乐观主义在我看来是最懦弱、也最具破坏性的。
statements.english: Of all forms of arrant untruthfulness, Victorian optimism appears to me to have been the most cowardly and the most damaging.

statements.chinese: 因此，真相是一种心智态度。
statements.english: Truth therefore, is an attitude of the mind.

statements.chinese: 如果一个人不想给朋友带来不便或让他们感到厌烦，那么不说谎是很重要的。
statements.english: It's important if one does not wish to inconvenience and to bore one's friends, not to tell lies.

statements.chinese: 但更重要的是不要谎想，不要陷入那些机械化且不真实的思维习惯，它们如此令人愉悦和轻松，以至于让人陷入心智上的迟钝。
statements.english: But it's more important not to think lies or to slide into those mechanical and untruthful habits of thought, which are so pleasant and so easy as to sense to mental ineptitude.

statements.chinese: 维多利亚时代的心智习惯——我认为那是一种糟糕的心智习惯——过分专注于社会和道德上便利的事物。
statements.english: The Victorian habit of mind, which I consider to have been a bad habit of mind, were unduly preoccupied by what was socially and morally convenient.

statements.chinese: 然而，便利在生活中的所有事务中，都是一个糟糕的价值衡量标准。
statements.english: Convenience is however, in all affairs of life, an execrable test of value.

statements.chinese: 一个人应该有勇气去思考令人不舒服的事情，因为只有拒绝便利，才能思考出真相。
statements.english: One should have the courage to think uncomfortably, since it is only by rejecting the convenience that one can come to think the truth.

statements.chinese: 毕竟，并非有什么东西是绝对的真相。
statements.english: Not after all that there is any such thing as truth.

statements.chinese: 充其量，我们只能接近某种相对的近似值。
statements.english: At best we can approach to some relative approximation.

statements.chinese: 另一方面，谎言无疑是存在的。
statements.english: On the other hand there is surely such a thing as untruth.

statements.chinese: 当一个人说了一些话或做了某些事，给他人留下与事实不符的印象时，他通常是心知肚明的。
statements.english: One is generally aware when one has said something or acted in some way, which has left on other people an impression not strictly in accordance with the facts.

statements.chinese: 当一个人抛开一个不便的念头，转而代之以另一个更方便的念头时，他也通常是心知肚明的。
statements.english: One is generally aware also when one has thrust aside an inconvenient thought and slid into its place another thought which is convenient.

statements.chinese: 在前一种情况下，一个人的意识通常比后一种情况更敏锐，因为我们更警惕自己说出的谎言，而不是仅仅在心里想的谎言。
statements.english: One's awareness in the former case is in general more acute than in the latter, since we are more on the lookout for the lies we utter than for those we merely think.

statements.chinese: 然而，事实上，不诚实的思想在两者中更为恶劣。
statements.english: In fact, however, it is the untruthful thought which is the more vicious of the two.

statements.chinese: 说出来的谎言总是令人厌烦，而且实际上可能是不诚实的。
statements.english: Spoken lies are invariably tiresome and may actually be dishonest.

statements.chinese: 然而，持续的心思谎言——一种盎格鲁-撒克逊人特别容易患上的疾病——预示着人类思想和品格的毁灭。
statements.english: But continuous lying in the mind, a disease to which the Anglo-Saxon is peculiarly exposed, spells the destruction of human thought and character.

statements.chinese: 哈罗德·尼科尔森，《论说真话》，选自《闲谈》。
statements.english: Harold Nicolson, On Telling the Truth, from Small Talk.

courses.title: Lesson 40: Waves
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 19 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 寄语 39。
statements.english: Message 39.

statements.chinese: 在伽利略生前，他一直是激烈争议的中心。
statements.english: In his own lifetime, Galileo was the center of violent controversy.
The scientific dust has long since settled, and today, we can see even his famous clash with the Inquisition in something like its proper perspective.
statements.chinese: 科学的尘埃早已落定，如今，即使是他与宗教裁判所的著名冲突，我们也能从一个恰当的角度来看待。
但相比之下，直到近代，伽利略才成为科学史学家眼中的“问题儿童”。
statements.english: But in contrast, it's only in modern times that Galileo has become a problem child for historians in science.

statements.chinese: 过去对伽利略的看法非常简单。
statements.english: The old view of Galileo was delightfully uncomplicated.

He was, above all, a man who experimented, who despised the prejudices and book-learning of the Aristotelians, who put his questions to nature instead of to the ancients, and who drew his conclusions fearlessly.
statements.chinese: 他首先是一位实验者，蔑视亚里士多德学派的偏见和书本知识，他向自然而不是向古人提出问题，并无畏地得出自己的结论。
他是第一个将望远镜对准天空的人，并在那里看到了足以同时推翻亚里士多德和托勒密的证据。
statements.english: He had been the first to turn a telescope to the sky, and he had seen there evidence enough to overthrow Aristotle and Ptolemy together.

He was the man who climbed the leaning tower of Pisa and dropped various weights from the top, who rolled balls down inclined planes, and then generalized the results of his many experiments into the famous law of free fall.
statements.chinese: 他曾爬上比萨斜塔，从塔顶扔下不同的重物，他曾让球从斜面滚下，然后将他众多实验的结果概括为著名的自由落体定律。
然而，对证据更深入的研究，加上对那个时代更深刻的理解，特别是对科学革命中哲学暗流的新认识，深刻地改变了对伽利略的看法。
statements.english: But a closer study of the evidence, supported by a deeper sense of the period and particularly by a new consciousness of the philosophical undercurrents in the scientific revolution, has profoundly modified this view of Galileo.

statements.chinese: 如今，尽管旧有的伽利略形象仍在许多流行著作中流传，但在科学史学家中，一个全新且更复杂的形象已经浮现。
statements.english: Today, although the old Galileo lives on in many popular writings, among historians of science, a new and more sophisticated picture has emerged.

statements.chinese: 与此同时，我们对伽利略的反对者的同情也有所增加。
statements.english: At the same time, our sympathy for Galileo's opponents has grown somewhat.

statements.chinese: 他的望远镜观测理应永垂不朽。
statements.english: His telescopic observations are justly immortal.

statements.chinese: 它们在当时引起了巨大兴趣，具有重要的理论意义，并有力地展示了仪器和设备中蕴藏的潜力。
statements.english: They aroused great interest at the time, they had important theoretical consequences, and they provided a striking demonstration of the potentialities hidden in instruments and apparatus.

statements.chinese: 但是，我们能责怪那些观察了却未能看到伽利略所见之人吗？
statements.english: But can we blame those who looked and failed to see what Galileo saw?

statements.chinese: 如果我们记住，要在望远镜的极限性能下使用它，需要长期的经验以及对仪器的深入了解。
statements.english: if we remember that to use a telescope at the limit of its powers calls for long experience and intimate familiarity with one's instrument.

statements.chinese: 拒绝透过伽利略望远镜观察的哲学家，是否比那些声称19世纪40年代用罗斯勋爵的巨型望远镜观测到的螺旋星云是研磨师留下的划痕的人，更应受责备？
statements.english: Was the philosopher who refused to look through Galileo's telescope more culpable than those who alleged that the spiral nebulae observed with Lord Rosse's great telescope in the 1840s were scratches left by the grinder?

We can perhaps forgive those who said that the moons of Jupiter were produced by Galileo's spyglass, if we recall that in his day, as for centuries before, curved glass was the popular contrivance for producing not truth but illusion, untruth.
statements.chinese: 也许我们可以原谅那些说木星的卫星是伽利略的望远镜产生的说法，如果我们回想起，在他的时代，以及之前的几个世纪，弯曲的玻璃是一种流行的工具，它不是用来产生真相，而是产生幻觉，即虚假。
如果一块弯曲的玻璃会扭曲自然，那么两块又会扭曲多少呢？
statements.english: And if a single curved glass would distort nature, how much more would a pair of them?

statements.chinese: 迈克尔·霍斯金，《伽利略重生》，选自《听众》杂志。
statements.english: Michael Hoskin, Galileo Reborn from The Listener.

courses.title: Lesson 41: Training Elephants
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 25 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 第6单元, 第51篇课文。
statements.english: Unit 6, Passage 51.

statements.chinese: 训练大象主要有两种方法，我们可分别称之为“强硬法”和“温柔法”。
statements.english: Two main techniques have been used for training elephants, which we may call respectively the tough and the gentle.

statements.chinese: 前者只是让大象工作，并鞭打它，直到它按要求行事。
statements.english: The former method simply consists of setting an elephant to work and beating him until he does what is expected of him.
Apart from any moral considerations, this is a stupid method of training, for it produces a resentful animal who at a later stage may well turn mankiller.
statements.chinese: 抛开道德因素不谈，这是一种愚蠢的训练方法，因为它会培养出心怀怨恨的大象，日后很可能会变成杀人象。

statements.english: The gentle method requires more patience in the early stages, but produces a cheerful, good-tempered elephant who will give many years of loyal service.
statements.chinese: 温柔法在初期需要更多的耐心，但会培养出性情开朗、温顺的大象，它们会提供多年忠诚的服务。

statements.english: The first essential in elephant training is to assign to the animal a single mahout, who will be entirely responsible for the job.
statements.chinese: 训练大象的首要任务是给它指派一个专属象夫，象夫将全权负责这项工作。

statements.english: Elephants like to have one master just as dogs do, and are capable of a considerable degree of personal affection.
statements.chinese: 大象喜欢有一个主人，就像狗一样，而且它们能够表现出相当程度的个人情感。
甚至有这样的故事：半驯化的小象，因不可避免的情况被剥夺了专属驯象师后，拒绝进食并最终饿死。
statements.english: There are even stories of half-trained elephant calves who have refused to feed and pined to death when by some unavoidable circumstance they have been deprived of their own trainer.
Such extreme cases must probably be taken with a grain of salt, but they do underline the general principle that the relationship between elephant and mahout is the key to successful training.
statements.chinese: 这种极端的例子可能需要有所保留，但它们确实强调了一个普遍原则：大象与象夫之间的关系是成功训练的关键。

statements.english: The most economical age to capture an elephant for training is between 15 and 20 years, for it is then almost ready to undertake heavy work and can begin to earn its keep straight away.
statements.chinese: 捕捉大象进行训练最经济的年龄是15到20岁之间，因为那时它几乎可以立即开始繁重的工作，并开始自食其力。

statements.english: But animals of this age do not easily become subservient to man, and a very firm hand must be employed in the early stages.
statements.chinese: 但这个年龄段的动物不容易顺从人类，因此在早期阶段必须采取非常坚定的手段。

statements.english: The captive elephant, still roped to a tree, plunges and screams every time a man approaches, and for several days will probably refuse all food through anger and fear.
statements.chinese: 被捕获的大象，仍然被绳子拴在树上，每当有人靠近时，它就会猛冲并尖叫，并且在几天内，可能会因为愤怒和恐惧而拒绝所有食物。
有时，会将一头驯服的大象拴在附近，以给予野生大象信心。
statements.english: Sometimes a tame elephant is tethered nearby to give the wild one confidence.

statements.chinese: 在大多数情况下，被捕获的大象会逐渐平静下来，并开始接受食物。
statements.english: In most cases the captive gradually quietens down and begins to accept its food.
The next stage is to get the elephant to the training establishment, a ticklish business which is achieved with the aid of two tame elephants roped to the captive on either side.
statements.chinese: 下一个阶段是将大象带到训练场所，这是一项棘手的工作，需要借助两头驯服的大象，它们被分别拴在被捕获大象的两侧。

statements.english: When several elephants are being trained at one time, it's customary for the new arrival to be placed between the stalls of two captives whose training is already well advanced.
statements.chinese: 当同时训练几头大象时，通常会将新来的大象放在两头训练有素的被捕获大象的兽栏之间。

statements.english: It's then left completely undisturbed with plenty of food and water, so that it can absorb the atmosphere of its new home and see that nothing particularly alarming is happening to its companions.
statements.chinese: 之后它会被完全不被打扰地留下，并有充足的食物和水，这样它就能融入新家的氛围，并看到它的同伴没有发生什么特别令人警惕的事情。
当它正常进食时，它自己的训练就开始了。
statements.english: When it's eating normally, its own training begins.

statements.chinese: 驯象师站在大象面前，手持一根带有锋利金属尖头的长棍。
statements.english: The trainer stands in front of the elephant holding a long stick with a sharp metal point.
Two assistants mounted on tame elephants control the captive from either side, while others rub their hands over his skin to the accompaniment of monotonous and soothing chant.
statements.chinese: 两名骑着驯服大象的助手从两侧控制被捕获的大象，而其他人则抚摸它的皮肤，同时伴随着单调而舒缓的歌唱。

statements.english: This is supposed to induce pleasurable sensations in the elephant, and its effects are reinforced by the use of endearing epithets such as "Ho, my son" or "Ho, my father" or "my mother" according to the age and sex of the captive.
statements.chinese: 这被认为能在大象身上引发愉悦的感觉，它的效果通过使用“嗨，我的儿子”或“嗨，我的父亲”或“我的母亲”等亲昵称呼而得到加强，具体根据被捕获大象的年龄和性别而定。

statements.english: The elephant is not immediately susceptible to such blandishments, however, and usually lashes fiercely with its trunk in all directions.
statements.chinese: 然而，大象并不会立即受这些甜言蜜语的影响，通常会用鼻子猛烈地向四面八方甩动。
这些动作由驯象师用带有金属尖头的棍子控制。
statements.english: These movements are controlled by the trainer with the metal-pointed stick.

statements.chinese: 鼻子最终会变得非常疼痛，以至于大象会把它卷起来，之后也很少用它来进行攻击。
statements.english: And the trunk eventually becomes so sore that the elephant curls it up and seldom afterwards uses it for offensive purposes.

statements.chinese: 理查德·卡林顿，《大象》。
statements.english: Richard Carrington, Elephants.

courses.title: Lesson 42: Recording an Earthquake
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 42 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 地震就像夜间的盗贼，不打招呼就来了。
statements.english: An earthquake comes like a thief in the night without warning.

statements.chinese: 因此，有必要发明一种既不打盹也不睡觉的仪器。
statements.english: It was necessary therefore to invent instruments that neither slumbered nor slept.

statements.chinese: 有些装置相当简单。
statements.english: Some devices were quite simple.
One, for instance, consisted of rods of various lengths and thicknesses, which would stand up on end like ninepins.
statements.chinese: 例如，其中一种装置由不同长度和厚度的杆组成，它们像九柱戏的木柱一样直立。

statements.english: When a shock came, it shook the rigid table upon which these stood.
statements.chinese: 当震动来临时，它会震动这些杆子所立的坚硬桌子。
如果震动轻微，只有那些较不稳定的杆子会倒下。
statements.english: If it were gentle, only the more unstable rods fell.

statements.chinese: 如果震动剧烈，它们都会倒下。
statements.english: If it was severe, they all fell.
Thus the rods by falling, and by the direction in which they fell, recorded for the slumbering scientist the strength of a shock that was too weak to awaken him, and the direction from which it came.
statements.chinese: 因此，这些杆子通过倒下，以及它们倒下的方向，为昏睡中的科学家记录下了一种震动的强度，这种震动太弱以至于无法唤醒他，以及震动传来的方向。

statements.english: But instruments far more delicate than that were needed, if any really serious advance was to be made.
statements.chinese: 但如果想要取得任何真正重要的进展，就需要比这更精密的仪器。

statements.english: The ideal to be aimed at was to devise an instrument that could record with a pen on paper the movements of the ground or of the table as the quake passed by.
statements.chinese: 理想的目标是设计一种仪器，能够用笔在纸上记录下地面或桌子在地震发生时的运动。
当我书写时，我的笔在动，但纸是静止的。
statements.english: While I write, my pen moves, but the paper keeps still.

statements.chinese: 毫无疑问，经过练习，我总有一天可以学会，在纸移动的时候，我的笔保持不动来书写。
statements.english: With practice, no doubt, I could in time learn to write by holding the pen still while the paper moved.

statements.chinese: 这听起来是个愚蠢的建议。
statements.english: That sounds a silly suggestion.
But that was precisely the idea adopted in some of the early instruments, seismometers, for recording earthquake waves.
statements.chinese: 但这正是早期一些仪器——即地震仪——用于记录地震波所采用的理念。

statements.english: But when table, penholder and paper are all moving, how is it possible to write legibly?
statements.chinese: 但是，当桌子、笔架和纸都在移动时，又怎么可能清晰地书写呢？

statements.english: The key to a solution of that problem lay in an everyday observation.
statements.chinese: 解决这个问题的关键在于一个日常观察。

statements.english: Why does a person standing in a bus or train tend to fall when a sudden start is made?
statements.chinese: 为什么一个人站在公共汽车或火车上，当车辆突然启动时，会倾向于跌倒？
这是因为他的脚随着车辆移动，但头部却保持静止。
statements.english: It is because his feet move on, but his head stays still.

statements.chinese: 一个简单的实验会帮助我们进一步理解。
statements.english: A simple experiment will help us a little further.

statements.chinese: 将一个重物系在一根长绳的末端。
statements.english: Tie a heavy weight at the end of a long piece of string.
With the hand held high in the air, hold the string so that the weight nearly touches the ground.
statements.chinese: 将手举高在空中，握住绳子，使重物几乎接触地面。

statements.english: Now move the hand to and fro and round, but not up and down.
statements.chinese: 现在将手来回、环绕移动，但不要上下移动。
会发现重物只会轻微移动，甚至根本不动。
statements.english: It will be found that the weight moves but slightly or not at all.

statements.chinese: 想象一支笔以某种方式附着在重物上，笔尖落在地板上的一张纸上。
statements.english: Imagine a pen attached to the weight in such a way that its point rests upon a piece of paper on the floor.
Imagine an earthquake shock shaking the floor, the paper, you and your hand.
statements.chinese: 想象一次地震震动了地板、纸张、你和你的手。
在所有这些运动中，重物和笔将是静止的。
statements.english: In the midst of all this movement, the weight and the pen would be still.
But as the paper moved from side to side under the pen point, its movements would be recorded in ink upon its surface.
statements.chinese: 但当纸在笔尖下左右移动时，它的运动就会用墨水记录在纸的表面。

statements.english: It was upon this principle that the first instruments were made, but the paper was wrapped round a drum which rotated slowly.
statements.chinese: 最初的仪器就是基于这个原理制造的，但纸是缠绕在一个缓慢旋转的鼓上。
只要一切静止，笔就会画出一条直线。
statements.english: As long as all was still, the pen drew a straight line.
But while the drum was being shaken, the line that the pen was drawing wiggled from side to side.
statements.chinese: 但当鼓被震动时，笔所画的线就会左右摆动。

statements.english: The apparatus thus described, however, records only the horizontal component of the wave movement, which is, in fact, much more complicated.
statements.chinese: 然而，这样描述的仪器，只记录波浪运动的水平分量，而实际上，波浪运动要复杂得多。

statements.english: If we could actually see the path described by a particle, such as a sand grain in the rock, it would be more like that of a bluebottle buzzing around the room.
statements.chinese: 如果我们能实际看到一个粒子，例如岩石中的一个沙粒所描述的路径，它会更像一只苍蝇在房间里嗡嗡飞舞。
它会上下、来回、左右移动。
statements.english: It would be up and down, to and fro, and from side to side.
Instruments have been devised and can be so placed that all three elements can be recorded in different graphs.
statements.chinese: 已经设计出仪器，并且可以这样放置，使所有三个分量都能在不同的图表中记录下来。

statements.english: When the instrument is situated at more than 700 miles from the earthquake centre, the graphic record shows three waves arriving one after the other at short intervals.
statements.chinese: 当仪器位于距震中700英里以外时，图形记录显示三波地震波以短间隔相继到达。
第一波记录了纵向振动的到达。
statements.english: The first records the arrival of longitudinal vibrations.
The second marks the arrival of transverse vibrations, which travel more slowly and arrive several minutes after the first.
statements.chinese: 第二波标志着横向振动的到达，它们传播较慢，比第一波晚几分钟到达。
这两波都穿过了地球。
statements.english: These two have travelled through the earth.

statements.chinese: 正是通过对它们的深入研究，人们对地球内部有了很多了解。
statements.english: It was from the study of these that so much was learned about the interior of the earth.
The third, or main wave, is the slowest and has travelled round the earth through the surface rocks.
statements.chinese: 第三波，或称主波，是最慢的，并且是沿着地表岩石绕地球传播的。
H. H. 斯温纳顿。
statements.english: H. H. Swinnerton.

statements.chinese: 《我们脚下的地球》。
statements.english: The Earth Beneath Us.

courses.title: Lesson 43: Are There Strangers in Space
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 22 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 我们与太空中其他智慧生物交流的“唯一理性方式”取决于什么？
statements.english: What does the 'uniquely rational way' for us to communicate with other intelligent beings in space depend on?
We must conclude from the work of those who have studied the origin of life, that given a planet only approximately like our own, life is almost certain to start.
statements.chinese: 从研究生命起源的那些人的工作中，我们必须得出结论，只要有一颗与我们地球大致相似的行星，生命几乎肯定会开始。
在我们太阳系的所有行星中，我们现在非常确定地球是唯一一个生命可以存活的行星。
statements.english: Of all the planets in our solar system, we are now pretty certain the Earth is the only one on which life can survive.
Mars is too dry and poor in oxygen, Venus far too hot, and so is Mercury, and the outer planets have temperatures near absolute zero and hydrogen-dominated atmospheres.
statements.chinese: 火星太干燥，氧气稀少；金星和水星都太热，而外行星的温度接近绝对零度，大气层以氢为主。

statements.english: But other suns, start as the astronomers call them, are bound to have planets like our own, and as is the number of stars in the universe is so vast, this possibility becomes virtual certainty.
statements.chinese: 但是其他太阳，天文学家称之为恒星，必定有像我们地球一样的行星，而且宇宙中恒星的数量如此之多，这种可能性几乎成了必然。

statements.english: There are one hundred thousand million starts in our own Milky Way alone, and then there are three thousand million other milky ways or galaxies, in the universe.
statements.chinese: 仅在我们的银河系中就有1000亿颗恒星，而宇宙中还有30亿个其他星系。
因此，我们已知存在的恒星数量现在估计约为300万亿亿。
statements.english: so the number of stars that we know exist is now estimated at about 300 million million million.

Although perhaps only 1 percent of the life that has started somewhere will develop into highly complex and intelligent patterns, so vast is the number of planets, that intelligent life is bound to be a natural part of the universe.
statements.chinese: 尽管在某个地方开始的生命中，可能只有1%会发展成高度复杂和智能的模式，但行星的数量如此之多，以至于智慧生命必然是宇宙的自然组成部分。
既然我们如此确定宇宙中存在其他智慧生命，那为什么我们还没有迎来外太空的访客呢？
statements.english: If then we are so certain that other intelligent life exists in the universe, why have we had no visitors from outer space yet?
First of all, they may have come to this planet of ours thousands or millions of years ago, and found our then prevailing primitive state completely uninteresting to their own advanced knowledge.
statements.chinese: 首先，他们可能在几千或几百万年前就已经来到过我们的星球，并发现我们当时普遍存在的原始状态对于他们自身先进的知识来说完全不感兴趣。

statements.english: Professor Ronald Bracewell, a leading American radio astronomer, argued in Nature that such a superior civilization, on a visit to our own solar system, may have left an automatic messenger behind to await the possible awakening of an advanced civilization.
statements.chinese: 罗纳德·布雷斯韦尔教授，一位杰出的美国射电天文学家，在《自然》杂志上提出，这样一个更高级的文明，在访问我们太阳系时，可能会留下一个自动信使，以等待一个先进文明的可能觉醒。

statements.english: Such a messenger, receiving our radio and television signals, might well re-transmit them back to its home-planet, although what impression any other civilization would thus get from us is best left unsaid.
statements.chinese: 这样一个信使，在接收到我们的无线电和电视信号后，很可能会将它们重新发送回它的母星，尽管其他文明会因此从我们这里得到什么样的印象最好还是不提为妙。

statements.english: But here we come up against the most difficult of all obstacles to contact with people on other planets -- the astronomical distances which separate us.
statements.chinese: 但在这里，我们遇到了与外星球人接触所有障碍中最困难的一个——将我们分开的巨大天文距离。
合理猜测，他们平均可能在100光年之外。
statements.english: As a reasonable guess, they might, on an average, be 100 light years away.

statements.chinese: (一光年是光以每秒18.6万英里的速度在一年中旅行的距离，即6万亿英里。)
statements.english: (A light year is the distance which light travels at 186, 000 miles per second in one year, namely 6 million million miles.)
Radio waves also travel at the speed of light, and assuming such an automatic messenger picked up our first broadcasts of the 1920's, the message to its home planet is barely halfway there.
statements.chinese: 无线电波也以光速传播，假设这样一个自动信使接收到了我们20世纪20年代的首次广播，那么它传回家园星球的信息才刚刚走了一半的路程。

statements.english: Similarly, our own present primitive chemical rockets, though good enough to orbit men, have no chance of transporting us to the nearest other star, four light years away, let alone distances of tens or hundreds of light years.
statements.chinese: 同样地，我们目前原始的化学火箭，尽管足以将人类送入轨道，却没有机会将我们运送到最近的恒星，距我们四光年之遥，更不用说几十或几百光年的距离了。

statements.english: Fortunately, there is a 'uniquely rational way' for us to communicate with other intelligent beings, as Walter Sullivan has put it in his excellent book, We Are not Alone.
statements.chinese: 幸运的是，我们有一种“唯一理性方式”可以与其他智慧生物交流，正如沃尔特·沙利文在他的优秀著作中所说，《我们并不孤单》。
这取决于21厘米波长，即每秒1420兆赫兹的精确无线电频率。
statements.english: This depends on the precise radio frequency of the 21-cm wavelength, or 1420 megacycles per second.
It is the natural frequency of emission of the hydrogen atoms in space and was discovered by us in 1951; it must be known to any kind of radio astronomer in the universe.
statements.chinese: 它是太空中氢原子的自然发射频率，由我们于1951年发现；宇宙中任何一种射电天文学家都必定知道它。

statements.english: Once the existence of this wave-length had been discovered, it was not long before its use as the uniquely recognizable broadcasting frequency for interstellar communication was suggested.
statements.chinese: 一旦这种波长被发现，很快就有人建议将其用作星际通信的独特可识别广播频率。

statements.english: Without something of this kind, searching for intelligences on other planets would be like trying to meet a friend in London without a pre-arranged rendezvous and absurdly wandering the streets in the hope of a chance encounter.
statements.chinese: 如果没有这种东西，寻找其他行星上的智慧生命，就像在伦敦没有事先约定地点就试图与朋友见面一样，荒唐地在街上闲逛，希望能偶然相遇。

courses.title: Lesson 44: Patterns of Culture
courses.description: 新概念英语第四册 · 26 条逐句练习

statements.chinese: 从我们出生那一刻起，什么在影响着我们？
statements.english: What influences us from the moment of birth?

statements.chinese: 习俗通常不被认为是一个举足轻重的问题。
statements.english: Custom has not commonly been regarded as a subject of any great moment.
The inner workings of our own brains we feel to be uniquely worthy of investigation, but custom, we have a way of thinking, is behaviour at is most commonplace.
statements.chinese: 我们认为我们自己大脑的内部运作是独一无二地值得研究的，但我们有一种想法，认为习俗是最常见的行为。
事实上，情况恰恰相反。
statements.english: As a matter of fact, it is the other way around.
Traditional custom, taken the world over, is a mass of detailed behaviour more astonishing than what any one person can ever evolve in individual actions, no matter how aberrant.
statements.chinese: 传统的习俗，遍布世界各地，是一堆详细的行为，比任何个人在单独行动中所能演变出的行为都更令人惊讶，无论多么反常。
然而，这只是问题的微不足道的一面。
statements.english: Yet that is a rather trivial aspect of the matter.
The fact of first-rate importance is the predominant role that custom plays in experience and in belief, and the very great varieties it may manifest.
statements.chinese: 最重要的事实是习俗在经验和信仰中扮演的主导角色，以及它可能表现出的巨大多样性。
没有人能以纯粹的眼光看待世界。
statements.english: No man ever looks at the world with pristine eyes.

statements.chinese: 他看到的世界是由一套明确的习俗、制度和思维方式所塑造的。
statements.english: He sees it edited by a definite set of customs and institutions and ways of thinking.
Even in his philosophical probings he cannot go behind these stereotypes; his very concepts of the true and the false will still have reference to his particular traditional customs.
statements.chinese: 即使在他的哲学探索中，他也无法超越这些刻板印象；他对真与假的观念仍然会与他特定的传统习俗相关联。

statements.english: John Dewey has said in all seriousness that the part played by custom in shaping the behaviour of the individual, as against any way in which he can affect traditional custom, is as the proportion of the total vocabulary of his mother tongue against those words of his own baby talk that are taken up into the vernacular of his family.
statements.chinese: 约翰·杜威曾非常严肃地说，习俗在塑造个人行为中所起的作用，与他能够影响传统习俗的任何方式相比，就像他母语的全部词汇量，与他自己咿呀学语中被家庭口语采纳的词语之比。

statements.english: When one seriously studies the social orders that have had the opportunity to develop autonomously, the figure becomes no more than an exact and matter-of-fact observation.
statements.chinese: 当人们认真研究那些有机会自主发展的社会秩序时，这个比喻就成了精确而实际的观察。

statements.english: The life history of the individual is first and foremost an accommodation to the patterns and standards traditionally handed down in his community.
statements.chinese: 个体的生命历程首先是一种适应，适应其社区中世代相传的模式和标准。

statements.english: From the moment of his birth, the customs into which he is born shape his experience and behaviour.
statements.chinese: 从他出生那一刻起，他所降生的习俗塑造了他的经验和行为。

statements.english: By the time he can talk, he is the little creature of his culture, and by the time he is grown and able to take part in its activities, its habits are his habits, its beliefs his beliefs, its impossibilities his impossibilities.
statements.chinese: 等到他会说话时，他已是其文化的小小产物，等到他长大成人并能参与其活动时，它的习惯是他的习惯，它的信仰是他的信仰，它的不可能之事是他的不可能之事。

statements.english: Every child that is born into his group will share them with him, and no child born into one on the opposite side of the globe can ever achieve the thousandth part.
statements.chinese: 每一个出生在他群体中的孩子都会与他分享这些，而出生在地球另一边的孩子连千分之一也无法做到。
没有比理解习俗的作用更重要的社会问题了。
statements.english: There is no social problem it is more incumbent upon us to understand than this of the role of custom.
Until we are intelligent as to its laws and varieties, the main complicating facts of human life must remain unintelligible.
statements.chinese: 在我们对其规律和多样性有充分了解之前，人类生活的主要复杂事实必然是难以理解的。

statements.english: The study of custom can be profitable only after certain preliminary propositions have been accepted, and some of these propositions have been violently opposed.
statements.chinese: 对习俗的研究只有在某些初步命题被接受之后才能有所裨益，而其中一些命题曾遭到强烈反对。

statements.english: In the first place, any scientific study requires that there be no preferential weighting of one or another of the items in the series it selects for its consideration.
statements.chinese: 首先，任何科学研究都要求，在它所选择的系列项目进行考量时，不应对其中任何一项有偏向性地加权。

statements.english: In all the less controversial fields, like the study of cacti or termites or the nature of nebulae, the necessary method of study is to group the relevant material and to take note of all possible variant forms and conditions.
statements.chinese: 在所有争议较少的领域，比如研究仙人掌、白蚁或星云的性质，必要的研究方法是将相关材料分组，并记录所有可能的变体形式和条件。
通过这种方式，我们掌握了天文学的所有规律，或者说，掌握了群居昆虫的习性。
statements.english: In this way, we have learned all that we know of the laws of astronomy, or of the habits of the social insects, let us say.
